It is imperative that academic curricula formally integrate competencies in bioethics, palliative care and emotional management to prepare graduates for extreme vulnerability and prevent early professional burnout.

resumo.texto: The evolution of Physiotherapy requires a shift from the biomedical model towards bioethical and humanistic approaches. This study explores how final-year students perceive their professional role when dealing with patients with complex neurodegenerative conditions, where traditional technical success is challenged by the irreversibility of the deterioration.

Qualitative research based on interpretative description. Thirty final-year students from the University of Almería (Spain) took part, divided into five working groups. Three training sessions and discussions were held on Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), Alzheimer's disease, stroke and Rett syndrome. The data were analysed using thematic analysis and triangulation by researchers external to the study, with reflexivity ensured through logbooks.

A shift in clinical reasoning was identified, with sensitivity taking precedence over technique. Students redefined therapeutic success in terms of "comfort" and support, valuing "microscopic achievements" such as the preservation of dignity and the alleviation of distress. Of particular note is the ability to adapt ethical principles according to the patient's cognitive integrity (autonomy in ALS versus protection in Alzheimer's) and the integration of the carer as an inseparable part of the therapeutic process.

Future physiotherapists perceive humanization and the empathetic interpretation of non-verbal cues as essential therapeutic tools. Unlike previous studies focused on clinical experience, this research explores pre-clinical ethical maturation, offering a unique perspective on the educational foundation and humanistic predisposition of future graduates prior to their immersion in the healthcare system. It is imperative that academic curricula formally integrate competencies in bioethics, palliative care and emotional management to prepare graduates for extreme vulnerability and prevent early professional burnout.

artigos.titulo: Large language model responses about PMOS : information quality, readability, transparency and perceived empathy
artigos.autores: Chen Y, Xiong YJ, Yu P et al.
artigos.destaque: Ratings differed for the specific configurations and single responses examined in this treatment-heavy question set. The findings neither establish stable model rankings nor demonstrate clinical correctness, safety or effectiveness for patients.

resumo.texto: Freely accessible large language models provide health information, but their communication characteristics require evaluation. We compared information quality, transparency, readability and perceived empathy for questions about polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS; formerly PCOS).

Thirty-three clinician-formulated English questions using PCOS terminology were submitted once to each of three free-access configurations during 20-25 July 2026. Two clinicians rated DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA benchmarks, global quality and perceived empathy. Six readability indices were calculated. Matched comparisons used Friedman tests, paired signed-rank permutation comparisons and Holm correction.

Across 99 archived responses, the DeepSeek-V4 configuration received higher final ratings than GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.5 on all five clinician-rated measures (Holm-adjusted pairwise P < 0.05). Median DISCERN scores were 67.0, 62.0 and 61.0, respectively. DeepSeek-V4 had higher median ARI, GFI, FKGL and SMOG values, whereas GPT-5.5 had the highest median Coleman-Liau score. FRES showed no overall difference (adjusted P = 0.100). Initial empathy agreement was low (ICC 0.05-0.43).

Ratings differed for the specific configurations and single responses examined in this treatment-heavy question set. The findings neither establish stable model rankings nor demonstrate clinical correctness, safety or effectiveness for patients.

artigos.titulo: Relation Between the Prevalence of Hearing Loss, Auditory Processing Disorder, and Cognitive Decline in Older Adults: A Retrospective Study
artigos.autores: Ghosh V, Yathiraj A
artigos.destaque: The study demonstrates that hearing loss, APD symptoms, and cognitive decline frequently coexist but are not strongly associated. This emphasizes that all 3 screening procedures should be performed in older adults for timely detection and management.

resumo.texto: Older adults are known to experience communication difficulties due to hearing loss, auditory processing disorder (APD), and cognitive decline. These conditions have been found to independently or in pairs affect communication, social participation, and quality of life. However, there are limited reports on the relationship of these 3 conditions among older adults. Thus, the study aimed to determine the association between hearing loss, APD, and cognitive decline in older adults and examine the influence of age and gender.
Using the records of 1100 older adults aged 50-95 years who visited a tertiary care geriatric clinic, the data of pure-tone hearing screening, risk for APD, and cognition were analyzed.

The number of participants referred was the highest for hearing screening (59.3%), followed by cognitive decline (55.6%), and APD (24.8%). Only 18.5% passed all 3 screening procedures, while 81.5% were referred on at least 1 screening procedure. In general, males were referred more frequently than females, with the referral rate being higher with advancement in age. Significant differences were found between APD and the other 2 screening procedures but not between hearing and cognition. The associations among the 3 screening procedures were weak to moderate, suggesting their independence.

The study demonstrates that hearing loss, APD symptoms, and cognitive decline frequently coexist but are not strongly associated. This emphasizes that all 3 screening procedures should be performed in older adults for timely detection and management.

artigos.titulo: Prospective associations between diet quality, frailty and incident cognitive impairment in the health and retirement study
artigos.autores: Beydoun MA, Wei C, Weiss J et al.
artigos.destaque: Higher diet quality was associated with lower physical frailty but not independently with incident cognitive impairment. Food-specific associations were heterogeneous and largely did not survive multiple-testing correction. Findings warrant replication before drawing dietary recommendations for cognitive health.

resumo.texto: Diet quality is a modifiable determinant of healthy aging, potentially influencing physical and cognitive functioning through inflammatory and metabolic pathways. Although healthier dietary patterns have been linked to reduced frailty and cognitive decline, findings remain inconsistent. The interrelationships among diet quality, physical frailty, and incident cognitive impairment, including potential modification by specific dietary components, remain poorly understood.

We analyzed 1,636 cognitively normal participants in 2016 from the Health and Retirement Study, a longitudinal study of adults in the United States (U.S.), with diet assessed in 2013, frailty in 2016, and cognitive follow-up through 2022. Cognitive impairment was assessed with cognitive tests and used the Langa-Weir classification; diet quality was measured using the Healthy Eating Index-2015 (HEI-2015); and physical frailty used a modified Fried phenotype. Survey-weighted regression, Cox models, four-way decomposition, competing-risk and multistate models, and additive Bayesian network (ABN)-informed generalized structural equation models (GSEM) were applied.

Higher HEI-2015 scores were associated with lower frailty (β = -0.13, P < 0.001), but not with incident cognitive impairment. Frailty was associated with higher cognitive risk in minimally adjusted models (Hazard Ratio (HR) = 2.27, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.56-3.32), with attenuation after full adjustment. Exploratory analyses identified 13 nominally significant food-item associations with composite cognitive impairment, including higher risks associated with selected dairy products, processed meats, and beverages, and an inverse association with red wine (HR = 0.77, 95% CI: 0.66-0.89). None survived FDR correction. Five dietary associations with probable dementia alone survived FDR correction but remained exploratory. Four-way decomposition provided limited evidence of dietary mediation or interaction, while sensitivity analyses supported attenuation of frailty-cognition associations.

Higher diet quality was associated with lower physical frailty but not independently with incident cognitive impairment. Food-specific associations were heterogeneous and largely did not survive multiple-testing correction. Findings warrant replication before drawing dietary recommendations for cognitive health.

artigos.titulo: EXPRESS: Brain Age Gap from Non-Contrast CT Is Independently Associated with Functional Outcome after Acute Ischemic Stroke
artigos.autores: Mahajna M, Charatpangoon P, Martin Ondrus M et al.
artigos.destaque: These findings support CT-based BrainAGE as a marker of brain health complementary to established prognostic factors. Whether BrainAGE improves patient-level risk stratification or clinical decision-making requires independent external validation and prospective evaluation.

resumo.texto: BackgroundOutcomes after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) vary beyond lesion burden and clinical severity, suggesting a role for baseline structural brain vulnerability. We evaluated whether brain age gap (BrainAGE) derived from routine non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) is associated with functional outcome after AIS.MethodsWe analyzed 1,173 AIS patients from a prospective multicenter cohort. A deep learning model estimated brain age from contralesional baseline NCCT to minimize lesion-related confounding. BrainAGE was defined as predicted minus chronological age. The primary outcome was 90-day functional status, assessed using proportional odds regression adjusted for age, sex, baseline stroke severity, early ischemic changes, and reperfusion therapy.ResultsBrainAGE was higher in AIS patients than in controls (+3.1 ± 9.1 years; p<0.001). Higher BrainAGE was associated with worse functional outcome after adjustment for age, sex, and other clinical predictors (POR 1.091 per 5 years; 95% CI 1.023-1.162; p=0.008). BrainAGE improved model fit but modestly improved discrimination.ConclusionsBrainAGE from routine NCCT provided modest incremental prognostic information beyond age and conventional clinical predictors. These findings support CT-based BrainAGE as a marker of brain health complementary to established prognostic factors. Whether BrainAGE improves patient-level risk stratification or clinical decision-making requires independent external validation and prospective evaluation.

artigos.titulo: Pharmacological chaperone treatment with Cystadane in aspartylglucosaminuria: an open-label, phase Ib/II trial
artigos.autores: Laine M, Banning A, Sairanen V et al.
artigos.destaque: Further studies should be carried out in a larger patient population over a longer time to demonstrate the effects on disease progression. EudraCT registration number 2017-000645-48.

resumo.texto: This phase Ib/II investigator-initiated, open label trial aims to show the safety and efficacy of Cystadane (betaine) in aspartylglucosaminuria, a lysosomal storage disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline, in Finnish patients homozygous for the Finnish major mutation, aged between 3 and 17 years at study begin (recruited: 25, analyzed: 21). Oral Cystadane efficacy and safety were studied over 48 months. The primary endpoint of the study, reduction of glycoasparagines in the urine, was quantitatively determined using liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry and normalized to urine creatinine. Urine glycoasparagines are significantly reduced upon Cystadane treatment (by 68.6% ±10.8%; p = 0.000), and the study thus meets its primary endpoint. Our data show that Cystadane/betaine efficiently improves the main disease biomarker, and it is safe to use in aspartylglucosaminuria. Further studies should be carried out in a larger patient population over a longer time to demonstrate the effects on disease progression. EudraCT registration number 2017-000645-48.

artigos.titulo: IGF binding proteins: emerging endocrine mediators of cancer-associated muscle wasting
artigos.autores: Dall'Olio F, Shalimanova E, Vassetzky Y
artigos.destaque: Furthermore, aging may contribute to susceptibility to cancer-associated muscle loss through alterations in the insulin-like growth factor (IGF)/insulin-like growth factor binding protein (IGFBP) axis and decreased muscle's anabolic and regenerative capacity. Recent mechanistic studies have identified the IGF/IGFBP axis as a promising source of biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets in cancer-associated muscle wasting.

resumo.texto: Cancer-associated sarcopenia is a key determinant of treatment toxicity and mortality. Recent data indicate that insulin-like growth factor binding protein 1 and insulin-like growth factor binding protein 2 may be endocrine mediators connecting tumor-derived signals, hepatic reprogramming, and defective muscle regeneration. Furthermore, aging may contribute to susceptibility to cancer-associated muscle loss through alterations in the insulin-like growth factor (IGF)/insulin-like growth factor binding protein (IGFBP) axis and decreased muscle's anabolic and regenerative capacity. Recent mechanistic studies have identified the IGF/IGFBP axis as a promising source of biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets in cancer-associated muscle wasting.

artigos.titulo: Reframing the gut-muscle axis through the lens of functional redundancy: A conceptual framework for chronic sarcopenia, acute muscle wasting, and microbiota-related interventions
artigos.autores: Li SY, Ma YF, Tian S et al.
artigos.destaque: Microbiota-related interventions are candidate adjuncts to nutrition and exercise. Purified metabolites are distinguished from postbiotics, and direct clinical efficacy in acute critical-illness sarcopenia remains unestablished.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia is a progressive systemic skeletal muscle disorder that predominantly affects older adults, and its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Research on sarcopenia has largely followed two lines of inquiry. The first concerns chronic, age-associated sarcopenia, which involves anabolic resistance, chronic low-grade inflammation, neuromuscular junction degeneration, and hormonal alterations. The second concerns acute sarcopenia and related rapid muscle wasting during severe illness (e.g. sepsis, trauma, major surgery), which must be distinguished from ICU-acquired weakness and cancer cachexia. The gut-muscle axis has attracted interest as a potential contributor to sarcopenia onset and progression. This narrative review integrates heterogeneous cell, animal, observational human, and intervention evidence through four proposed functional modules: anabolic support, anti-catabolic protection, redox/mitochondrial homeostasis, and inflammatory-immune regulation. From the perspective of functional redundancy, we discuss a hypothetical "sarcopenia-susceptible state" and stage-informed research questions; these are conceptual constructs rather than validated disease stages or treatment algorithms. Microbiota-related interventions are candidate adjuncts to nutrition and exercise. Purified metabolites are distinguished from postbiotics, and direct clinical efficacy in acute critical-illness sarcopenia remains unestablished.

artigos.titulo: α-Actinin-3 deficiency protects skeletal muscle function from the effects of acute cold exposure
artigos.autores: Houweling PJ, Tiong CF, Kiriaev L et al.
artigos.destaque: This work emphasizes the important role that skeletal muscle plays in mammalian thermogenesis. Deficiency of the fast-muscle fibre protein α-actinin-3 protects skeletal muscle mass and function following acute cold exposure - providing a potential explanation for the increased frequency of the ACTN3 577X allele during the evolution of modern-day humans.

resumo.texto: Homozygosity for a nonsense polymorphism in the ACTN3 gene (rs1815739; ACTN3 577X) results in the loss of the fast-twitch skeletal muscle protein α-actinin-3 in an estimated 1.5 billion humans worldwide. α-Actinin-3 deficiency does not cause disease but is detrimental to elite sprint/power performance through a metabolic and physiological "slowing" of fast twitch muscle fibers. We have previously shown that α-actinin-3 deficiency is also associated with improved cold tolerance in humans following acute cold-water immersion.

Using published archaic and modern human DNA data we assessed the frequency of the ACTN3 577X allele. To further understand the mechanisms behind improved cold tolerance we examined the molecular and physiological impacts of acute cold exposure using the Actn3 knockout mouse model.

Here we inferred that ACTN3 577X arose ∼135,000 years ago and increased in frequency in European and Asian populations around 42,000 years ago, a period that aligns with modern human migration into cooler climates. Haplotype analyses around the ACTN3 R577X locus confirmed distinct inheritance patterns in different ethnic groups. Following acute cold exposure (4° C for 5 h), Actn3 knockout mice show lower muscle mass loss and improved fatigue resistance compared to wildtype. Actn3 knockout mouse muscles also exhibit higher levels of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, with reduced activation of metabolic and protein breakdown pathways following cold exposure.

This work emphasizes the important role that skeletal muscle plays in mammalian thermogenesis. Deficiency of the fast-muscle fibre protein α-actinin-3 protects skeletal muscle mass and function following acute cold exposure - providing a potential explanation for the increased frequency of the ACTN3 577X allele during the evolution of modern-day humans.

artigos.titulo: NutriA-Senior, a Mobile App to Enhance Nutritional Awareness in Older Adults: Design and Pilot Usability Study
artigos.autores: Bosoni P, Vincenti A, Bolpagni F et al.
artigos.destaque: This pilot usability study shows encouraging results, suggesting that NutriA-S is a highly usable, intuitive, and credible digital health tool for older adults. The identified limitations in items like customizability, willingness to pay, and willingness to use the app frequently, which received lower scores, will guide app refinements before deploying NutriA-S in an upcoming randomized controlled trial for older adults with sarcopenia or probable sarcopenia.

resumo.texto: Mobile health is emerging as a ubiquitous paradigm for delivering health care interventions when self-management is feasible. However, interventions targeting older or frail participants should account for age-related cognitive, visual, and physical needs to optimize usability and long-term retention.

This paper describes the rationale, design, and implementation of Nutritional App-Senior (NutriA-S), a theory-informed mobile app developed to enhance nutritional education in older adults with sarcopenia or probable sarcopenia. Moreover, we present the results of a usability study conducted in a cohort of age-matched healthy volunteers.

NutriA-S was designed as a self-instructional app built on the Moodle e-learning platform. It includes 24 progression modules containing interactive quizzes and associated informational items aimed at engaging users by sustaining attention and improving nutritional knowledge. A 4-week pilot usability study was conducted with 35 healthy volunteers aged 65 to 85 years, recruited through flyers posted in 2 outpatient settings. After recruitment, participants used the app remotely at home with telemedicine-based monitoring and support. At the end of the study, usability was quantitatively assessed using the Italian version of the standard System Usability Scale (SUS) and the User Version of the Mobile Application Rating Scale (uMARS).

The SUS questionnaire yielded a median total score of 80 out of 100 (IQR 55.00-92.50), indicating good perceived usability, with more than half of the participants rating the app as acceptable (above the threshold of 68). The overall median uMARS score was 4.083 (IQR 3.68-4.30), with the functionality and information domains achieving the highest median scores of 4.5 (with IQRs of 4.00-4.50 and 4.13-4.75, respectively), confirming that older adults perceived the tool as technically reliable and highly credible.

This pilot usability study shows encouraging results, suggesting that NutriA-S is a highly usable, intuitive, and credible digital health tool for older adults. The identified limitations in items like customizability, willingness to pay, and willingness to use the app frequently, which received lower scores, will guide app refinements before deploying NutriA-S in an upcoming randomized controlled trial for older adults with sarcopenia or probable sarcopenia.

artigos.titulo: Causal effects of connective tissue diseases on sarcopenia-related traits and the mediating role of immune cell phenotypes: a mediation Mendelian randomization study
artigos.autores: Kang H, Wang Q, Zhou Y et al.
artigos.destaque: This mediation MR study provides genetic evidence that DM, MCTD, PM and RA are causally associated with specific sarcopenia-related traits. The partial mediation of RA's effects through HLA-DR up-regulation on CD14⁻CD16⁻ cells suggests a potential immune pathway linking RA to muscle loss, though these findings require confirmation in independent cohorts. Key Points • The first mediation MR study to quantifies the mediating role of a specific immune cell phenotype in the causal pathway from CTDs to sarcopenia-related traits. • DM, MCTD, PM, and RA were causally associated with sarcopenia-related traits, with PM and RA showing the most consistent detrimental effects. • HLA-DR expression on CD14-CD16- cells may partially mediate the effect 3 of RA on appendicular lean mass and whole body fat free mass.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia is increasingly recognized as a common comorbidity of connective tissue diseases (CTDs). However, the causal relationships between CTDs and sarcopenia-related traits, and whether immune cells mediate these effects, remain unclear.

We performed a three-step Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis using genome-wide association study summary data of European ancestry. Step 1 evaluated the causal effects of seven CTDs on five sarcopenia-related traits. Step 2 screened 731 immune cell phenotypes for associations with these traits. Step 3 assessed the causal effects of the selected CTDs on the selected immune cell phenotypes. For each exposure-mediator-outcome triplet, the indirect effect and the mediation proportion were estimated using a two-step MR approach.

Dermatomyositis (DM), mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), polymyositis (PM), and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) were causally associated with at least one sarcopenia-related trait. Among 731 immune traits, 15 were significantly associated with at least three traits after FDR correction. In patients with RA, mediation analysis indicated that HLA-DR expression on CD14-CD16- cells partially mediated the effect on appendicular lean mass (mediation proportion = 9.76%, P = 0.040, q = 0.099) and whole-body-fat-free mass (mediation proportion = 5.76%, P = 0.039, q = 0.099), though these mediation findings did not survive FDR correction and should therefore be considered exploratory.

This mediation MR study provides genetic evidence that DM, MCTD, PM and RA are causally associated with specific sarcopenia-related traits. The partial mediation of RA's effects through HLA-DR up-regulation on CD14⁻CD16⁻ cells suggests a potential immune pathway linking RA to muscle loss, though these findings require confirmation in independent cohorts. Key Points • The first mediation MR study to quantifies the mediating role of a specific immune cell phenotype in the causal pathway from CTDs to sarcopenia-related traits. • DM, MCTD, PM, and RA were causally associated with sarcopenia-related traits, with PM and RA showing the most consistent detrimental effects. • HLA-DR expression on CD14-CD16- cells may partially mediate the effect 3 of RA on appendicular lean mass and whole body fat free mass.

artigos.titulo: Chronic cholestatic liver disease impairs skeletal muscle regeneration: partial modulation by ursodeoxycholic acid of satellite cells and innate immunity
artigos.autores: Cifuentes-Silva E, Tacchi F, Portal-Rodríguez M et al.
artigos.destaque: UDCA at 15 mg/kg/day altered selected myogenic and immune marker-defined readouts and MyHC-IIB abundance but did not improve histological indices of post-cryoinjury repair at day 12. A single endpoint cannot distinguish delayed progression, differences in initial injury burden, or persistently incomplete regeneration. These data do not support a clinical recommendation of UDCA for muscle repair.

resumo.texto: Chronic cholestatic liver disease (CCLD) is associated with skeletal muscle dysfunction, but its effects on muscle regeneration and the response to ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) remain incompletely characterized.

Male C57BL/6 mice received standard chow or a 0.1% 3,5-diethoxycarbonyl-1,4-dihydrocollidine (DDC) diet, with vehicle or UDCA (15 mg/kg/day); tibialis anterior cryoinjury at week 6 was followed by a 12-day recovery (n = 3-6 per group, depending on the assay). We assessed histology, fiber morphometry, embryonic myosin heavy chain (MyHC-emb) staining, flow cytometry, and adult MyHC isoforms. CCLD + UDCA exhibited more histologically altered tissue, more centrally nucleated fibers (both p < 0.0001), and more MyHC-emb⁺ fibers (p = 0.0002) than CCLD at day 12. The Pax7⁺ fraction was greater in CCLD than in controls (18.55% vs. 4.67%; adjusted p = 0.0001) and lower in CCLD + UDCA than in CCLD (4.63%; p = 0.0001), without a change in Myf5/MyoD composition within Pax7⁺ cells. CCLD + UDCA did not differ significantly from CCLD for MHC-II⁺, M1-like, or M2-like macrophage-associated frequencies, whereas the CD11b⁺Ly6G⁺ fraction was higher (p = 0.0043). MyHC-IIB abundance was greater in CCLD + UDCA than in CCLD (p = 0.0436).

UDCA at 15 mg/kg/day altered selected myogenic and immune marker-defined readouts and MyHC-IIB abundance but did not improve histological indices of post-cryoinjury repair at day 12. A single endpoint cannot distinguish delayed progression, differences in initial injury burden, or persistently incomplete regeneration. These data do not support a clinical recommendation of UDCA for muscle repair.

artigos.titulo: Small bites for big risks: efficacy of the small-bites closure technique in a real-world laparotomy cohort
artigos.autores: Açar S, Karaevli Ç, Aydın C et al.
artigos.destaque: The small-bites technique is a safe and comparably effective closure method for real-world cohorts. It maintains fascial integrity in high-risk patients and significantly reduces incisional hernia risk in non-malignant cases.

resumo.texto: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of the continuous small-bites fascial closure technique compared to standard large-bites closure in an unselected, consecutive series of high-risk patients undergoing midline laparotomy. The primary objective was to investigate whether the small-bites approach remains effective and safe in a real-world surgical population burdened with systemic comorbidities.

A retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained clinical database was conducted on 101 patients assigned via an institutional protocol (53 small-bites, 48 large-bites). The primary outcome was the one-year incidence of incisional hernia (IH). Secondary outcomes included surgical site infections and operative metrics. Multivariable binary logistic regression was utilized to adjust for baseline confounding factors, specifically variations in abdominal muscle quality as measured by the L3 cross-sectional mass ratio.

At the one-year follow-up, overall IH occurred in 7.5% of the small-bites group versus 12.5% of the large-bites group (p = 0.405). The small-bites approach required significantly longer fascial closure times (p = 0.016) but resulted in non-significant reductions in surgical site infections (30.2% vs. 39.6%, p = 0.322) and early evisceration (5.4% vs. 15.8%, p = 0.072). Additionally, baseline L3 cross-sectional mass ratio did not independently predict herniation (p = 0.142). Subgroup analyses revealed no significant differences in IH rates between the closure techniques in high-risk patients presenting with underlying malignancy (p = 0.632), sarcopenia (p = 0.689), or stomas (p = 1.000). However, in patients without malignancy, the small-bites technique yielded a significantly lower incidence of IH compared to the standard approach (p = 0.022). Adjusted multivariable regression indicated a non-significant decreased risk of IH development with small-bites (p = 0.360).

The small-bites technique is a safe and comparably effective closure method for real-world cohorts. It maintains fascial integrity in high-risk patients and significantly reduces incisional hernia risk in non-malignant cases.

artigos.titulo: A pilot study on the impact of Hydroxiram D supplementation on nutritional status and sarcopenia-related parameters
artigos.autores: Gallo P, Flagiello V, Di Cola S et al.
artigos.destaque: Six months of Hydroxiram D was associated with a more favorable change in PA in patients with compensated MASLD-related cirrhosis, with favorable trends in muscle parameters. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant confirmation in larger, prospectively registered, double-blind trials to confirm efficacy and long-term outcomes.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia is a frequent and prognostically relevant complication of chronic liver disease. The SARCIRAM pilot trial investigated the effect of Hydroxiram D, a formulation of branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB), and vitamin D, on nutritional status and sarcopenia-related parameters in patients with compensated cirrhosis due to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). In this single-center, randomized pilot study, adults with compensated MASLD-related cirrhosis (Child-Pugh A) received Hydroxiram D plus standard care or standard care alone for 6 months. The primary outcome was phase angle (PA), while secondary outcomes were appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASMM)/height², handgrip strength (HGS), and 4-meter walk test (4-mWT). Between-group comparisons used baseline-adjusted models. Post-hoc simulation analyses were used exploratorily to inform the design of future studies. Thirty-two patients were analyzed. After 6 months, the adjusted change in PA was significantly more favorable in the treated group versus controls (+ 0.36° vs. - 0.45°, p = 0.046). Between-group differences in muscle mass, HGS, and gait speed were not statistically significant, although effect estimates directionally favoured the intervention. No treatment-related adverse events were observed. Six months of Hydroxiram D was associated with a more favorable change in PA in patients with compensated MASLD-related cirrhosis, with favorable trends in muscle parameters. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant confirmation in larger, prospectively registered, double-blind trials to confirm efficacy and long-term outcomes.

artigos.titulo: Reactivating young muscle regenerative pathways in ageing through inhibition of the 'gerozyme' 15-hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase
artigos.revista: Philos Trans R Soc Lond B Biol Sci
artigos.autores: Nalbandian M, Blau HM
artigos.destaque: Pharmacological inhibition of 15-PGDH restores PGE2 signalling and improves muscle mass, strength and regenerative capacity in old mice and constitutes a promising therapeutic strategy to counter sarcopenia and promote late-life muscle function. This article is part of the theme issue 'Developmental circuits in ageing'.

resumo.texto: We are living longer, but the years lived free from chronic diseases and disabilities have not increased at the same rate. The loss of skeletal muscle function in late life constitutes a major barrier to achieving this goal. With age, muscle mass and strength progressively decline. When the loss of muscle function becomes pathological, it is clinically recognized as a syndrome, sarcopenia. The goal of our laboratory is to understand the cellular and molecular mechanisms that drive muscle ageing and sarcopenia and to identify therapeutic strategies that preserve or restore muscle function in older individuals. In this review, we discuss our discovery of the gerozyme 15-hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase (15-PGDH), a molecular driver of ageing that impedes muscle tissue growth, maintenance and regeneration. 15-PGDH abundance and enzymatic activity increase with age, leading to degradation of prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), a lipid mediator with key roles in skeletal muscle regeneration and tissue homeostasis. By limiting PGE2 bioavailability, elevated 15-PGDH contributes to the impaired regenerative and adaptive capacity of aged muscle. Pharmacological inhibition of 15-PGDH restores PGE2 signalling and improves muscle mass, strength and regenerative capacity in old mice and constitutes a promising therapeutic strategy to counter sarcopenia and promote late-life muscle function. This article is part of the theme issue 'Developmental circuits in ageing'.

artigos.titulo: Developmental epigenetic circuits and their epigenetic drift in skeletal muscle ageing
artigos.revista: Philos Trans R Soc Lond B Biol Sci
artigos.autores: Schaeffer L, Afanaseva L, Belotti E
artigos.destaque: By integrating developmental and epigenetic perspectives, we argue that myofibre ageing reflects not only cumulative damage but also the long-term consequences of how these exceptionally long-lived cells were originally built. This article is part of the theme issue 'Developmental circuits in ageing'.

resumo.texto: Development and ageing are two deeply intertwined processes, but it remains unclear how programmes established during early development influence the long-term stability of post-mitotic tissues. Skeletal muscle provides a model of choice to study the connection between these processes. Myofibres are long-lived, multinucleated syncytia whose identity and homeostasis rely on transcriptional, metabolic and epigenetic states established during embryonic and postnatal development. Throughout life, these states are further reinforced by satellite cell-derived inputs. In this review, we discuss how early specification cues, chromatin architecture and metabolic wiring establish durable regulatory circuits preserving myofibre integrity but also limiting its plasticity across the lifespan. These developmental features, combined with decades of physiological strain, progressively challenge genomic integrity and destabilize the maintenance of epigenetic information. Over time, this instability causes an epigenetic drift, encompassing alterations in DNA methylation, changes in histone landscapes and disruption in higher-order chromatin organization. Such alterations erode transcriptional fidelity and contribute to the appearance of hallmarks of the ageing phenotype. By integrating developmental and epigenetic perspectives, we argue that myofibre ageing reflects not only cumulative damage but also the long-term consequences of how these exceptionally long-lived cells were originally built. This article is part of the theme issue 'Developmental circuits in ageing'.

artigos.titulo: Depressive symptoms, possible sarcopenia, and functional disability among Chinese adults aged 50 years or more: A five-wave longitudinal study
artigos.autores: Mai T, Chao G
artigos.destaque: Participants with both exposures had the highest standardized risk, but there was no evidence of positive additive interaction and the joint association was less than multiplicative. The clinical usefulness of joint assessment requires prospective evaluation.

resumo.texto: To examine separate and joint associations of baseline depressive symptoms and possible sarcopenia with repeatedly assessed functional disability among Chinese adults aged 50 years or more.
Five-wave longitudinal cohort analysis, 2011-2020.

The presence of depressive symptoms was defined as a score ≥ 10 on the 10-item Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale. Possible sarcopenia was defined as low handgrip strength determined using the 2025 Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia age- and sex-specific thresholds because directly measured muscle mass was unavailable. We assessed disability in terms of basic and instrumental activities of daily living, separately and jointly. Modified Poisson generalized estimating equations estimated risk ratios; logistic models provided standardized risks and risk differences with cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals.

Of 9346 eligible participants, 8790 contributed 30,366 complete-case person-wave observations. Compared with neither exposure, adjusted risk ratios were 1.38 (95% confidence interval 1.32-1.44) for depressive symptoms only, 1.27 (1.18-1.37) for possible sarcopenia only, and 1.46 (1.38-1.56) for both. Standardized risks were 30.7%, 41.3%, 38.0%, and 46.0%, respectively. The risk difference for both versus neither was 15.3 percentage points (12.6-18.1). Additive interaction was -2.6 percentage points (-6.2 to 1.2), and the multiplicative interaction ratio was 0.84 (0.77-0.91). After multiple imputation, the contrast between the two single-exposure groups attenuated (risk ratio 1.06, 0.99-1.13).

Participants with both exposures had the highest standardized risk, but there was no evidence of positive additive interaction and the joint association was less than multiplicative. The clinical usefulness of joint assessment requires prospective evaluation.

artigos.titulo: Real-world effectiveness of tirzepatide in individuals with obesity: weight response, treatment-related factors and diabetes status
artigos.autores: Parrotta ME, Milani I, Chinucci M et al.
artigos.destaque: Tirzepatide was effective and well tolerated in routine practice. Greater weight loss occurred in obesity without T2D, while prior GLP-1RA exposure was independently associated with a reduced weight response. Previous GLP1-RA exposure may partly account for the different weight-loss trajectories observed between obesity with and without T2D. Residual differences at longer follow-up may reflect additional unmeasured clinical, metabolic, and treatment-related factors.

resumo.texto: Tirzepatide reduces body weight and improves glycemic control, but real-world comparisons between individuals with obesity with and without type 2 diabetes (T2D) remain limited, as well as the potential influence on weight-loss response of baseline characteristics (especially sex and previous treatment exposure). We aimed to compare anthropometric and metabolic outcomes in these populations, as well as treatment persistence, discontinuation, and the influence of prior GLP-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) exposure.

This retrospective multicenter study included adults with overweight/obesity without T2D (Ob) or with T2D (ObT2D) treated with tirzepatide. Data were collected at baseline and after 2-4 (T1), 5-8 (T2), and 9-15 (T3) months. Longitudinal changes were assessed using linear mixed-effects models, and multivariable analyses identified predictors of weight loss.

Ob participants (n=210, 74.8% female) were younger, had higher BMI, better glycemic control, and less previous GLP-1RA exposure than ObT2D participants (n=378, 49.7% female) (45.7% vs 79.3%; p<0.001). Weight loss was greater in Ob than ObT2D at all follow-ups (-5.0% vs -2.8%, -10.1% vs -3.3%, and -14.2% vs -4.7%; all p≤0.011), with mixed-effects models confirming different trajectories. This difference was attenuated and no longer statistically significant when analyses were restricted to treatment-naïve participants. Prior GLP-1RA exposure was independently associated with lower weight loss, while an interaction between prior GLP-1RA exposure and T2D status emerged at longer follow-up. No effect modification by sex or age was clearly detectable in this cohort. Discontinuation was more frequent in Ob, with adverse events, and financial barriers among the main reported reasons. Adverse events occurred in 16.9%, were mainly mild, transient gastrointestinal events, more frequent in Ob than ObT2D (26.9% vs 11.1%; p<0.001).

Tirzepatide was effective and well tolerated in routine practice. Greater weight loss occurred in obesity without T2D, while prior GLP-1RA exposure was independently associated with a reduced weight response. Previous GLP1-RA exposure may partly account for the different weight-loss trajectories observed between obesity with and without T2D. Residual differences at longer follow-up may reflect additional unmeasured clinical, metabolic, and treatment-related factors.

artigos.titulo: "Exploring the experiences of burnout and job satisfaction of mammographers engaging in enhanced and advanced practice within NHS breast services: A qualitative interview study of UK practice"
artigos.autores: Shariff SR, Scragg B, Spacey A
artigos.destaque: EP and AP mammographers experience professional fulfilment alongside occupational strain. Role expansion alone is insufficient to support workforce sustainability without investment in staffing, protected professional time, supportive leadership, and wellbeing. Addressing these factors may improve retention, resilience, and service sustainability.

resumo.texto: Enhanced practice (EP) and advanced practice (AP) mammographers are integral to UK National Health Service (NHS) Breast Services. While role expansion has increased service capacity and improved patient pathways, it has also introduced greater clinical responsibility, emotional labour, and organisational demands. Although burnout is recognised across healthcare professions, little is known about how EP and AP mammographers experience burnout alongside job satisfaction. This study therefore explored how EP and AP mammographers working within NHS Breast Services experience, perceive and negotiate burnout and job satisfaction and examined the organisational factors influencing occupational wellbeing.

A qualitative study using online semi-structured interviews was conducted with fifteen EP and AP mammographers across NHS Breast Services. Participants were recruited through purposive sampling, and interviews were analysed using inductive reflexive thematic analysis.

Four themes were developed: organisational pressure and constraints, emotional and cognitive burden, professional identity and meaning, and support systems and coping. Participants described workload, workforce shortages, administrative responsibilities, and emotional labour as contributors to burnout. Despite these challenges, AP provided professional fulfilment through autonomy, specialist expertise, meaningful patient interactions, and influence over care. Participants perceived limited organisational support as affecting their ability to cope with workplace demands. Findings demonstrate that burnout and professional fulfilment coexist, reflecting a balance between demands and resources.

EP and AP mammographers experience professional fulfilment alongside occupational strain. Role expansion alone is insufficient to support workforce sustainability without investment in staffing, protected professional time, supportive leadership, and wellbeing. Addressing these factors may improve retention, resilience, and service sustainability.

Workforce wellbeing strategies should extend beyond individual resilience and focus on organisational interventions supporting EP and AP roles while recognising the emotional demands of breast-imaging.

artigos.titulo: Cognitive and physiological responses to prolonged video viewing: Activities of the autonomic nervous system and hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal axis in relation to video interest
artigos.autores: Matsui H, Tanabe R, Mogi R et al.
artigos.destaque: A significant main effect of interest was observed only for LF. These findings indicate that the video conditions differed in subjective cognitive evaluation, with condition-dependent temporal changes detected for HR, whereas no significant interest × time interactions were detected for the other physiological indicators.

resumo.texto: In recent years, online lectures and conferences have become widespread, but prolonged video viewing has been suggested to affect psychological state and physiological regulation. However, few studies have objectively examined how such viewing influences autonomic and endocrine activity. This study aimed to evaluate changes in autonomic nervous system (ANS) activity and hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activity during the viewing of high- and low-interest videos. Twenty-six university students (10 males, 16 females; aged 21-24 years) watched high-interest (comedy) and low-interest (lecture) videos (90 minutes each). After viewing each video, they recorded subjective ratings of concentration, comprehension, interest, and fatigue. To assess autonomic nervous system activity, heart rate (HR) and heart rate variability (HRV) analyses, including the low-frequency (LF)/high-frequency (HF) ratio (LF/HF), LF and HF power, and very low-frequency (VLF) power, were performed. As stress markers, saliva samples were collected before, during, and after video viewing to measure cortisol, amylase, and chromogranin A (CgA). Subjective ratings showed that scores for concentration, comprehension, and interest were significantly higher, and fatigue was lower during the high-interest video. Regarding physiological indicators, significant main effects of time were observed for heart rate, LF/HF, LF, HF, and VLF, with overall patterns of lower heart rate and LF/HF and higher LF, HF, and VLF power during viewing. Salivary cortisol also decreased over time during both videos, demonstrating a significant main effect of time. However, no significant changes were observed in salivary amylase or chromogranin A. Furthermore, a significant interest × time interaction was observed for HR, but not for the other physiological indicators. A significant main effect of interest was observed only for LF. These findings indicate that the video conditions differed in subjective cognitive evaluation, with condition-dependent temporal changes detected for HR, whereas no significant interest × time interactions were detected for the other physiological indicators.

artigos.titulo: Network analysis of physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress among Chinese university students
artigos.autores: Wang J, Ma Y, Han T et al.
artigos.destaque: Cross-domain associations among physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress were concentrated in a limited number of dimensions, particularly stress, daytime dysfunction, exercise frequency, and exercise duration. Stress and daytime dysfunction showed relatively prominent sleep-psychological distress associations, whereas higher exercise frequency and longer exercise duration were associated with lower stress and fewer subjective sleep problems, respectively. No gender-related network differences were detected, but this does not establish network equivalence. These cross-sectional findings identify dimension-specific associations but cannot establish causal relationships or intervention targets.

resumo.texto: Physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress may be interconnected among university students, but their dimension-specific associations remain unclear. This study examined their network structure and compared male and female networks.

A convenience sample of 1,600 university students from two higher-education institutions in central China was surveyed from 16 March to 29 May 2026. Physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress were assessed using the Physical Activity Rating Scale, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and 21-item Depression Anxiety Stress Scales. A 12-node regularized partial correlation network was estimated. Expected influence, bridge expected influence, bootstrap procedures, and network comparison tests were used.

The network retained 27 non-zero edges, with stronger connections mainly within domains. Daytime dysfunction-stress had the largest positive cross-domain edge-weight point estimate, whereas exercise frequency-stress and exercise duration-subjective sleep quality were prominent negative connections. Stress showed relatively high expected influence and positive bridge expected influence point estimates, although bootstrap difference tests did not clearly distinguish these estimates from those of several other nodes. No gender-related differences were detected in global strength, network structure, or individual edges after multiple-comparison correction, while supplementary analyses indicated limited detection capability.

Cross-domain associations among physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress were concentrated in a limited number of dimensions, particularly stress, daytime dysfunction, exercise frequency, and exercise duration. Stress and daytime dysfunction showed relatively prominent sleep-psychological distress associations, whereas higher exercise frequency and longer exercise duration were associated with lower stress and fewer subjective sleep problems, respectively. No gender-related network differences were detected, but this does not establish network equivalence. These cross-sectional findings identify dimension-specific associations but cannot establish causal relationships or intervention targets.

artigos.titulo: A SIRT6-OVOL2 axis governs excitatory neuron resilience to chronic stress
artigos.autores: Zhou P, Li X, Sun H et al.
artigos.destaque: The SIRT6 allosteric agonist MDL-800 recapitulates these findings, eliciting antidepressant-like effects. These findings elucidate SIRT6's role in promoting stress resilience and support SIRT6-targeting strategies for treating depression.

resumo.texto: Current antidepressants primarily target monoaminergic and glutamatergic systems, but insufficiently protect against stress-induced neuronal dysfunction, highlighting the need for mechanism-based therapies. Here, we propose SIRT6 as a determinant of stress resilience. Excitatory neuron-specific SIRT6 overexpression attenuates chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced anhedonia, despair, anxiety-like phenotypes, and circadian disruption, whereas astrocytic or inhibitory neuronal overexpression provides no comparable effect. Conversely, excitatory neuron-specific SIRT6 deletion induces depression-like behaviors and disrupts circadian locomotor activity under basal conditions. Hippocampal single-nucleus transcriptomics identifies a stress-sensitive excitatory neuronal subtype depleted following CUMS but restored by SIRT6 overexpression. Regulatory network analysis positions OVOL2 as a central transcription factor governing stress-associated transcriptional alterations. SIRT6 directly interacts with OVOL2 and modulates its stability, thereby driving transcription of downstream targets, including Nrg1. The SIRT6 allosteric agonist MDL-800 recapitulates these findings, eliciting antidepressant-like effects. These findings elucidate SIRT6's role in promoting stress resilience and support SIRT6-targeting strategies for treating depression.

artigos.titulo: Ruff Shift Recharge: Feasibility and Acceptability of Canine-Assisted Breaks for Night-Shift Psychiatric Nurses
artigos.autores: Zock G, Hawks M
artigos.destaque: Drop-in AAA breaks were deliverable and acceptable to participating nurses at this site. Findings do not establish effectiveness, comparative advantage, mechanism, sustainability, or generalizability. Future studies should retain structured canine welfare monitoring and include usual-break and active nonanimal comparison conditions.

resumo.texto: To evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of canine-assisted breaks for night-shift psychiatric nurses and the practicality of participant measures and canine welfare monitoring in inpatient staff-focused animal-assisted activity (AAA) research.

Night-shift nurses (N = 11) were offered voluntary drop-in AAA breaks over 3 weeks at an inpatient psychiatric facility. Feasibility indicators included enrollment, attendance, survey completion, canine welfare monitoring, and adverse events. Acceptability indicators included session duration, observed engagement, and participant feedback. Mood was assessed before and after each break using the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule. Burnout and well-being were assessed 1 week before and after the intervention period. Outcomes were summarized descriptively. Therapy dog welfare was monitored through structured observation and repeated Canine Behavioral Assessment and Research Questionnaire assessments.

Eight nurses participated in 21 AAA breaks; durations ranged from 2 to 47 min (M = 22.3 min). Break-embedded data collection and canine welfare monitoring did not disrupt workflow, but follow-up survey attrition limited postintervention data. Feedback respondents described improved mood and energy and reduced stress. None of the 21 AAA breaks were terminated for canine stress. One site visit ended 30 min early after stress occurred without participants present.

Drop-in AAA breaks were deliverable and acceptable to participating nurses at this site. Findings do not establish effectiveness, comparative advantage, mechanism, sustainability, or generalizability. Future studies should retain structured canine welfare monitoring and include usual-break and active nonanimal comparison conditions.

artigos.titulo: Integrating U.S. embassy visits into global health education: student reflections on diplomacy-focused experiential learning
artigos.autores: Wallace LS, Mousetes S
artigos.destaque: The embassy visit expanded students' understanding of diplomacy while introducing previously unrecognized career pathways. Drawing on these findings, we propose a conceptual framework comprising four interconnected learning domains, suggesting that embassy visits provide a valuable component of global health education abroad.

resumo.texto: U.S. embassy visits offer a unique opportunity to examine the intersection of diplomacy and healthcare yet are rarely incorporated into health professions education. This study examined student reflections following a U.S. Embassy visit in North Macedonia to inform the integration of diplomacy-focused experiential learning into global health curricula.

Twenty-one Ohio State University undergraduates (12 females; mean age=19.48±0.60 years) participated in an experiential learning activity at the U.S. Embassy-Skopje, North Macedonia, which included discussions with embassy personnel on diplomacy and healthcare delivery within a diplomatic setting, as well as an Embassy Health Unit tour. Immediately following the visit, students completed a structured written reflection describing a meaningful or surprising aspect of the experience and its influence on their understanding of diplomacy, healthcare, or international collaboration. Reflections were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis. Themes were developed through iterative coding and refinement, with the second author independently reviewing the thematic framework to confirm interpretations and achieve consensus.

Reflexive thematic analysis identified three major themes-Expanding Conceptions of Diplomacy and the U.S. Foreign Service, Recognizing Healthcare as a Diplomatic Enterprise, and Broadening Professional Identity through Exposure to Global Health Careers-each comprising two related subthemes.

Student reflections highlighted adaptability, resilience, cross-cultural communication, teamwork, and flexibility while revealing progression from knowledge to understanding to professional identity. The embassy visit expanded students' understanding of diplomacy while introducing previously unrecognized career pathways. Drawing on these findings, we propose a conceptual framework comprising four interconnected learning domains, suggesting that embassy visits provide a valuable component of global health education abroad.

artigos.titulo: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy in Alzheimer Disease Continuum: Prevalence and Clinical Relevance in a Biomarker-Defined Memory Clinic Cohort
artigos.autores: Lalive HM, Ribaldi F, Mendes AJ et al.
artigos.destaque: The binary probable CAA label may therefore reflect greater amyloid burden without necessarily delineating a clinically distinct subgroup within the AD continuum. Marker-specific approaches targeting cortical superficial siderosis and high lobar CMB burden may prove more informative.

resumo.texto: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) frequently co-occurs with Alzheimer disease (AD), yet the prevalence and clinical significance of comorbid CAA among cognitively impaired individuals on the AD continuum remain unclear. We aimed to determine the frequency of probable CAA (Boston criteria v2.0) in a memory-clinic cohort of symptomatic amyloid-positive individuals and to compare demographic, clinical, cognitive, and biomarker profiles between those with and without comorbid probable CAA.

We conducted a retrospective cohort study at the Geneva Memory Center including amyloid-positive patients confirmed by CSF or amyloid PET. Participants meeting the Boston criteria v2.0 for probable CAA were classified as AD-probable CAA, whereas those with possible or no CAA were classified as AD-nonprobable CAA. Group differences were assessed using standard parametric and nonparametric tests, linear mixed-effects models for cognitive trajectories, logistic regression for cerebral microbleed (CMB)-CSF biomarker associations, and voxel-wise Statistical Parametric Mapping for regional amyloid PET differences.

Among 533 participants (mean age 73.8 ± 6.7 years, 59% female), 148 (28%) met criteria for probable CAA. Demographic characteristics, baseline cognition (mini-mental state examination: rank-biserial r = -0.05, 95% CI -0.16 to 0.07, p = 0.410), and longitudinal cognitive decline (β = -0.02, 95% CI -0.05 to 0.02, p = 0.309; median follow-up 28.1 months) did not differ between groups. Lower CSF Aβ42 was associated with lobar CMB burden (odds ratio per 1 SD decrease = 1.48, 95% CI 1.14-1.92, p = 0.004). Voxel-wise PET analyses revealed higher cortical amyloid uptake in AD-probable CAA with tracer-dependent patterns (cluster-level family-wise error p < 0.05).

More than one-quarter of amyloid-positive patients fulfilled the Boston criteria v2.0 for probable CAA. Probable CAA was not associated with a distinct clinical presentation or trajectory of cognitive decline. Higher cortical amyloid PET uptake in probable CAA and the association of lower CSF Aβ42 with lobar CMB burden suggest more prominent cerebral amyloidosis in this population. The binary probable CAA label may therefore reflect greater amyloid burden without necessarily delineating a clinically distinct subgroup within the AD continuum. Marker-specific approaches targeting cortical superficial siderosis and high lobar CMB burden may prove more informative.

artigos.titulo: Environmental epimutagens, epigenetic memory, and cancer latency
artigos.autores: Arimondo P, Coumoul X, Lepeule J et al.
artigos.destaque: Establishing causality will require physiologically realistic exposure models, longitudinal and lineage-resolved analyses, and functional tests distinguishing biomarkers of exposure from persistent mediators of cancer susceptibility. Such work may identify preventable exposures, informative biomarkers, and opportunities for cancer interception.

resumo.texto: Environmental exposures can cause cancer through DNA damage and mutations, but whether they can also leave durable, cancer-relevant changes in gene regulation is less clear. Chromatin helps maintain cell identity, differentiation state, and plasticity, providing a route by which non-genetic effects of exposure could persist after exposure. We define environmental epimutagens as agents or conditions that perturb chromatin regulation, and examine how such perturbations may influence cancer initiation and latency. Exposures can reach chromatin through altered metabolite or cofactor availability, interference with chromatin-regulating proteins, and direct chemical modification. Most resulting changes are transient, adaptive, or secondary. The central question is which become biologically embedded in long-lived cell populations, remain silent during latency, and alter responses to later genetic, inflammatory, or tissue-level pressures. Studies of inflammatory memory and transient disruption of chromatin repression show that short-lived perturbations can durably reprogram cellular potential, lower the threshold for tumor initiation, or generate tumorigenic states. Exposures may also influence the later selection of primed cells. Establishing causality will require physiologically realistic exposure models, longitudinal and lineage-resolved analyses, and functional tests distinguishing biomarkers of exposure from persistent mediators of cancer susceptibility. Such work may identify preventable exposures, informative biomarkers, and opportunities for cancer interception.

artigos.titulo: Exercise is medicine: Translating exercise-induced cognitive benefits into rehabilitation practice
artigos.autores: Nagamatsu LS, Nikpal MA, Marshall S et al.
artigos.destaque: Our goal is to provide clinicians and researchers with the background knowledge that will equip them with what, how, and why exercise should be part of usual care for all types of patients in rehabilitation settings.

resumo.texto: Exercise is one of the most impactful activities we can do to support physical, cognitive, and mental health across the lifespan and within both healthy and clinical populations. There is robust evidence that exercise promotes cognitive function, enhancing our ability to plan, think, and execute goal-directed behaviours. These cognitive benefits directly support patients in rehabilitation contexts to understand, follow, and safely apply clinical recommendations.

In this expert review, we provide an overview of the exercise neuroscience literature, highlighting key findings for the effects of exercise on cognition and brain health, followed by an overview of proposed mechanisms for these findings. Next, we translate these findings and offer a perspective in how they may be beneficial in rehabilitation settings, including special considerations for different populations experiencing cognitive decline. Finally, we end with a discussion of the limitations and future directions of this work, with special attention to equity, diversity, and inclusion to ensure that this knowledge remains accessible to all.

Our goal is to provide clinicians and researchers with the background knowledge that will equip them with what, how, and why exercise should be part of usual care for all types of patients in rehabilitation settings.

artigos.titulo: Effect of intensive blood pressure control on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes: prespecified analysis of secondary outcomes of BPROAD randomised controlled trial
artigos.autores: Wang W, Xu Y, Xu F et al.
artigos.destaque: Over a median of about four years, no statistically significant difference in incidence of a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment was observed among adults with type 2 diabetes receiving standard treatment of SBP (target <140 mm Hg) and intensive treatment (target <120 mm Hg). Intensive treatment was, however, associated with a reduction in the accrual of cerebral white matter lesion volume.

resumo.texto: To evaluate the effect of intensive compared with standard treatment of systolic blood pressure (SBP) on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes.
Multicentre, open label, outcome assessor masked, randomised controlled trial.
145 clinical centres across seven geographical regions in China.

12 821 adults aged ≥50 years with type 2 diabetes, raised SBP, and increased cardiovascular risk, of whom 12 434 without probable dementia at baseline were included in this cognitive ancillary study. Further assessments were performed annually and at the end of study.
Participants were randomly assigned to receive intensive treatment targeting SBP <120 mm Hg or standard treatment targeting SBP <140 mm Hg for up to five years.

The primary cognitive outcome was a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Secondary cognitive outcomes included all cause dementia, mild cognitive impairment, changes in cognitive functions, and changes in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics. A subset of participants underwent brain MRI at baseline (n=862) and at the end of study (n=605) to assess changes in white matter lesion volume and total brain volume.

6219 participants were assigned to receive intensive treatment and 6215 to receive standard treatment. Baseline mean age was 63.7 years, and 5567 (44.8%) participants were women. After one year, mean SBP was 121.6 mm Hg in the intensive treatment group and 133.2 mm Hg in the standard treatment group. During a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the primary cognitive outcome of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment occurred in 747 participants (3.69 events per 100 person years) in the intensive treatment group and 783 participants (3.89 events per 100 person years) in the standard treatment group (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86 to 1.06; P=0.38). In the MRI substudy (428 intensive treatment v 434 standard treatment), the intensive treatment group had a smaller increase in white matter lesion volume compared with the standard treatment group (between group difference -0.09 inverse hyperbolic sine (asinh) transformed cm3, 95% CI -0.15 to -0.02; P=0.01).

Over a median of about four years, no statistically significant difference in incidence of a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment was observed among adults with type 2 diabetes receiving standard treatment of SBP (target <140 mm Hg) and intensive treatment (target <120 mm Hg). Intensive treatment was, however, associated with a reduction in the accrual of cerebral white matter lesion volume.
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03808311.

artigos.titulo: L1CAM promotes motor function and cognitive function in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis in mice
artigos.autores: Li W, Wu J, Peng Y et al.
artigos.destaque: L1CAM can also suppress the neuroinflammation in the hippocampus of EAE mouse to ameliorate cognitive dysfunction. These results suggest that L1CAM may represent a promising therapeutic method for curing multiple sclerosis.

resumo.texto: Multiple sclerosis is an inflammatory demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system. L1 cell adhesion molecule (L1CAM) plays a critical role in neural development and injury repair. However, its influence on motor and cognitive functions in the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE)animal model of multiple sclerosis remains poorly understood. In this study, we utilized an EAE mouse model induced by MOG35-55 and administered recombinant L1CAM. We systematically evaluated its effects using behavioral assessments, histopathological analyses, and molecular biology. L1CAM can significantly ameliorate the demyelination in the spinal cord and sciatic nerve, increase the survival of spinal cord neurons, suppress the neuroinflammation in the lumbar spinal cord to reduce the clinical scores, and enhance hindlimb motor function. L1CAM can also suppress the neuroinflammation in the hippocampus of EAE mouse to ameliorate cognitive dysfunction. These results suggest that L1CAM may represent a promising therapeutic method for curing multiple sclerosis.

artigos.titulo: Irosustat and STX140 improve cognitive function and modulate amyloid, oxidative stress, and inflammatory pathways in experimental Alzheimer's disease
artigos.autores: Anbar HS, Lozon Y, Khodr V et al.
artigos.destaque: Morphological assessments showed that the drugs protected against brain atrophy and neuronal loss. Irosustat and STX140 are therefore promising therapeutic candidates for the management of Alzheimer's Disease.

resumo.texto: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is currently the most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder affecting the geriatric population. The pathology of AD has been described as neuronal loss caused by the accumulation of beta-amyloid plaques and the formation of neurofibrillary tangles resulting from tau protein phosphorylation. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic potential of steroid sulfatase inhibition using two drugs, the clinical steroid sulfatase inhibitor Irosustat and the multi-targeting preclinical candidate STX140, in scopolamine-induced AD in male Wistar rats compared to Donepezil as a standard drug. Behavioral tests such as the Open Field Test, Elevated Plus Maze Test, and Morris Water Maze Test were conducted to confirm the disease state and assess any improvement. At the end of the study, the animals were dissected to collect blood and brain samples for morphological, histological, immunohistochemical, biochemical, quantitative polymerase chain reaction and western blotting analyses. Treatment with Irosustat or STX140 improved learning, memory, and cognitive function compared with the disease group. The treated groups showed lowered brain tissue Aβ-40 & 42 levels, acetylcholinesterase activity, oxidative stress, and inflammatory markers. Morphological assessments showed that the drugs protected against brain atrophy and neuronal loss. Irosustat and STX140 are therefore promising therapeutic candidates for the management of Alzheimer's Disease.

artigos.titulo: Obesity linked to up to 27% lower risk of death in dementia
artigos.destaque: A surprising study of more than 4,500 older adults found that people who were overweight or obese when diagnosed with dementia had a 16% to 27% lower risk of death than those at a normal weight. Researchers suspect that extra energy and muscle reserves may help patients survive the disease's toll on the body, although the reason for the survival advantage remains unclear.

artigos.titulo: Weight-inclusive Care
artigos.autores: Crespo C, Tucker T
artigos.destaque: The conventional weight-centric model of care exacerbates weight stigma and leads to discrimination, gaps in care, and patient harm. The weight-inclusive care model is an alternative paradigm that can improve patient outcomes without damaging stigma. Behavior-focused management techniques used within integrative medicine can be embraced from a weight-inclusive lens, with respect to social and community factors such as body image and social influencers of health, to improve and sustain health from a personalized, respectful, and equitable lens.

resumo.texto: The conventional weight-centric model of care exacerbates weight stigma and leads to discrimination, gaps in care, and patient harm. The weight-inclusive care model is an alternative paradigm that can improve patient outcomes without damaging stigma. Behavior-focused management techniques used within integrative medicine can be embraced from a weight-inclusive lens, with respect to social and community factors such as body image and social influencers of health, to improve and sustain health from a personalized, respectful, and equitable lens.

artigos.titulo: Impact of Clinical Pharmacist Integration on Weight Management and Transplant Eligibility Among Patients With End-Stage Kidney Disease With Obesity
artigos.autores: Yang A, Tecza D, Medwin C et al.
artigos.destaque: IIP therapy appears safe and effective in ESKD. CPP integration was associated with greater weight loss, increased achievement of active transplant eligibility, and improved treatment optimization, highlighting its potential role in addressing obesity-related barriers to transplantation.

resumo.texto: Obesity is a barrier to kidney transplantation in patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). Injectable incretin peptides (IIP) have transformed weight management; however, real-world data in ESKD are limited. This study evaluated the impact of integrating a clinical pharmacist practitioner (CPP) into an interprofessional high body mass index (BMI) kidney transplant clinic on weight loss and transplant eligibility outcomes.

This single-center, retrospective study included adults with ESKD and obesity-prescribed IIP for transplant eligibility between June, 2022 and December, 2024. Cohort 1 included patients treated before CPP implementation; Cohort 2 included patients following implementation. The primary outcome was the percent change in body mass index (BMI) at 3, 6, and 12 months following IIP initiation. Secondary outcomes included changes in transplant eligibility status, IIP dose intensity, and predefined adverse events (AEs) at 12 months.

Eighty-four patients were included (Cohort 1: n = 28; Cohort 2: n = 56). Cohort 2 achieved greater BMI reductions at 3 (-2.0% vs. +1.45%), 6 (-3.3% vs. +1.16%), and 12 months (-8.0% vs. +2.8%; p < 0.01 for all). Among patients initially ineligible for kidney transplantation, 45% of patients in Cohort 2 became active on the transplant waitlist by 12 months compared with 11.5% in Cohort 1 (p = 0.006). More patients in Cohort 2 reached high IIP dose intensity (48.2% vs. 3.6%, p < 0.001), without differences in AE.

IIP therapy appears safe and effective in ESKD. CPP integration was associated with greater weight loss, increased achievement of active transplant eligibility, and improved treatment optimization, highlighting its potential role in addressing obesity-related barriers to transplantation.

artigos.titulo: The association between malnutrition and sarcopenia in community-dwelling older adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis
artigos.autores: Brandão AF, Zucatti KP, Frenzel AP et al.
artigos.destaque: Given the very low certainty of the evidence and the high risk of bias among the above-included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Nevertheless, the available evidence suggests that malnutrition or risk of malnutrition may be associated with sarcopenia in community-dwelling older adults, highlighting the need for early identification while emphasizing that well-designed longitudinal studies are required to confirm this association and better understand its temporal relationship, thereby supporting the development of integrated interventions.

resumo.texto: Malnutrition contributes to functional decline in older adults and may precede the development of sarcopenia. This review examined their underexplored relationship in community-dwelling older adults.

A systematic search, conducted up to February 6, 2024, across six databases and grey literature, identified studies on malnutrition (as measured by the MNA) and sarcopenia in community-dwelling older adults. Reviewers screened and extracted data independently, assessed bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and performed meta-analyses with random-effects models. Evidence certainty was rated using GRADE.

Twenty studies were included in the systematic review. Malnutrition prevalence ranged from 0.4% to 35.1%, while sarcopenia prevalence ranged from 4.8% to 50.2%. Nineteen studies contributed to the quantitative synthesis, depending on data availability. Meta-analysis of 13 studies (6,459 participants) showed that older adults with malnutrition or risk of malnutrition were more likely to present sarcopenia than their well-nourished counterparts (OR = 3.54; 95% CI: 2.52-4.98). No evidence of publication bias was identified for the OR analysis. A meta-analysis of nine studies reporting MNA as a score showed significantly lower MNA scores among individuals with sarcopenia (SMD = -1.17; 95% CI: -2.28 to -0.05). Most studies were classified as having a high risk of bias (n = 19). the certainty of the evidence was rated as very low in both analyses.

Given the very low certainty of the evidence and the high risk of bias among the above-included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Nevertheless, the available evidence suggests that malnutrition or risk of malnutrition may be associated with sarcopenia in community-dwelling older adults, highlighting the need for early identification while emphasizing that well-designed longitudinal studies are required to confirm this association and better understand its temporal relationship, thereby supporting the development of integrated interventions.

artigos.titulo: Trevogrumab (anti-GDF8) with or without garetosmab (anti-activin A) for prevention of muscle loss during semaglutide-induced weight reduction in people with obesity (COURAGE): a two-part, phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial
artigos.autores: Mosenzon O, Rosenstock J, Raya JG et al.
artigos.destaque: This study establishes proof of concept for GDF8 inhibition by trevogrumab alone as a generally well tolerated strategy to preserve lean mass during GLP-1 receptor agonist-induced weight loss. Although the addition of ActA inhibition by garetosmab further improved body composition and weight loss, the combination did not have favourable safety and tolerability. Further study is required to understand whether improved body composition during weight loss might preserve physical function and overall metabolic health.

resumo.texto: Rapid weight loss, as induced by GLP-1 receptor agonists, is accompanied by pronounced muscle loss. GDF8 (myostatin) and activin A (ActA), acting via ActRIIA/B receptors, are negative regulators of muscle mass. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of antibodies blocking GDF8 (trevogrumab) and ActA (garetosmab) on semaglutide-induced weight and muscle loss.

COURAGE is a two-part, phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial. This multicentre (60 sites), US-based trial enrolled participants aged 18-80 years with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2). In part A, participants were treated for 26 weeks with semaglutide (titrated to 2·4 mg subcutaneously weekly) in addition to a randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) concomitant treatment: placebo, trevogrumab 200 mg, trevogrumab 400 mg, or trevogrumab 400 mg and garetosmab 10 mg/kg. Trevogrumab was administered subcutaneously weekly and garetosmab was administered intravenously every 4 weeks. Part A also included a subsequent semaglutide withdrawal period, at which point participants (randomly assigned at baseline 1:1 within each group) received either trevogrumab 400 mg or placebo for an additional 26 weeks. In part B, participants were treated with semaglutide for 52 weeks and randomly assigned (1:2:2) to concomitant treatment with placebo, trevogrumab 25 mg, or trevogrumab 75 mg. Groups were stratified according to sex, BMI (<35 kg/m2vs ≥35 kg/m2), and participation in an exploratory MRI substudy assessing thigh muscle volume. Study participants, the principal investigators, and study site personnel were masked to all randomisation assignments throughout the study. Primary endpoints were percent change in lean mass, fat mass, and bodyweight from baseline to week 26 (part A) or week 52 (part B).
