Efficacy and safety analyses were done in all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of a study drug (efficacy, as randomly assigned; safety, as treated). COURAGE is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06299098, and is currently active, not recruiting.

975 participants were enrolled between June 21, 2024, and April 14, 2025. Mean age was 49·0 years (SD 13·2) and mean BMI was 36·7 kg/m2 (SD 5·0); 627 (64%) of 975 participants were female and 348 (36%) were male. In part A (n=605, of whom n=599 received at least one dose of study drug), a substantial decrease in lean mass was observed in the semaglutide plus placebo group at week 26 (-6·6% [95% CI -7·4 to -5·7]); the estimated treatment difference (ETD) versus semaglutide plus placebo was +3·1% (95% CI 1·9 to 4·3) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 200 mg, +2·7% (1·5 to 4·0) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg, and +4·5% (3·1 to 5·9) with semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg. In part B (n=376), lean mass percent change from baseline to week 52 for semaglutide plus placebo was -7·3% (-8·8 to -5·8); the ETD versus semaglutide plus placebo was +1·5% (-0·3 to 3·3) for semaglutide plus trevogrumab 25 mg, and +3·1% (1·3 to 4·9) for semaglutide plus trevogrumab 75 mg. Change from baseline in fat mass in part A was -15·6% (-17·4 to -13·9) in the semaglutide plus placebo group; the ETD was significant in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg group (-3·4% [-5·9 to -0·9]) and the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (-11·7% [-14·4 to -9·0]) in part A. No other groups in part A nor any in part B had significantly different changes in fat mass compared with semaglutide plus placebo. Percent change in bodyweight in part A was -10·6 (-11·6 to -9·7) in the semaglutide plus placebo group; the ETD was significant for the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (-2·7 [-4·1 to -1·2]). No other groups in part A nor any in part B had significantly different changes in bodyweight compared with semaglutide plus placebo. Semaglutide plus trevogrumab (25 mg, 75 mg, 200 mg, or 400 mg) was generally well tolerated with a safety profile similar to semaglutide plus placebo; however, semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg had a high incidence of serious adverse events (14 [9%] of 149) and treatment discontinuations (48 [32%] of 149). Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most commonly reported, and they occurred with similar incidence across treatment groups. Muscle spasms occurred more frequently in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group (61 [41%] of 149) compared with the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 200 mg or 400 mg groups (23 [8%] of 299) and semaglutide plus placebo groups (seven [5%] of 151). Most adverse events were mild to moderate in severity. Two deaths occurred during the study, both in the semaglutide plus trevogrumab 400 mg plus garetosmab 10 mg/kg group; a causal association between treatment and these events was not identified.

This study establishes proof of concept for GDF8 inhibition by trevogrumab alone as a generally well tolerated strategy to preserve lean mass during GLP-1 receptor agonist-induced weight loss. Although the addition of ActA inhibition by garetosmab further improved body composition and weight loss, the combination did not have favourable safety and tolerability. Further study is required to understand whether improved body composition during weight loss might preserve physical function and overall metabolic health.
Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

artigos.titulo: Prevalence and Prognostic Impact of Sarcopenic Dysphagia in Older Patients With Heart Failure
artigos.autores: Matsuo K, Yoneki K, Kobayashi K et al.
artigos.destaque: Sarcopenic dysphagia affected 24.0% of patients with HF, and was associated with poorer swallowing-related measures and prognosis.

resumo.texto: Dysphagia is common in older patients with heart failure (HF), but evidence regarding sarcopenic dysphagia remains limited. The purpose of this retrospective study was to clarify the prevalence of sarcopenic dysphagia and its relationship with swallowing-related measures and prognosis in older patients with HF.

The study group included patients aged ≥65 years admitted with HF between June 2021 and December 2023. Patients were classified into 3 groups using the diagnostic algorithm for sarcopenic dysphagia at discharge: robust (without sarcopenia), sarcopenia (with sarcopenia only), and sarcopenic dysphagia (with sarcopenia and dysphagia). Outcomes were swallowing-related measures (maximal tongue pressure, geniohyoid muscle area, and geniohyoid muscle echogenicity) and a 1-year composite outcome (all-cause death or HF-related readmission). Of 524 screened patients, 363 were analyzed (median age 83 years [Q1-Q3: 78-90 years], 46.6% women); 61 patients were robust (16.8%), 215 had sarcopenia (59.2%), and 87 had sarcopenic dysphagia (24.0%). In the analysis of covariance, swallowing-related measures were poorer in the sarcopenic dysphagia group compared with the robust group (P<0.05). In the Cox regression analysis compared with robust, sarcopenia was not statistically significantly associated with prognosis, but sarcopenic dysphagia was associated with a higher risk (hazard ratio 2.53, 95% confidence interval 1.30-4.90, P=0.006).
Sarcopenic dysphagia affected 24.0% of patients with HF, and was associated with poorer swallowing-related measures and prognosis.

artigos.titulo: Residual Risk Despite High Short Physical Performance Battery Scores in Older Patients With Heart Failure: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study
artigos.autores: Iwasaki T, Kurata H, Hata Y et al.
artigos.destaque: Even among older patients with HF and preserved physical performance (SPPB ≥10), accumulation of sarcopenia-related impairments was associated with an increased risk of adverse outcomes. Supplementing the SPPB with simple functional assessments may improve risk stratification in clinical practice.

resumo.texto: The prognostic value of the Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB), which is widely used to assess physical function and prognostic risk in patients with heart failure (HF), is unclear in patients with high SPPB scores. In this study we evaluated whether sarcopenia-related factors defined by the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia in 2019 provided additional prognostic value in this population.

This retrospective multicenter cohort study of the J-Proof HF registry included 3,044 patients aged ≥65 years with a discharge SPPB score ≥10. Impairments in handgrip strength, five-times chair stand test, and calf circumference were aggregated into a composite physical function score (range, 0-3). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or rehospitalization for HF within 1 year, which occurred in 25.0% of the cohort. The composite outcome risk increased in a stepwise manner with each additional impaired domain (adjusted hazard ratio per 1-point increase, 1.245; 95% confidence interval 1.132-1.370; P<0.001). The fully adjusted model showed acceptable discrimination (Harrell's C-index=0.694). Each domain independently demonstrated a similar magnitude of association with the outcome.

Even among older patients with HF and preserved physical performance (SPPB ≥10), accumulation of sarcopenia-related impairments was associated with an increased risk of adverse outcomes. Supplementing the SPPB with simple functional assessments may improve risk stratification in clinical practice.

artigos.titulo: Oops! I Cut It Again: Modulatory Proteolysis in Metabolic Health and Disease
artigos.autores: Pánico P, Velasco M, Ortíz-Huidobro RI et al.
artigos.destaque: Proteolytic systems regulate processes essential for maintaining metabolic homeostasis, including insulin secretion, insulin sensitivity and glucose uptake, adipose tissue physiology, muscle mass, and lipid metabolism in the liver. Concordantly, dysregulation of these systems contributes to the development of metabolic diseases, such as metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, obesity, sarcopenia, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, acting both as causal and aggravating factors.

resumo.texto: Proteolysis is an irreversible posttranslational modification that modulates protein stability, localization, interactions, and function. There are four intracellular proteolytic systems (calpains, caspases, ubiquitin-proteasome system, and lysosomes) and several extracellular proteases (metalloproteases and serine proteases). In this work, we review the diverse effects of proteolysis on the physiology of tissues vital for metabolic homeostasis as well as the contribution of proteolytic systems to the development of metabolic diseases. Proteolytic systems regulate processes essential for maintaining metabolic homeostasis, including insulin secretion, insulin sensitivity and glucose uptake, adipose tissue physiology, muscle mass, and lipid metabolism in the liver. Concordantly, dysregulation of these systems contributes to the development of metabolic diseases, such as metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, obesity, sarcopenia, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, acting both as causal and aggravating factors.

artigos.titulo: GLP-1 based therapy of obesity and type 2 diabetes
artigos.autores: Holst JJ
artigos.destaque: In addition, any prescription of a GLP-1RA should include a plan to mitigate adverse effects of treatment termination. Nevertheless, GLP-1RAs represent a major breakthrough in the therapy of metabolic disease and are now included among the essential medicines of the WHO.

resumo.texto: GLP-1 is 30-amino acid peptide that is secreted from the intestine in response to food intake. The release mechanism involves luminal exposure to as well as absorption and metabolism of the major nutrients. It functions mainly as a part of the ileal brake mechanism whereby nutrient entry in distal segments of the small intestine inhibit gastrointestinal secretion and motility as well as appetite and food intake, signalling nutritional abundance. It also functions as a second line incretin hormone. It acts on the brain via sensory vagal afferents, but also interacts with exposed neurons expressing the GLP-1 receptor in the circumventricular organs, in turn activating brain nuclei involved in appetite regulation and reward. High doses of GLP-1 cause nausea and vomiting, but slow dosing titration mitigates this. GLP-1 Receptor Agonists owe their actions to these physiological mechanisms and therefore represent powerful antidiabetic agents (A1c levels below 5.7%) and cause major weight loss (up to 20%), but also appear to reduce the systemic low-grade inflammation of obesity and type 2 diabetes and to exert beneficial action on the blood vessels, providing the GLP-1RAs with preventive effects on cardiovascular, hepatic, renal and central nervous system complications. Orally active GLP-1rAs have also been developed. It is emphasized that GLP-1RA therapy should be accompanied by lifestyle changes for efficacy and to prevent side effects of the weight loss. In addition, any prescription of a GLP-1RA should include a plan to mitigate adverse effects of treatment termination. Nevertheless, GLP-1RAs represent a major breakthrough in the therapy of metabolic disease and are now included among the essential medicines of the WHO.

artigos.titulo: Durable and Additive Disease Control at 52 Weeks With Ixekizumab Plus Tirzepatide Versus Ixekizumab Alone in Adults With Psoriatic Arthritis and Obesity or Overweight: Additional Results From a Randomized Clinical Trial
artigos.autores: Merola JF, Kartman CE, Fischer P et al.
artigos.destaque: Comprehensive improvements in disease activity, including ACR50, quality of life, weight, and metabolic outcomes, continued through week 52 and were greater with IXE+TZP than IXE alone, with no new safety concerns. These findings support concomitant IXE+TZP in patients with active PsA and immunometabolic disease.

resumo.texto: Obesity or overweight occurs in 72% to 82% of individuals with psoriatic arthritis (PsA). Previous data revealed greater disease control with concomitant ixekizumab (IXE) and tirzepatide (TZP) versus IXE alone in adults with active PsA and obesity or overweight with at least one weight-related comorbidity at the week 36 primary end point. The objective of this report is to evaluate the effect of IXE+TZP versus IXE on psoriatic disease control and safety measures up to week 52.

TOGETHER-PsA (ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT06588296) is a phase 3b, randomized, open-label, assessor-blinded 52-week trial. Participants were randomized 1:1 to IXE+TZP or IXE using US-approved doses. Week 52 outcomes were prespecified, non-multiplicity-controlled, and exploratory. Outcomes included 50% improvement in American College of Rheumatology response criteria (ACR50) and rheumatologic, dermatologic, patient-reported, metabolic, and safety outcomes.

A total of 271 participants were randomized (IXE+TZP, n = 138; IXE, n = 133). The proportion achieving the primary outcome of simultaneous ACR50 and ≥10% weight reduction continued to increase from week 36 through week 52 for IXE+TZP (39.2%) versus IXE (1.7%) (Δ37.5%; P < 0.001). ACR50 continued to diverge after week 36, with a clinically meaningful difference at week 52 for IXE+TZP (43.7%) versus IXE (15.7%) (Δ 28.0%; P < 0.001). IXE+TZP demonstrated significant improvements in ACR20, minimal disease activity, Disease Activity Index for Psoriatic Arthritis, patient-reported outcomes, and metabolic outcomes versus IXE alone. Safety profiles were consistent with previous studies for each drug.

Comprehensive improvements in disease activity, including ACR50, quality of life, weight, and metabolic outcomes, continued through week 52 and were greater with IXE+TZP than IXE alone, with no new safety concerns. These findings support concomitant IXE+TZP in patients with active PsA and immunometabolic disease.

artigos.titulo: Cardiovascular Outcomes in Semaglutide Versus Tirzepatide Users With Obesity and Atherosclerotic Disease: A Target Trial Emulation
artigos.autores: Aubrac G, Raquib RV, Le MT et al.
artigos.destaque: Among adults with overweight or obesity and ASCVD without diabetes, there was no significant difference in cardiovascular risk between semaglutide and tirzepatide.

resumo.texto: Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, is approved for cardiovascular risk reduction in individuals with overweight or obesity and cardiovascular disease. Whether tirzepatide, a dual GLP-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonist, has similar cardiovascular benefits remains unknown. The objective was to compare the effectiveness of semaglutide versus tirzepatide on the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in individuals with overweight or obesity and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) without diabetes.

This active comparator, new user study emulated a trial using national claims data from Komodo Health. Eligible individuals had a history of ASCVD and, within 1 year prior to initiation: BMI ≥ 27 with a diagnosis of overweight or obesity, continuous insurance coverage and no diabetes or contraindications. Prior GLP-1 receptor agonist or obesity medication users were excluded. The primary outcome was a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, hospitalization for heart failure or unstable angina, coronary revascularization and mortality (revised 5-point MACE). Secondary outcomes included revised 3-point MACE and individual endpoints. Hazard ratios were estimated using Cox models with inverse probability weighting.

There was a non-significant difference in risk of revised 5-point MACE (HR = 1.21, 95% CI: 0.99-1.51) or secondary outcomes between semaglutide and tirzepatide. Sensitivity analyses showed directionally consistent point estimates for revised 5-point MACE but highlighted sensitivity to decisions surrounding early events, off-label use, analytic approach and outcome definition.
Among adults with overweight or obesity and ASCVD without diabetes, there was no significant difference in cardiovascular risk between semaglutide and tirzepatide.

artigos.titulo: Pharmacomicrobiomics of GLP-1 receptor agonist gastrointestinal tolerability: integrating host genetics and the gut microbiome
artigos.autores: Kumbhare SV, Pedroso I, Sinha R et al.
artigos.destaque: Published methodological studies have suggested why such a study would be challenging: both interaction detection and the measurement unreliability associated with single-timepoint microbiome profiling impose substantial sample size penalties. This review summarizes what host genetics and the microbiome individually do and do not explain about GLP-1 RA tolerability, and describes the study design features, paired genotyping, repeat-sample metagenomics, and prospective symptom capture that a future joint analysis would require.

resumo.texto: Gastrointestinal (GI) adverse events, such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation, remain a dominant barrier to the sustained use of GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), driving discontinuation independently of the drug's metabolic benefits. Two host-side biological systems have been independently established as determinants of this variability. The first is host genetics, anchored by a 2026 genome-wide association study in which GLP1R variants predicted both weight-loss efficacy and nausea or vomiting risk, while a GIPR signal for vomiting was restricted to tirzepatide users. The second system is the gut microbiome, which regulates endogenous GLP-1 secretion through short-chain fatty acid and bile acid signaling and is itself reshaped by GLP-1 RA exposure. Pharmacomicrobiomics integrates host genetic and microbiome data to explain drug response. In the literature surveyed for this review, these two determinants are consistently examined in parallel rather than jointly: we did not identify a study, in GLP-1 RA therapy or in another drug class, that fit a 'host-genotype-by-microbiome' interaction model against a drug tolerability outcome. Published methodological studies have suggested why such a study would be challenging: both interaction detection and the measurement unreliability associated with single-timepoint microbiome profiling impose substantial sample size penalties. This review summarizes what host genetics and the microbiome individually do and do not explain about GLP-1 RA tolerability, and describes the study design features, paired genotyping, repeat-sample metagenomics, and prospective symptom capture that a future joint analysis would require.

artigos.titulo: "Are you going to get busy living or are you going to get busy dying?" Traumatic stressors in older adult-caregiver dyads during COVID-19 social scarcity in the USA
artigos.revista: Int J Qual Stud Health Well-being
artigos.autores: Kilaberia TR, Bell JF, Mair CA et al.
artigos.destaque: Powerlessness was a feature of traumatic stress reflected among older adults, and it was responsibility among caregivers. The study underscores the importance of trauma-informed support in caregiving at a time of involuntary and prolonged exposure to social scarcity.

resumo.texto: The 2022 US National Strategy to Support Caregivers emphasises the importance of understanding trauma as part of caregiving relationships. However, this focus has not been applied to understanding caregiving during social scarcity such as COVID-19 from a dyadic older adult-caregiver perspectives.

Drawing on joint perspectives of 11 older adult-caregiver dyads (N = 22), this qualitative thematic study explored how social scarcity impacted caregiving relationships, and whether there was evidence of traumatic stress in shared experiences. Dyads represented parent-child, relatives, and friend relationships aside from spouses.

Three themes were identified: (1) interactional micro-injuries and micro-adaptations; (2) nested troubles: present challenges and old wounds; and (3) eudaemonic deprivation-a perception of the erosion of order, meaning and purpose. Stressors were described as continuous fear, losses, grief, loneliness, loss of meaning, and disruptive feelings of anxiety impacting caregiving relationships.

Older adults demonstrated keener, sharper experiences of losses, and generally expressed self-focused distress whereas caregivers expressed generally adaptive and dyad-oriented responses. Powerlessness was a feature of traumatic stress reflected among older adults, and it was responsibility among caregivers. The study underscores the importance of trauma-informed support in caregiving at a time of involuntary and prolonged exposure to social scarcity.

artigos.titulo: Physiological acclimation to freshwater conditions reshapes the megalopae holobiont of Eriocheir sinensis
artigos.autores: Huang P, Du J, Cao L et al.
artigos.destaque: Correlation analysis revealed that the Amaricoccus was significantly correlated with key genes involved in host amino acid metabolism, oxidative stress, and the PI3K-Akt pathway, indicating that microbe-host interactions play a central role in coordinating energy redistribution to cope with osmotic stress. This study reveals the multi-dimensional adaptation mechanisms through which megalopae achieve the transition from a hyperosmotic to a hypoosmotic environment by integrating microbial community reconstruction, precise cell clearance mechanisms, and systematic metabolic reprogramming.

resumo.texto: To investigate the effects of natural salinity transition on megalopae of Eriocheir sinensis, this study systematically deciphered the response and adaptation mechanisms of megalopae to low-salinity stress. The results showed that the marine-to-freshwater habitat shift significantly reshaped the intestinal microbial community structure and increased the α-diversity index. The relative abundance of core bacterial taxa such as Amaricoccus was significantly elevated, while that of the conditional pathogen Flavobacterium was significantly reduced. At the host level, natural salinity transition stress triggered a series of profound cellular and molecular responses. To eliminate damaged cells, the Caspase-mediated apoptotic pathway and the LC3-mediated autophagic pathway were significantly activated. Meanwhile, signaling pathways controlling cell proliferation and growth, including Focal adhesion, Hippo, and PI3K-Akt, were significantly inhibited. Metabolically, stress response-related pathways such as Cortisol synthesis and secretion and AMP/Adenosine signaling were activated, driving an "energy-saving" strategy characterized by enhanced catabolism and reduced anabolism of proteins and lipids. Changes in the levels of key metabolites, such as 8-hydroxyguanosine and Ectoine, further confirmed the occurrence of oxidative stress and the shift in osmotic regulation strategies. Correlation analysis revealed that the Amaricoccus was significantly correlated with key genes involved in host amino acid metabolism, oxidative stress, and the PI3K-Akt pathway, indicating that microbe-host interactions play a central role in coordinating energy redistribution to cope with osmotic stress. This study reveals the multi-dimensional adaptation mechanisms through which megalopae achieve the transition from a hyperosmotic to a hypoosmotic environment by integrating microbial community reconstruction, precise cell clearance mechanisms, and systematic metabolic reprogramming.

artigos.titulo: Beyond Survival: A Systems-Integrated Approach to Clinical Self-Care in Primary Care
artigos.autores: Mehta DH, Locke A
artigos.destaque: Primary care clinician burnout is rising and is driven not only by individual stress, but also by structural inefficiency, workplace culture, and moral distress that limits clinicians' ability to deliver value-aligned care. This article reframes clinical self-care as a professional competency and patient safety imperative, grounded in integrative and salutogenic principles. It proposes a systems-integrated Swiss cheese prevention model with 3 aligned layers: (1) structural safeguards (workload/panel size, team-based care, and inbox time), (2) a culture of psychological and moral safety (leadership, dialogue, and peer support), and (3) embedded individual skills (sleep, boundaries, and mind-body regulation).

resumo.texto: Primary care clinician burnout is rising and is driven not only by individual stress, but also by structural inefficiency, workplace culture, and moral distress that limits clinicians' ability to deliver value-aligned care. This article reframes clinical self-care as a professional competency and patient safety imperative, grounded in integrative and salutogenic principles. It proposes a systems-integrated Swiss cheese prevention model with 3 aligned layers: (1) structural safeguards (workload/panel size, team-based care, and inbox time), (2) a culture of psychological and moral safety (leadership, dialogue, and peer support), and (3) embedded individual skills (sleep, boundaries, and mind-body regulation).

artigos.titulo: Addressing Primary Care Access with an Integrative Medicine Lens
artigos.autores: Gordon A, Rosenbaum E
artigos.destaque: All of these empower patients in their own health. Healthier patients, a broader team, and better physician retention combine to improve primary care access.

resumo.texto: Integrative medicine/ whole person care widens the lens through which we view health and healing, offering patients and physicians more options for care. Group visits and team-based care amplify physician effectiveness by increasing numbers of patients seen, addressing loneliness and social needs, and decreasing burnout. Interdisciplinary care addresses more health needs. All of these empower patients in their own health. Healthier patients, a broader team, and better physician retention combine to improve primary care access.

artigos.titulo: Acute Suffering, Act of Togetherness and On-Scene Space: A Concept Synthesis for Caring in Prehospital Emergency Care
artigos.autores: Holmberg M, Wallinvirta E, Rantala A et al.
artigos.destaque: Using the STOP-sign metaphor, the STOP synthesis highlights the importance of pausing in prehospital emergency care to recognize the patient as a multidimensional human being experiencing acute suffering. By integrating the concepts of acute Suffering, act of Togetherness and On-scene space within the prehospital context, the synthesis promotes a shift beyond a solely biomedical perspective toward a caring science understanding of suffering and care. The synthesis may support prehospital professionals, particularly nurses, in integrating caring and medical knowledge in clinical practice and provides a theoretical basis for future research, education and a holistic prehospital emergency care.

resumo.texto: Prehospital emergency care attends to patients experiencing acute suffering; a sudden and profound disruption affecting the person's life, body and existential well-being in the context of illness, injury or crisis. In this unpredictable and vulnerable setting, a central question emerges: how can caring needs be effectively met?
The aim of this paper is to develop a concept synthesis grounded in a caring science paradigm within the prehospital context, clarifying the nature of caring.

A concept synthesis based on a caring science theoretical framework was conducted using a combined deductive-inductive approach, integrating theory, clinical experience and relevant literature through an abductive and iterative process.

The synthesis introduces three interrelated concepts: acute Suffering (S), act of Togetherness (T) and On-scene space (O), situated within Prehospital emergency care (P). These concepts collectively shape the STOP synthesis. STOP positions caring as the core of prehospital emergency care, emphasizing a holistic perspective that extends beyond a purely biological understanding. It provides a structured framework for understanding and practicing the complexity of caring in this setting.

Using the STOP-sign metaphor, the STOP synthesis highlights the importance of pausing in prehospital emergency care to recognize the patient as a multidimensional human being experiencing acute suffering. By integrating the concepts of acute Suffering, act of Togetherness and On-scene space within the prehospital context, the synthesis promotes a shift beyond a solely biomedical perspective toward a caring science understanding of suffering and care. The synthesis may support prehospital professionals, particularly nurses, in integrating caring and medical knowledge in clinical practice and provides a theoretical basis for future research, education and a holistic prehospital emergency care.

artigos.titulo: Capturing Habits in Humans: Neural Circuitry, Computations, and Clinical Mechanisms
artigos.autores: Gera R, Wassum KM, Oh S et al.
artigos.destaque: Recent laboratory paradigms aim to reveal habit formation more sensitively than traditional outcome-devaluation paradigms, whereas real-world digital approaches use smartphones, wearables, and intensive longitudinal measurement to track habit formation and expression in everyday life. Integrating these approaches can help link habits to physiology, symptoms and neural circuits across laboratory to real-world and clinical contexts.

resumo.texto: Habits allow repeated behaviors to be executed efficiently, but habitual control can contribute to maladaptive inflexibility when it dominates despite changing goals or consequences. This review examines recent advances in understanding habitual control across neural circuits, computation, clinical phenotypes, and measurement. We first consider dorsomedial striatal mechanisms that support action-outcome learning and flexible goal-directed behavior and how chronic stress can alter striatal inputs to bias learning toward habitual control. Progress on what computational reinforcement-learning accounts for arbitration between goal-directed and habitual systems is described along prefrontal mechanisms guiding model-based control, action perseveration, and compulsivity in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). A wider behavioral spectrum beyond action initiation is provided, reviewing emerging work on habitual inhibition and frontostriatal circuit dynamics of avoidance in OCD. Recent laboratory paradigms aim to reveal habit formation more sensitively than traditional outcome-devaluation paradigms, whereas real-world digital approaches use smartphones, wearables, and intensive longitudinal measurement to track habit formation and expression in everyday life. Integrating these approaches can help link habits to physiology, symptoms and neural circuits across laboratory to real-world and clinical contexts.

artigos.titulo: Effects of short-term transport and relocation on stress-related hormones, bone metabolism, and growth performance in growing Holstein heifers
artigos.autores: Itagaki K, Kim S, Tsuchiaka S et al.
artigos.destaque: Additionally, free fatty acid (FFA) concentrations increased after transport (P<0.01), whereas average daily height gain (ADHG) significantly decreased following transport (P=0.018). In conclusion, short-term transport and relocation did not induce an increase in plasma cortisol but were associated with transient changes in bone metabolic markers, plasma FFA concentrations, and ADHG.

resumo.texto: Livestock transport is widely recognized as a significant stressor that affects animal health, growth, and welfare. This study evaluated the effects of short-term transport and relocation on stress-related hormones, bone metabolism, and growth in 14 Holstein heifers. Data were collected 14 days before transport (-14 d), on the day of transport (0 d), and 7 days after transport (7 d) across two seasons (spring and summer). Measurements included cortisol (plasma and saliva), fecal glucocorticoid metabolites (FGMs), oxytocin (plasma and saliva), bone metabolic markers (plasma), several biochemical parameters (plasma), and growth metrics. Plasma cortisol significantly decreased post-transport (P=0.037), indicating that plasma cortisol did not increase following short-term transport and relocation. While salivary cortisol and FGM concentrations remained stable after transport, FGM concentrations were significantly higher in summer than in spring (P<0.01), suggesting a possible association with seasonal environmental differences. Regarding bone metabolism, both tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase 5b (TRAP5b) and alkaline phosphatase isoenzyme 3 (ALP3) decreased after transport (P<0.01). The bone-formation to -resorption ratio (ALP3/TRAP5b index) increased transiently on day 0, before declining. Additionally, free fatty acid (FFA) concentrations increased after transport (P<0.01), whereas average daily height gain (ADHG) significantly decreased following transport (P=0.018). In conclusion, short-term transport and relocation did not induce an increase in plasma cortisol but were associated with transient changes in bone metabolic markers, plasma FFA concentrations, and ADHG.

artigos.titulo: Metabolic-translational control of NK cell fitness under chronic stress
artigos.autores: Ortutu BF, Guo X, Thomas CJ et al.
artigos.destaque: We propose that the interaction between metabolic capacity and translational demand may determine whether NK cells maintain function or become dysfunctional under persistent stress. This framework provides a rationale for engineering NK cells with greater metabolic-translational reserve and resilience to metabolically restrictive tumor microenvironments, with potential implications for improving the persistence and therapeutic efficacy of adoptive and CAR-NK cell therapies.

resumo.texto: Natural killer (NK) cells are critical mediators of immune surveillance, yet their functional capacity is frequently compromised by chronic metabolic and environmental stress. Although metabolic reprogramming is recognized as a major determinant of NK-cell activity, how metabolic capacity is coordinated with translational control to sustain effector function and cellular persistence remains poorly understood. This review examines NK-cell fitness as a dynamic metabolic-translational balance in which nutrient availability, mitochondrial function, redox homeostasis, and nutrient-sensing pathways determine the resources available for biosynthesis, while translational control regulates their allocation toward effector protein production, adaptation, and cellular maintenance. We highlight eukaryotic elongation factor-2 kinase (eEF2K) as a mechanistically defined regulator of translational elongation with direct evidence of relevance to NK-cell function, while Nucleus Accumbens-Associated Protein 1 (NAC1) is considered a candidate regulator of NK-cell metabolic adaptation whose role remains to be established. We propose that the interaction between metabolic capacity and translational demand may determine whether NK cells maintain function or become dysfunctional under persistent stress. This framework provides a rationale for engineering NK cells with greater metabolic-translational reserve and resilience to metabolically restrictive tumor microenvironments, with potential implications for improving the persistence and therapeutic efficacy of adoptive and CAR-NK cell therapies.

artigos.titulo: A Co-Designed and Bilingual WhatsApp-Based Chatbot Intervention (PflegeBot) for Informal Caregivers in Germany: Single-Arm Nonrandomized Feasibility Study
artigos.autores: Gencer H, Mena E, Freund T et al.
artigos.destaque: PflegeBot could be delivered through WhatsApp, and participants providing follow-up data reported high usability and generally favorable satisfaction. Controlled evaluations with objective engagement data and assessment of differential reach and outcomes are warranted.

resumo.texto: Informal caregivers play a central role in long-term care but experience elevated risks of stress, depressive symptoms, and caregiver burden, alongside barriers to accessing preventive support. Low-threshold digital public health interventions may offer scalable support; however, evidence on their feasibility, usability, and contextual fit remains limited, particularly for heterogeneous caregiver populations.

This study describes the development and implementation of PflegeBot, an intersectionality-informed WhatsApp-based chatbot intervention, and evaluates its feasibility, usability, and acceptability among informal caregivers in Germany.

A single-arm, nonrandomized feasibility study with pre-post assessments was conducted between December 2023 and March 2024. Informal caregivers aged 18 years and older were recruited via community-based, institutional, and online channels. PflegeBot was a co-designed, bilingual (German and Turkish) WhatsApp-based chatbot that delivered 84 scheduled messages over 12 weeks. Content included caregiving information, self-care, and cognitive behavioral therapy-informed self-help, plus optional frequently asked questions and question functions. Baseline and full follow-up assessments were administered online. Feasibility was assessed using indicators of recruitment, chatbot initiation and message delivery, opt-out, and provision of follow-up measures. Usability was assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUS), and acceptability was assessed using study-specific items. Exploratory outcomes included perceived stress (4-item Perceived Stress Scale [PSS-4]), caregiver burden (4-item Zarit Burden Interview [ZBI-4]), depressive symptoms (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale [CES-D]), and loneliness (6-item De Jong Gierveld Loneliness Scale [DJGLS-6]). Analyses were descriptive; no hypothesis tests were conducted. Open-ended follow-up feedback was examined using a systematic inductive descriptive approach.

Of 102 participants included in the baseline analysis sample, 84 (82%) were women. According to chatbot log data, message delivery was initiated for 67 participants. Forty-nine participants provided at least one follow-up measure, and complete SUS data were available for 46 participants. The mean SUS score was 82.45 (SD 14.86, 95% CI 78.03-86.86; range 47.5-100), and 35 out of 46 (76%) participants scored at or above the benchmark of 68. Overall satisfaction with PflegeBot had a mean rating of 4.02 out of 5 (SD 0.98; n=46). Among participants responding to the relevant item, 1 out of 45 (2%) reported using the optional FAQ function. Mean changes were -0.57 (95% CI -1.24 to 0.10; n=35) for perceived stress, 0.81 (95% CI -0.02 to 1.63; n=36) for caregiver burden, -2.38 (95% CI -5.42 to 0.66; n=34) for depressive symptoms, and -0.39 (95% CI -0.90 to 0.12; n=36) for loneliness. Open-ended feedback highlighted needs for more flexible delivery, greater tailoring, and easier navigation.

PflegeBot could be delivered through WhatsApp, and participants providing follow-up data reported high usability and generally favorable satisfaction. Controlled evaluations with objective engagement data and assessment of differential reach and outcomes are warranted.

artigos.titulo: Evaluating Wearable Electrodermal Activity as a Candidate Digital Biomarker of Occupational Well-Being: Longitudinal Real-World Study
artigos.autores: Salonius H, Kytölä P, Pakarinen S et al.
artigos.destaque: These findings provide practical evidence that continuous wearable EDA monitoring can be combined with mEMA in naturalistic occupational settings. Associations between the proprietary DNE index, valence, burnout, and work engagement provide preliminary convergent evidence supporting further evaluation of DNE as a candidate digital biomarker in occupational well-being research. Interpretation remains constrained by the proprietary signal-processing pipeline, and this study does not establish construct-specific validity, prospective predictive performance, screening or diagnostic validity, sensitivity to change, or individual-level monitoring usage.

resumo.texto: Wearable physiological sensing and mobile self-report methods offer new opportunities for monitoring occupational well-being in real-world settings. However, interpreting continuous physiological signals in relation to psychological states such as job burnout and work engagement remains challenging, particularly when using deployable systems that rely on proprietary signal processing.

This study examined a proprietary electrodermal activity (EDA)-derived arousal index as a candidate digital biomarker for research on occupational well-being. We examined associations between job burnout, work engagement, and sympathetic activation indexed by a device-derived EDA metric, and assessed whether combining physiological data with mobile-based ecological momentary assessment (mEMA) of valence provides complementary information.

A total of 75 knowledge workers participated, with sufficient paired physiological and mEMA data obtained from 57 participants in wave 1 and 51 in wave 2 (total observations=108). Participants were monitored continuously over 14 consecutive days at 2 time points 6 months apart. Autonomic arousal was operationalized using the device-derived double normalized electrodermal activity (DNE) index obtained from wearable EDA recordings. Valence was assessed using mEMA. Associations between physiological activation, valence, and occupational well-being outcomes were analyzed using generalized least squares models with a compound-symmetry covariance structure to account for repeated observations within participants.

The wearable-derived DNE index showed a clear diurnal pattern, with higher values during daytime and lower values during nighttime. Greater within-nighttime DNE variability was associated with higher burnout (estimate=0.02, 95% CI 0.01-0.03; P<.001) and lower engagement (estimate=-0.03, 95% CI -0.05 to -0.01; P=.009). The daily DNE × valence interaction was also associated with engagement (estimate=-0.35, 95% CI -0.69 to -0.00; P=.047). Removing all DNE and valence variables significantly worsened model fit for both burnout (χ²₁₀=28.5; P=.002) and engagement (χ²₁₀=23.7; P=.009), supporting their combined explanatory value. Model-based profiles further showed that negative valence was associated with higher predicted burnout and lower predicted engagement than positive valence across both high- and low-arousal scenarios, although prediction intervals were wide and partially overlapping. Model comparisons showed that including physiological and mEMA-based variables improved explanatory power.

These findings provide practical evidence that continuous wearable EDA monitoring can be combined with mEMA in naturalistic occupational settings. Associations between the proprietary DNE index, valence, burnout, and work engagement provide preliminary convergent evidence supporting further evaluation of DNE as a candidate digital biomarker in occupational well-being research. Interpretation remains constrained by the proprietary signal-processing pipeline, and this study does not establish construct-specific validity, prospective predictive performance, screening or diagnostic validity, sensitivity to change, or individual-level monitoring usage.

artigos.titulo: Depression, anxiety, and stress and fulfillment of contraceptive preferences among young people in Texas and California
artigos.autores: Hecht HK, Yarger J, Hopkins K et al.
artigos.destaque: Young people experiencing mental distress were less likely to realize their contraceptive preference. Future interventions should focus on providing mental health support and improving contraceptive access for young people, including addressing insurance barriers. A primary care model integrating both mental and reproductive healthcare will help to address important health needs of young people.

resumo.texto: Young people face both increased mental health concerns and growing barriers to accessing reproductive healthcare.
This study examined the association of depressive, anxiety and stress symptoms with preferred contraceptive method use, a measure of healthcare access and reproductive autonomy.

We used baseline data (April 2018-May 2023) from a cluster randomized trial at 29 community colleges in Texas and California. Participants were 2,065 sexually active, first-year community college students ages 18-25. We used multivariable mixed effects multinomial logistic regression for clustered data to examine the association of depressive (CESD-10) or anxiety and stress symptoms (DASS-21) and fulfillment of participants' contraceptive preferences (unfulfilled, fulfilled or unknown), controlling for factors related to mental health and care access.

Overall, 51% of participants had an unfulfilled contraceptive preference, and 4% did not know what they preferred. Multivariable results showed elevated depressive symptoms (relative risk ratio [RRR]: 1.31, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.01, 1.71) or anxiety and stress symptoms (RRR: 1.31, 95% CI 1.03, 1.66) were associated with having an unfulfilled contraceptive preference versus a fulfilled preference. Additionally, elevated depressive symptoms were associated with having an unknown preference versus fulfilled preference (RRR: 2.98, 95% CI: 1.78, 4.99). Participants with mental distress were also significantly more likely to report cost or insurance barriers as reasons for having an unfulfilled preference (p < 0.05).

Young people experiencing mental distress were less likely to realize their contraceptive preference. Future interventions should focus on providing mental health support and improving contraceptive access for young people, including addressing insurance barriers. A primary care model integrating both mental and reproductive healthcare will help to address important health needs of young people.
ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03519685.

artigos.titulo: Examining the Feasibility, Acceptability, and Preliminary Efficacy of a Health App for Postacute Pandemic Years in Managing Physical and Psychological Distress Symptoms: Pilot Quasi-Experimental Study
artigos.autores: Liu JYW, Man D, Lai FHY et al.
artigos.destaque: The study demonstrated the HAPPY app's feasibility, acceptability, and potential efficacy for managing physical and psychological distress symptoms. High recruitment, retention, and adherence rates, along with measurable improvements in distress, fatigue, sleep quality, and pain, suggest the app's promise as a scalable intervention.

resumo.texto: Physical and psychological distress symptoms can adversely affect daily functioning and quality of life, highlighting the need for accessible self-management support. Although mobile health (mHealth) interventions show promise in supporting physical symptom management, evidence regarding their feasibility and potential effects on psychological distress remains limited.

This pilot study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of the health app for postacute pandemic years (HAPPY) for managing physical and psychological distress symptoms.

A 2-arm, single-blind, quasi-experimental trial was conducted from July 2023 to January 2024. Thirty-eight participants experiencing distress symptoms related to COVID-19 were assigned to the experimental group or a waitlist control group. The experimental group received a 24-week mHealth intervention through the HAPPY app, which included an 8-week supervised phase with weekly face-to-face sessions and a 16-week self-management phase. The control group received no active treatment. Feasibility was assessed through recruitment, adherence, and adverse event monitoring, whereas preliminary efficacy was evaluated at 8 weeks (T1) and 24 weeks (T2) and compared with baseline (T0) using quantitative measures of distress, fatigue, sleep quality, pain, emotional regulation, and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

The study demonstrated the feasibility of the HAPPY app, with a recruitment rate of 88.37% (38/43), a dropout rate of 10.5% (4/38), and an adherence rate of 93.33% (14/15) for the supervised sessions. No adverse events were reported. Significant within-group improvements were observed for distress (Kessler Psychological Distress Scale [K10]; P<.001), fatigue (Brief Fatigue Inventory-Chinese [BFI-C]; P<.001), sleep quality (Chinese Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index [CPSQI]; P=.009), and PTSD symptoms (Chinese Impact of Event Scale-Revised [CIES-R]; P=.02). However, between-group differences were limited.

The study demonstrated the HAPPY app's feasibility, acceptability, and potential efficacy for managing physical and psychological distress symptoms. High recruitment, retention, and adherence rates, along with measurable improvements in distress, fatigue, sleep quality, and pain, suggest the app's promise as a scalable intervention.
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05459896; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05459896.

artigos.titulo: Human cognitive performance-associated gut microbiota influences learning and memory in mice through arginine and pterin metabolism
artigos.autores: Tracey H, Antolín A, Teichenne J et al.
artigos.destaque: Our findings highlight the potential role of the gut microbiome in cognitive performance among older individuals, particularly information processing speed, and identify potential mechanisms involving alterations in arginine and pterin metabolism. Integrating human and mouse data supports a model in which microbiota-associated metabolic remodeling influences cognitive performance.

resumo.texto: The human gut microbiome undergoes changes across the lifespan and has been implicated in age-related decline. The symbol digit modalities test (SDMT) is a measure of information processing speed and is sensitive to mild cognitive impairment. Here, we assessed SDMT scores and fecal shotgun metagenomics in older individuals from the Imageomics cohort (n = 867) and performed fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from human donors to male C57BL/6 mouse recipients. In mice, we evaluated cognitive performance using the Morris water maze (MWM) and measured neurone density, fecal shotgun metagenomics, hippocampal metabolomics, and cortical gene expression to identify microbial-derived functional properties related to cognitive performance. In humans, both microbial species composition and functional profiles were associated with cognitive performance. FMT from high-SDMT donors improved cognitive performance and increased neuronal density in recipient mice compared with FMT from low-SDMT donors. In both humans and mice, higher cognitive performance was associated with arginine and proline metabolism and pterin-related pathways. In mice receiving microbiota from high-SDMT donors, cortical gene expression showed enrichment of dopamine receptor pathways and reduced dopamine reuptake and catecholamine biosynthesis. Our findings highlight the potential role of the gut microbiome in cognitive performance among older individuals, particularly information processing speed, and identify potential mechanisms involving alterations in arginine and pterin metabolism. Integrating human and mouse data supports a model in which microbiota-associated metabolic remodeling influences cognitive performance.

artigos.titulo: Semantic Processing in Unresponsive Patients With Acute Brain Injury
artigos.autores: Alkhachroum A, Manolovitz B, McKeown J et al.
artigos.destaque: Semantic processing was a specific but insensitive biomarker of recovery, suggesting potential utility as a rule-in marker of preserved cognitive function. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger multicenter cohorts before clinical implementation.

resumo.texto: Early prognostication after acute brain injury (ABI) is challenging because behavioral responsiveness may not accurately reflect preserved cognitive function. Neural responses to semantic incongruity can identify language processing despite the absence of overt behavior. We investigated whether bedside EEG could detect semantic processing in unresponsive patients with ABI and whether its presence was associated with long-term outcomes.

In this prospective 2-center cohort study, unresponsive adults with ABI admitted to neurologic intensive care units between 2022 and 2025 underwent bedside EEG during a language paradigm comparing congruent and incongruent sentence endings (e.g., "my favorite color is green/soon"). Semantic processing was defined by differential event-related responses within centroparietal channels (300-500 milliseconds) using cluster-based permutation testing with false discovery rate correction. Outcomes were assessed for recovery of consciousness and functional recovery (Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended score ≥4) at 12 months by blinded interviewers. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, accuracy, and likelihood ratios.

Among 105 patients (mean age 58 ± 19 years; 21% women; 53% Hispanic/Latino), the most common etiologies were intracerebral hemorrhage (45%), traumatic brain injury (43%), and subarachnoid hemorrhage (10%). Withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy occurred in 31%. Semantic processing was detected in 13 patients (12%). Recovery of consciousness occurred in 77% of patients with semantic processing compared with 49% without semantic processing (odds ratio [OR] 3.5; 95% CI 0.9-13.5, p = 0.08). Functional recovery occurred in 42% with semantic processing compared with 14% without semantic processing (OR 4.5; 95% CI 1.2-16.6, p = 0.03). Semantic processing was highly specific but insensitive for predicting both recovery of consciousness (specificity 94%, sensitivity 18%) and functional recovery (specificity 92%, sensitivity 29%). After excluding patients who underwent withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy or died of non-neurologic medical complications, specificity increased to 100% for recovery of consciousness and 95% for functional recovery.

EEG evidence of semantic processing can be detected in a subset of unresponsive patients with ABI during the acute phase of injury and is associated with favorable long-term outcomes. Semantic processing was a specific but insensitive biomarker of recovery, suggesting potential utility as a rule-in marker of preserved cognitive function. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger multicenter cohorts before clinical implementation.

artigos.titulo: Active Inference and Predictive Processing for Skill Learning: Implications for Skill Acquisition in Coaching Practice
artigos.autores: Mackey J, Collins D, Taylor J
artigos.destaque: We suggest that AIF offers a parsimonious perspective, accommodating the dynamic, embodied and enactive nature of skill acquisition without the necessity of committing to either framework's specific assumptions. This perspective provides practitioners with a coherent and flexible framework for understanding and designing skill learning interventions, offering a practically useful account of skill acquisition for coaching practice.

resumo.texto: This paper explores the potential of the Active Inference Framework (AIF) and Predictive Processing (PP) to advance our understanding of skill and motor learning with a key focus on introducing these concepts to coaches and highlighting their practical implications. Conceptual frameworks such as Information Processing (IP) and Ecological Dynamics (ED) have contributed significantly to the field of skill acquisition. Despite recent efforts to reconcile these perspectives, however, their fundamentally different theoretical foundations concerning perception, cognition and learning processes pose substantial challenges for integration. Although ED has made valuable contributions through its focus on perception-action coupling and direct interaction with the environment, it involves adopting a radical ontological stance that emphasises rejecting traditional cognitive constructs that can complicate practical applications in coaching. Conversely, IP's reliance on concepts such as stored motor programs and the view of the brain as a computer-like processor can limit its ability to account for the dynamic, emergent nature of skill acquisition in real-world contexts. We suggest that AIF offers a parsimonious perspective, accommodating the dynamic, embodied and enactive nature of skill acquisition without the necessity of committing to either framework's specific assumptions. This perspective provides practitioners with a coherent and flexible framework for understanding and designing skill learning interventions, offering a practically useful account of skill acquisition for coaching practice.

artigos.titulo: Modest loss of sleep increases susceptibility to cybersecurity threats
artigos.revista: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
artigos.autores: Schechtman E
artigos.destaque: The transition led to a ~13% increase in the probability of clicking a suspicious link, without affecting the probability of opening the email or reporting it as spam. These results demonstrate that even modest, mundane, and acute loss of sleep has real-life, potentially hazardous, implications for cognitive function.

resumo.texto: Sleep restriction leads to impaired cognitive processing across domains. I examined whether the transition to daylight saving time (DST), typically accompanied by compromised sleep, would lead to an increase in the probability of falling prey to a simulated phishing attack using a fully naturalistic experiment with random assignment and blinding. A predatory email was sent to employees at the University of California, Irvine (N = 11,218) either on the morning of Monday following the transition to DST or one week earlier. The transition led to a ~13% increase in the probability of clicking a suspicious link, without affecting the probability of opening the email or reporting it as spam. These results demonstrate that even modest, mundane, and acute loss of sleep has real-life, potentially hazardous, implications for cognitive function.

artigos.titulo: Cross-Species Approaches to Understanding Human Cognition
artigos.autores: Buffalo EA, Cohen MR, Constantinidis C et al.
artigos.destaque: By linking mechanism to behavior, these approaches guide targeted interventions and effective clinical translation. While challenges remain, these integrated approaches are advancing our understanding of the mechanistic foundation of human cognition.

resumo.texto: Recent methodological advances including high-density intracranial recordings and population-level analytical frameworks enable deeper and more direct integration between animal models and human neuroscience. As a result, there is an increasing need for standardized behavioral paradigms and circuit-level analyses that can be used in both animals and humans. Cross-species approaches provide crucial foundations for treating neurological and psychiatric disorders. Parallel experiments validate therapeutic targets and enable development of mechanistically grounded behavioral biomarkers for early disease detection. Here, we provide a brief review of recent findings that have direct implications for attention deficits, memory impairments, and decision-making dysfunctions. By linking mechanism to behavior, these approaches guide targeted interventions and effective clinical translation. While challenges remain, these integrated approaches are advancing our understanding of the mechanistic foundation of human cognition.

artigos.titulo: Six Challenges for a Mechanistic Science of Human Interoception
artigos.autores: Avidan G, Allen MG, Khalsa SS et al.
artigos.destaque: These challenges are best understood as linked requirements for moving interoception research from relevance to mechanism. Together, they highlight the need to move beyond predominantly static, passive, and single-modality approaches toward studies that can test how internal bodily signals relate to neural activity, behavior, and health.

resumo.texto: Human interoception has become a major focus of systems, cognitive, and clinical neuroscience. Work across the past decade has shown that signals originating within the body shape perception, emotion, cognition, behavior, and health. Despite rapid methodological and conceptual progress, which substantially expanded our understanding of how bodily signals are processed and represented, much of the field remains constrained by descriptive methods. As these approaches passively assess bodily signals or subjective awareness, they have limited ability to establish causal mechanisms or translate interoceptive findings into clinically informative frameworks. Here, we identify six challenges and corresponding methodological directions for advancing human interoception research: strengthening integration of animal and human models, developing causal perturbation paradigms, capturing interoception in ecologically valid contexts, standardizing multidimensional measurement across bodily systems, adjudicating between computational accounts, and translating mechanistic insights into clinically informative models of health and disease. These challenges are best understood as linked requirements for moving interoception research from relevance to mechanism. Together, they highlight the need to move beyond predominantly static, passive, and single-modality approaches toward studies that can test how internal bodily signals relate to neural activity, behavior, and health.

artigos.titulo: Embodied Computation: How Does Embodiment Impact Sensorimotor and Cognitive Processing?
artigos.autores: Schaffer ES, Saxena S, Keller R et al.
artigos.destaque: This review focuses on embodied computation: how the physical body shapes neural activity and behavior across functions ranging from motor control to cognitive processes. We examine the impact of embodiment in several domains, including compositional reuse, intrinsic motivation, metabolic costs, and connectome-constrained computation, with the broader aim of asking when the body can be abstracted away and when it is essential for explaining what the brain computes.

resumo.texto: Animals act on the world through a physical body and continually adjust behavior in response to the sensory feedback their actions produce. This closed loop between brain, body, and environment is central to motor control, but its role in other neural computations remains less clear. This review focuses on embodied computation: how the physical body shapes neural activity and behavior across functions ranging from motor control to cognitive processes. We examine the impact of embodiment in several domains, including compositional reuse, intrinsic motivation, metabolic costs, and connectome-constrained computation, with the broader aim of asking when the body can be abstracted away and when it is essential for explaining what the brain computes.

artigos.titulo: The Burden of Occult Cerebrovascular Disease in CKD: A Scoping Review
artigos.autores: Vasaghi-Gharamaleki M, Jazayeri SB, Pillai A et al.
artigos.destaque: Occult cerebrovascular abnormalities are frequently reported across diverse CKD populations, particularly among patients with advanced kidney disease. Variation in the prevalence of abnormalities may reflect differences in CKD severity, participant characteristics, neuroimaging protocols, and outcome definitions. These findings highlight the need for standardized neuroimaging approaches and prospective studies to better characterize the clinical implications of OCCD in CKD.

resumo.texto: Occult cerebrovascular diseases (OCCD) including extracranial and intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ECAD and ICAD) and cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) are asymptomatic cerebrovascular abnormalities associated with future risk of stroke and dementia. Although chronic kidney disease (CKD) is strongly associated with adverse brain health outcomes, the breadth of evidence regarding OCCD in people with CKD has not been comprehensively characterized. This scoping review summarizes the available literature on OCCD among adults with CKD without clinically overt cerebrovascular disease.
PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for studies published between January 2000 and July 2025.
Peer-reviewed studies reporting the frequency or characteristics of OCCD manifestations in adults with CKD without a known history of stroke or transient ischemic attack.

Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on study characteristics, CKD definitions, neuroimaging modalities, and reported OCCD findings. Methodological quality was assessed using a modified Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.

Forty-six studies comprising 5,153 participants with CKD were included. Study populations varied substantially with respect to CKD stage, dialysis status, study design, and imaging methodology. Two studies evaluating ICAD reported moderate-to-severe intracranial stenosis in approximately one-quarter of participants with CKD. Across studies evaluating ECAD, the frequency of significant extracranial carotid stenosis ranged from approximately 3% in patients with non-dialysis-dependent CKD to 28% among patients receiving dialysis. Thirty-eight studies evaluated manifestations of CSVD, including cerebral microbleeds, silent cerebral infarctions, white matter hyperintensities, and enlarged perivascular spaces. Several studies suggested a greater burden of CSVD manifestations among patients with advanced CKD or dialysis dependence. Reported frequencies varied considerably across studies.
Considerable heterogeneity in study populations, CKD definitions, imaging protocols, and outcome ascertainment methods limited direct comparison across studies.

Occult cerebrovascular abnormalities are frequently reported across diverse CKD populations, particularly among patients with advanced kidney disease. Variation in the prevalence of abnormalities may reflect differences in CKD severity, participant characteristics, neuroimaging protocols, and outcome definitions. These findings highlight the need for standardized neuroimaging approaches and prospective studies to better characterize the clinical implications of OCCD in CKD.

artigos.titulo: Deep learning-based estimation of multi-tracer PET phenotypes from structural MRI for A/T/N-related analysis and progression prediction in Alzheimer's disease
artigos.autores: Xie W, Pan X, Zhan Y et al.
artigos.destaque: In OASIS, generated PET-derived features improved CDR stratification and future cognitive decline prediction, increasing AUCs from 0.662 to 0.739 and from 0.569 to 0.643. These findings suggest that the method can provide PET-derived phenotypes related to A/T/N analysis from structural MRI when PET is unavailable, but should not be interpreted as a replacement for molecular PET assessment.

resumo.texto: Early identification and staging of Alzheimer's disease (AD) require integrated assessment of amyloid deposition, tau pathology, and neurodegeneration. PET provides spatially resolved in vivo imaging biomarkers, but its routine use is constrained by cost, tracer availability, and radiation exposure, limiting access to complete A/T/N imaging profiles. We propose a conditional flow matching-based framework that estimates SUV-space PET-derived phenotypes related to 18F-FDG, 18F-florbetapir and 18F-flortaucipir from a single T1-weighted MRI scan. To address limitations in SUV-level quantitative fidelity, single-tracer applicability, and external generalization, the framework combines a PET prior network with a time-conditioned velocity network and uses multi-constraint losses to preserve SUV accuracy, regional uptake consistency, and anatomical boundaries. The model was developed using 1,978 paired ADNI MRI-PET records from 991 participants and evaluated in a predefined ADNI test set and an independent hospital PET/MR cohort of 514 participants. In ADNI, voxel-level MAEs were 0.012, 0.034, and 0.021 SUV, with representative ROI Pearson correlations of 0.978, 0.842, and 0.781. In the hospital cohort, corresponding MAEs were 0.014, 0.037, and 0.024 SUV, with ROI correlations of 0.952, 0.803, and 0.834. In OASIS, generated PET-derived features improved CDR stratification and future cognitive decline prediction, increasing AUCs from 0.662 to 0.739 and from 0.569 to 0.643. These findings suggest that the method can provide PET-derived phenotypes related to A/T/N analysis from structural MRI when PET is unavailable, but should not be interpreted as a replacement for molecular PET assessment.

artigos.titulo: The blood-brain barrier imports diverse neuroprotective proteins through pathways impaired early in Alzheimer's disease models
artigos.autores: Zhou H, Maynard JC, Pennacchio AJ et al.
artigos.destaque: Hepatic APOA1 overexpression restores APOA1 in the 5xFAD brain, rescuing astrocytic, synaptic, and behavioral deficits. These findings recast the BBB as a selective interface that recruits neuroprotective circulatory proteins for brain health.

resumo.texto: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) has been defined primarily by what it excludes, yet the scale and function of physiological blood-to-brain protein transport remain largely unknown. Using bioorthogonal proteomics, we find that the healthy BBB samples 191 plasma proteins and permits 92 into the brain parenchyma. Enriched for carrier and metabolic functions, these proteins home to distinct brain cell types, such as apolipoprotein A1 (APOA1) to astrocytes and alpha-1 antitrypsin (SERPINA1) to microglia. This cell-type tropism relies on a BBB-parenchyma receptor hand-off: APOA1 crosses the BBB via SR-B1 and engages astrocytic ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1), a key Alzheimer's risk gene, driving cholesterol efflux that supports synapse integrity. Unlike LPS-induced nonspecific leakage, early-stage 5xFAD mice show selective BBB transport remodeling, with reduced APOA1 and increased SERPINA1 uptake. Hepatic APOA1 overexpression restores APOA1 in the 5xFAD brain, rescuing astrocytic, synaptic, and behavioral deficits. These findings recast the BBB as a selective interface that recruits neuroprotective circulatory proteins for brain health.

artigos.titulo: Rhodotorula mucilaginosa DM2025 ameliorates obesity through cholesterol binding and the gut mycobiome-BAT PPARγ/UCP1 axis
artigos.autores: Jing Y, Xiang Y, Zafir OC et al.
artigos.destaque: Additionally, physical cholesterol binding to the yeast cell surface provides a complementary cholesterol‑reduction mechanism. Thus, R. mucilaginosa DM2025 represents a promising live probiotic candidate for obesity intervention.

resumo.texto: Obesity is a major global health challenge, necessitating safe and effective therapies. Although probiotics are promising for obesity management, research has focused on bacteria, leaving non-Saccharomyces yeasts underexplored. Here, we investigated the anti‑obesity mechanisms of Rhodotorula mucilaginosa DM2025, isolated from the healthy murine gut. To test whether benefits depend on viable cells, high‑fat diet‑fed mice received either live yeast or its cell‑free supernatant, followed by integrated physiological, genomic, and metabolomic analyzes. Live yeast, but not supernatant, significantly reduced body weight gain, improved serum lipids, and was associated with activation of brown adipose tissue thermogenesis (upregulated PPARγ, PGC1α, UCP1). Though the supernatant lowered total cholesterol, it failed to affect weight or thermogenic genes, indicating cholesterol‑lowering and weight reduction are distinct processes. Live cells were enriched in propionate, indole, and carotenoid‑related metabolites, with genomic support for their biosynthesis. Live yeast reshaped the gut mycobiome, promoting Basidiomycota/Rhodotorula dominance; this fungal restructuring was absent in HFD controls. These findings suggest that R. mucilaginosa DM2025 anti‑obesity efficacy relies on the continuous metabolic activity of live cells, producing thermogenesis‑associated metabolites that may contribute to BAT activation. Additionally, physical cholesterol binding to the yeast cell surface provides a complementary cholesterol‑reduction mechanism. Thus, R. mucilaginosa DM2025 represents a promising live probiotic candidate for obesity intervention.

artigos.titulo: Nutrition Care Strategies at the Intersection of Menopause and Obesity Pharmacotherapy
artigos.autores: Christensen S, Hurtado Andrade MD, Sampson-Paine K et al.
artigos.destaque: Clinical strategies to mitigate these risks, including protein optimization, micronutrient monitoring, menopausal hormone therapy (osteoporosis/musculoskeletal health), and multidisciplinary care, are discussed alongside research priorities to inform targeted nutrition frameworks. Addressing these gaps is essential to ensure safe, effective, and sustainable obesity management for women in midlife and beyond.

resumo.texto: The premenopause to menopause transition, known as perimenopause, is a critical period of metabolic vulnerability, characterized by hormonal changes, shifts in body composition, and increased cardiometabolic risk. Concurrently, incretin mimetic pharmacotherapies have emerged as highly effective treatments for obesity, achieving weight reductions that are approximating those previously observed only after bariatric surgery. While these agents confer substantial benefits, their mechanisms-appetite suppression, delayed gastric emptying, and enhanced satiety-introduce nutritional risks that intersect with pre-existing vulnerabilities of women experiencing this transition. Reduced energy intake and inadequate micronutrient intake, combined with estrogen deficiency, heighten the risk for osteoporosis and sarcopenic obesity. Likewise, gastrointestinal adverse events further compromise dietary quality and hydration, while aging physiology amplifies susceptibility to malnutrition. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on nutritional risks during perimenopause in the context of incretin mimetic pharmacotherapy, highlighting overlapping pathways that influence musculoskeletal health, metabolic resilience, and quality of life. Clinical strategies to mitigate these risks, including protein optimization, micronutrient monitoring, menopausal hormone therapy (osteoporosis/musculoskeletal health), and multidisciplinary care, are discussed alongside research priorities to inform targeted nutrition frameworks. Addressing these gaps is essential to ensure safe, effective, and sustainable obesity management for women in midlife and beyond.

artigos.titulo: Paraspinal Muscle Quality Modifies Frailty-Related Functional Recovery After Lumbar Instrumented Fusion
artigos.autores: Eryilmaz F
artigos.destaque: Paraspinal muscle quality modified frailty-related recovery following lumbar instrumented fusion. Combined assessment of frailty and muscle quality may be useful for preoperative risk assessment.

resumo.texto: Frailty and paraspinal muscle degeneration are associated with adverse outcomes after lumbar fusion surgery. However, whether paraspinal muscle quality modifies frailty-related functional recovery remains unclear. This study evaluated the interaction between frailty and multifidus fatty infiltration (MFI) in predicting functional recovery following lumbar instrumented fusion.

A retrospective analysis was performed in 124 patients who underwent lumbar instrumented fusion for degenerative lumbar spine disorders between January 2020 and December 2024. Frailty was assessed using the 11-item Modified Frailty Index, and paraspinal muscle quality was quantified using MFI on preoperative magnetic resonance imaging. Functional recovery was defined as improvement in Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) score at 6 months. Multivariable linear regression, including a Frailty × MFI interaction term, was used to evaluate associations with recovery.

Higher MFI was associated with less ODI improvement. In multivariable analysis, frailty (β = -0.31, p < 0.001), MFI (β = -0.27, p = 0.001), and age (β = -0.16, p = 0.014) were independently associated with poorer functional recovery. A significant Frailty × MFI interaction was observed (β = -0.23, p = 0.003), indicating that the adverse association between frailty and recovery was stronger with greater MFI. ODI improvement ranged from 29 ± 10 points in non-frail patients with preserved muscle quality to 11 ± 7 points in frail patients with poor muscle quality.
Paraspinal muscle quality modified frailty-related recovery following lumbar instrumented fusion. Combined assessment of frailty and muscle quality may be useful for preoperative risk assessment.

artigos.titulo: Associations between sarcopenic obesity subtypes, cognitive function and neurodegenerative diseases risk in middle-aged and older adults
artigos.autores: Yu D, Liu T, Qian J et al.
artigos.destaque: Distinct SO subtypes were associated with different cognitive profiles. Recognizing the CS-MSI subtype, which conventional obesity- and metabolism-based screening would miss, may improve early identification of middle-aged and older adults at risk, pending validation in independent cohorts.

resumo.texto: This study aimed to identify subtypes of sarcopenic obesity (SO) in middle-aged and older adults and examine their associations with cognitive function and the risk of incident neurodegenerative diseases (NDs), to inform subtype-specific screening.

We utilized data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), with baseline in 2011 and follow-up through 2020, incorporating 1,010 middle-aged and older adults with SO. Latent class analysis (LCA) was used to identify SO subtypes. Cross-sectional associations of subtypes and cognitive function were examined using linear regression models, and Cox proportional hazards models were applied to evaluate association with incident NDs.

Three SO subtypes were identified: Covert sarcopenia-muscle strength imbalance (CS-MSI), Low metabolic burden-muscle maintenance (LMB-MM), and High metabolic burden-inflammation driven (HMB-ID). Compared with LMB-MM, the CS-MSI subtype had lower performance across multiple cognitive domains, whereas the HMB-ID subtype showed a comparatively prominent decrement in orientation (β = -1.12, 95% CI: -1.66 to -0.58). Longitudinally, the CS-MSI subtype showed a directionally higher but non-significant hazard of incident NDs.

Distinct SO subtypes were associated with different cognitive profiles. Recognizing the CS-MSI subtype, which conventional obesity- and metabolism-based screening would miss, may improve early identification of middle-aged and older adults at risk, pending validation in independent cohorts.

artigos.titulo: Low Muscle Mechanical Power, Worse Clinical Outcomes? A Cohort of Patients on Hemodialysis
artigos.autores: Disessa HS, Duarte MP, Roure JG et al.
artigos.destaque: In patients on hemodialysis, low muscle mechanical power was strongly associated with a greater mortality risk, particularly among older patients. These findings position low muscle mechanical power as a clinically and potentially relevant aging-related condition.

resumo.texto: In older adults, low muscle mechanical power is an independent predictor of adverse clinical outcomes. In patients with chronic kidney disease, this has not yet been explored. In this study, we hypothesized that low muscle mechanical power is independently associated with increased risks of all-cause mortality and hospitalization in patients on hemodialysis.

This study is a secondary analysis of the SARC-HD cohort, which enrolled patients from 19 dialysis centers across Brazil.
