Among 1406 adults (mean age 54.6 ± 11.8 years; 76.8% female), those with uncontrolled MetS (n = 634) had significantly worse global PSQI, sleep latency, and sleep disturbance scores compared with adults without MetS (n = 483) (P < .05). Sleep outcomes did not differ between adults with controlled MetS (n = 289) and those without MetS (P > .05).

Poorly controlled MetS was associated with poorer sleep quality, whereas clinically controlled MetS was not. Future research is needed to determine if effective clinical management of MetS may confer benefits for sleep health in rural populations.

artigos.titulo: Weight management in people with HIV
artigos.autores: Manne-Goehler J, Magodoro I, Ramírez BC et al.
artigos.destaque: Finally, bariatric surgical interventions are suggested to be safe and efficacious for those with chronic HIV infection and comorbid obesity. This Series paper identifies a range of key evidence gaps and research priorities for obesity management in people with HIV, including a lack of trials of GLP-1 therapies in people with HIV powered to key clinical outcomes, such as major adverse cardiovascular events and body composition endpoints, implementation science to define models of care, and research on the heterogeneities in clinical outcomes of obesity treatment by sex.

resumo.texto: Excess weight gain in people with HIV is now recognised as a common risk associated with the use of guideline-recommended antiretroviral therapy, such that nearly 50% of people with HIV are living with comorbid obesity. Weight gain and clinical obesity exacerbate cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic health complications in this population and chronic weight management strategies that reduce these risks are now an urgent priority. Behavioural interventions can be offered to improve diet and increase physical activity, including increasing protein intake and promoting regular physical activity. Additionally, there is a growing body of evidence to support the use of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapies in people with HIV, along with a historical literature showing the efficacy of tesamorelin; however, there are sparse data to direct the use of other approved obesity management medicines specific to this population. Finally, bariatric surgical interventions are suggested to be safe and efficacious for those with chronic HIV infection and comorbid obesity. This Series paper identifies a range of key evidence gaps and research priorities for obesity management in people with HIV, including a lack of trials of GLP-1 therapies in people with HIV powered to key clinical outcomes, such as major adverse cardiovascular events and body composition endpoints, implementation science to define models of care, and research on the heterogeneities in clinical outcomes of obesity treatment by sex.

artigos.titulo: Motivation in adolescents and caretakers undergoing a weight management program - longitudinal data from the cluster-randomized, motivation-focused STARKIDS trial
artigos.autores: Herschbach A, Junne F, Erschens R et al.
artigos.destaque: This motivation-focused weight management program produced motivational gains at the Maintenance stage, supporting sustained behavioral change. Baseline obesity-related quality of life predicted motivational change, suggesting its value as a clinical marker for tailoring interventional approaches. Future research should explore distinct motivational trajectories to inform more individualized pediatric weight management strategies.

resumo.texto: Motivation towards behavior change is an important determinant of long-term weight management. Previous research demonstrates that children's and adolescents' motivation can be increased through participation in weight management programs. However, little is known about motivational changes in caretakers of children and adolescents with overweight and obesity despite their recognized role as "agents of change" in pediatric weight management. The study aims to compare motivational changes in caretakers and adolescents between a group receiving a motivation-focused weight management program and a control group. Furthermore, predictors for motivational changes are unknown.

This study is a secondary analysis of the cluster-randomized STARKIDS trial. The intervention group received an 18-month motivation-focused weight management program, the control group received optimized treatment-as-usual. Motivation was assessed based on Transtheoretical Model, using the University of Rhode Island Change Assessment-Short, as well as the related parent-perspective version. Each of these instruments contains four subscales: Precontemplation, Contemplation, Action, and Maintenance. Linear mixed models with multiply imputed data were employed to evaluate changes within the subscales between pre- to post-intervention measurements and to compare these changes between the intervention and control group. A multiple linear regression was subsequently used to identify predictors of motivational change.

Caretakers in the intervention group showed significantly greater changes on Maintenance subscale compared to caretakers in the control group at both T0-T1 and T0-T2 and trends for these changes on Action subscale. No group differences were found in adolescents. Among caregivers in the intervention group, multiple regression analysis for T0-T1 changes on Action subscale identified parent-reported adolescents' obesity-related quality of life as significant negative predictor for an increase on Action stage.

This motivation-focused weight management program produced motivational gains at the Maintenance stage, supporting sustained behavioral change. Baseline obesity-related quality of life predicted motivational change, suggesting its value as a clinical marker for tailoring interventional approaches. Future research should explore distinct motivational trajectories to inform more individualized pediatric weight management strategies.
Preregistered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS) DRKS000228 13 (acknowledged primary register of the World Health Organization) on 27 November 2020 (Universal Trial Number U111112549536).

artigos.titulo: Effects of exercise interventions on leptin and ghrelin levels in middle-aged and older adults with overweight or obesity: a systematic review and meta-analysis
artigos.autores: Guo Z, Guo W, Gu Y et al.
artigos.destaque: Exercise interventions were associated with reduced leptin levels and increased ghrelin levels in middle-aged and older adults with overweight or obesity. The leptin finding appeared relatively consistent, whereas the ghrelin finding should be interpreted cautiously because of fewer comparisons and substantial heterogeneity. Subgroup findings remain exploratory and should not be used to define an optimal exercise prescription. Further randomized controlled trials with more standardized exercise protocols, clearer dietary control, and consistent hormone measurement are needed to clarify the clinical relevance of these changes.

resumo.texto: Overweight and obesity are common among middle-aged and older adults, and obesity is a chronic, multifactorial disease that, particularly when accompanied by central adiposity or metabolic abnormalities, is associated with increased cardiometabolic, cancer-related, musculoskeletal, and functional risks. Leptin and ghrelin are key hormones involved in energy balance regulation and may be dysregulated in obesity, but evidence regarding the effects of exercise interventions on leptin and ghrelin levels in middle-aged and older adults with overweight or obesity remains inconsistent. This review aimed to evaluate the effects of exercise interventions on leptin and ghrelin levels in this population.

PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and CNKI were searched from database inception to 5 July 2026. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials that enrolled middle-aged or older adults with overweight or obesity and reported leptin or ghrelin levels before and after an exercise intervention. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were synthesized using Review Manager 5.4 and Stata 15. Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using I 2; a fixed-effect model was used when I 2 < 50%, and a random-effects model when I 2 ≥ 50%. Subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and publication-bias assessments were conducted.

Twenty-one randomized controlled trials were included. Exercise interventions were associated with significantly lower leptin levels than control conditions based on 18 comparisons (SMD = -0.32, 95% CI [-0.47 to -0.18], P < 0.0001), with low between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 22%). Exercise interventions were also associated with significantly higher ghrelin levels based on nine comparisons (SMD = 0.45, 95% CI [0.11-0.79], P = 0.01), although heterogeneity was substantial (I 2 = 74%). Subgroup analyses suggested that exercise-related characteristics may partly contribute to variability in leptin and ghrelin responses, but these findings were exploratory. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses supported the stability of the main estimates. For leptin, Egger's test suggested possible funnel-plot asymmetry, but trim-and-fill analysis did not impute any missing comparison and the pooled estimate remained unchanged.

Exercise interventions were associated with reduced leptin levels and increased ghrelin levels in middle-aged and older adults with overweight or obesity. The leptin finding appeared relatively consistent, whereas the ghrelin finding should be interpreted cautiously because of fewer comparisons and substantial heterogeneity. Subgroup findings remain exploratory and should not be used to define an optimal exercise prescription. Further randomized controlled trials with more standardized exercise protocols, clearer dietary control, and consistent hormone measurement are needed to clarify the clinical relevance of these changes.

artigos.titulo: Phenotypic Clustering as a Tool for Uncovering Hidden Risk Profiles in End-stage Liver Disease: An Exploratory Analysis of Sarcopenia and 1-Year Mortality
artigos.autores: Dhami-Shah H, Pranesh G, Mogre D et al.
artigos.destaque: Exploratory clustering analysis suggests that phenotypic variation in muscle composition exists among ESLD patients undergoing liver transplantation, with differential associations with short-term mortality. Muscle quality, as reflected by PMDI, may provide additional prognostic information beyond conventional measures of disease severity. These findings are hypothesis generating and require validation in larger, prospective studies before clinical application.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia is associated with adverse outcomes in patients with end-stage liver disease (ESLD), but the relative contribution of muscle quantity versus muscle quality to posttransplant outcomes remains incompletely understood. Radiological indices such as psoas muscle area index (PMAI), transverse psoas muscle thickness index (TPMTI), and psoas muscle density index (PMDI) provide objective measures of muscle mass and myosteatosis. This study aimed to explore phenotypic patterns in ESLD patients using clinical and radiological parameters and examine their association with 1-yr posttransplant mortality.

In this retrospective study, 86 adult ESLD patients who underwent liver transplantation were analyzed. Clinical and radiological variables (age, PMAI, TPMTI, PMDI, MELD, Child-Turcotte-Pugh score, and body mass index) were normalized and subjected to hierarchical and k-means clustering to identify phenotypic groups. One-year posttransplant mortality rates were compared across clusters. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess the discriminative ability of PMDI.

Five phenotypic clusters were identified, demonstrating heterogeneity in muscle quantity, muscle quality, and disease severity. A cluster characterized by relatively preserved muscle mass but reduced muscle density exhibited the highest 1-yr mortality (41.7%), whereas a cluster with preserved muscle density showed no mortality although these data were limited by a small sample size. Intermediate clusters demonstrated mortality rates ranging from 15.8% to 17.9%. PMDI showed modest discriminative ability for 1-yr mortality (area under the curve [AUC] 0.662), comparable to MELD (AUC 0.659).

Exploratory clustering analysis suggests that phenotypic variation in muscle composition exists among ESLD patients undergoing liver transplantation, with differential associations with short-term mortality. Muscle quality, as reflected by PMDI, may provide additional prognostic information beyond conventional measures of disease severity. These findings are hypothesis generating and require validation in larger, prospective studies before clinical application.

artigos.titulo: Circulating Tsukushi Predicts Incident Sarcopenia and Functional Decline in Older Adults: A Prospective Cohort Study
artigos.autores: He MQ, Dai XN, Zhang M et al.
artigos.destaque: Lower circulating TSK levels are associated with a higher risk of incident sarcopenia in older adults, particularly subsequent muscle-related functional decline. TSK may be a candidate biomarker for early sarcopenia risk stratification and may reflect systemic metabolic processes relevant to muscle health.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia is a major age-related condition associated with functional decline, disability and mortality in older adults, yet reliable circulating biomarkers for early risk stratification remain limited. Tsukushi (TSK), a secreted hepatokine involved in systemic metabolic regulation, has recently been implicated in skeletal muscle homeostasis. However, prospective clinical evidence linking circulating TSK to sarcopenia development is lacking. We therefore investigated the association between serum TSK levels and incident sarcopenia in a community-based cohort of older adults.

A total of 1370 community-dwelling individuals aged ≥ 65 years were followed for 4 years. Baseline serum TSK levels were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the association between TSK and incident sarcopenia after adjustment for confounding factors. Restricted cubic spline analyses were applied to explore dose-response relationships, and predictive performance was evaluated using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.

Lower baseline TSK levels were associated with a higher cumulative incidence of sarcopenia. In multivariable analyses, higher TSK levels were associated with a lower risk of incident sarcopenia (hazard ratio per SD increase = 0.64, 95% CI = 0.53-0.76, p < 0.001). Dose-response analyses demonstrated a non-linear association with overall sarcopenia risk, whereas associations with low muscle strength and low physical performance were more nearly linear. The association appeared more evident in women than in men. TSK alone showed moderate discrimination for incident sarcopenia (AUC = 0.700), while a combined clinical model improved discrimination (AUC = 0.808 at 4 years).

Lower circulating TSK levels are associated with a higher risk of incident sarcopenia in older adults, particularly subsequent muscle-related functional decline. TSK may be a candidate biomarker for early sarcopenia risk stratification and may reflect systemic metabolic processes relevant to muscle health.

artigos.titulo: Sleep characteristics and sarcopenia in patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis: nonlinear associations and a potential adiposity-related pathway
artigos.autores: Sun X, Lin X, Deng J et al.
artigos.destaque: Albumin interacts with PBF, yet does not significantly modify the overall indirect pathway. Due to the cross-sectional design, findings are hypothesis-generating and not causal.

resumo.texto: Sleep disturbances are common in patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD), yet the pathways linking sleep characteristics to sarcopenia remain poorly understood. We examined associations of sleep duration and quality with sarcopenia and whether these associations included an indirect component involving percent body fat (PBF), with albumin and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) as potential modifiers. This cross-sectional study included 562 patients receiving PD. Sleep was assessed by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Sarcopenia was defined by 2025 Asian Working Group criteria; PBF was assessed by bioelectrical impedance. Restricted cubic splines, mediation/moderated mediation analyses, and sensitivity tests (E-values) were used. Sleep duration showed a U-shaped association with sarcopenia (p-nonlinear < 0.001), with the lowest estimated odds at approximately 7.29 h/night. PSQI score was positively associated with sarcopenia (OR = 1.12 per one-point increase). An indirect association involving PBF was observed for PSQI (ACME = 0.002, p = 0.031) and short sleep (ACME = 0.026, p = 0.030), but not for long sleep. Albumin interacted with PBF in the sarcopenia model for the PSQI (p = 0.042) and short-sleep (p = 0.031) pathways, but the indices of moderated mediation were not statistically significant. NLR showed no evidence of interaction. Mediation sensitivity analysis suggested that the observed indirect associations were not readily explained by modest residual confounding. Sleep duration and quality are associated with sarcopenia in PD patients. An indirect association involving PBF was observed for poorer sleep quality and short sleep, but not for long sleep. Albumin interacts with PBF, yet does not significantly modify the overall indirect pathway. Due to the cross-sectional design, findings are hypothesis-generating and not causal.

artigos.titulo: Kidney dysfunction under cardiometabolic stress promotes calorie-intake-independent wasting and frailty-like muscle phenotypes
artigos.autores: Kojima M, Sato Y, Hirayama A et al.
artigos.destaque: Cornstarch-based nutritional modulation improved exercise capacity, muscle mass, and serum albumin, highlighting slow-release carbohydrate modulation as a potential therapeutic entry point. These findings support a model in which kidney dysfunction promotes wasting by limiting systemic metabolic reserve and skeletal muscle metabolic flexibility.

resumo.texto: Although age-related sarcopenia and frailty are linked to impaired metabolic flexibility and disrupted energy homeostasis, whether this framework explains chronic kidney disease (CKD)-related wasting remains unclear. We show that superimposed nephron loss redirects cardiometabolic stress from obesity and glucose intolerance toward calorie-intake-independent wasting with sarcopenic and physical frailty features. This switch was accompanied by impaired skeletal muscle glucose-utilization programs, a blunted glycemic response to gluconeogenic substrates, and altered hepatic-renal gluconeogenic programs. Integrated omics revealed suppressed glucose programs, impaired fatty acid utilization-related compensation, and amino acid catabolic signatures in skeletal muscle. Similar features occurred with aging plus nephron loss and in older human CKD kidneys with reduced renal PCK1 expression. Cornstarch-based nutritional modulation improved exercise capacity, muscle mass, and serum albumin, highlighting slow-release carbohydrate modulation as a potential therapeutic entry point. These findings support a model in which kidney dysfunction promotes wasting by limiting systemic metabolic reserve and skeletal muscle metabolic flexibility.

artigos.titulo: Weaker or Just Lighter? Monitoring Strength and Function, Not Just Lean Mass, During GLP-1 Weight Loss
artigos.autores: O'Leary RT
artigos.destaque: Functional discordance is a confirmed within-person decline in strength or physical performance beyond measurement error without an adverse lean-mass signal (exploratory default: lean loss beyond the scan's least significant change and above 40% of weight lost). For higher-risk patients (older adults; low strength, frailty or rapid weight loss), the review proposes grip strength, five-times chair-stand time and usual gait speed, with a timed stair climb where feasible, before treatment, at 3, 6 and 12 months and around dose changes, with declines confirmed by repeat testing, assistance recorded and stepwise clinical review. The schedule is pragmatic and not validated. If lean-mass change identifies the patients whose function declines, functional monitoring may add little; if discordance is common, lean mass is an inadequate surrogate.

resumo.texto: Body-composition studies of GLP-1-based therapy report how much of the weight lost is lean mass, not whether the patient is getting weaker. This review asks how to monitor strength and function during treatment.
Narrative review of October 2026 PubMed searches pairing incretin drugs with strength, performance, walking and measurement-error terms, plus hand-checked reference lists.

In older adults, strength declines about three times faster than lean mass and predicts mortality where lean mass does not. On GLP-1-based therapy, randomized trials show longer walks and better reported function, while some cohorts of older adults show falling strength and gait speed; a 2026 review of 35 body-composition trials found none that measured objective physical function. Recent recommendations advise assessing strength and function, but none identified here judges change against measurement error.

Functional discordance is a confirmed within-person decline in strength or physical performance beyond measurement error without an adverse lean-mass signal (exploratory default: lean loss beyond the scan's least significant change and above 40% of weight lost). For higher-risk patients (older adults; low strength, frailty or rapid weight loss), the review proposes grip strength, five-times chair-stand time and usual gait speed, with a timed stair climb where feasible, before treatment, at 3, 6 and 12 months and around dose changes, with declines confirmed by repeat testing, assistance recorded and stepwise clinical review. The schedule is pragmatic and not validated. If lean-mass change identifies the patients whose function declines, functional monitoring may add little; if discordance is common, lean mass is an inadequate surrogate.

artigos.titulo: Body composition in octogenarians with chronic kidney disease. Role of gender
artigos.autores: Cigarrán Guldris S, Sanjurjo Amado A, Rios Guillermo J et al.
artigos.destaque: These findings highlight a marked sexual dimorphism in body composition and functional status among octogenarians with CKD, with important clinical implications for risk stratification and individualized management in this population.

resumo.texto: The population with chronic kidney disease (CKD) is undergoing marked ageing, and octogenarian patients represent a growing group with distinctive clinical and functional characteristics. In this context, alterations in fluid status and body composition (BC) limit the usefulness of body mass index, necessitating a more accurate assessment with bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA). The aim of this study was to evaluate gender-related differences in body composition in octogenarian patients with CKD in a prospective observational cohort study with a 14-year longitudinal follow-up of clinical events.

A total of 724 patients were included (46.4% women), with a mean age of 84.7 years and a mean estimated glomerular filtration rate of 36.6 ml/min/1.73 m2. Vectorial tetrapolar BIA was used to analyse body composition parameters, hydration status, and bioelectrical variables, while muscle strength was assessed by handgrip dynamometry. In addition, risk of progression to kidney replacement therapy, fracture risk, cardiovascular risk, and age-adjusted comorbidity were evaluated.

The results revealed clinically relevant gender differences. Women exhibited lower comorbidity and a lower risk of initiating kidney replacement therapy, but a significantly higher risk of osteoporotic and hip fractures. From a BC perspective, women showed higher adiposity and a greater proportion of ECW, together with lower muscle mass, lower TBW and ICW, and reduced muscle strength. Men presented greater muscle mass and strength but a higher prevalence of dynapenia. Overall sarcopenia was infrequent in the cohort.

These findings highlight a marked sexual dimorphism in body composition and functional status among octogenarians with CKD, with important clinical implications for risk stratification and individualized management in this population.

artigos.titulo: The impact of the gut microbiome on skeletal muscle in health and disease
artigos.autores: Bongers KS
artigos.destaque: Several clinical trials of microbiome-focused therapies have also been conducted, with suggestion of benefits as well as potential harms. Taken together, the gut microbiome plays a key role in modulating skeletal muscle physiology, and may serve as the basis for novel therapeutics targeting muscle disease.

resumo.texto: The gut microbiome, the community of bacteria residing the lower gastrointestinal tract, is increasingly recognized as an important influence on skeletal muscle physiology, with critical implications for muscle disorders such as sarcopenia and muscular dystrophy. Researchers have uncovered multiple microbiome-derived metabolites that alter skeletal muscle protein synthesis, mitochondrial biogenesis, protein degradation, and glucose transport. Moreover, the microbiome mediates systemic cytokine release of interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor alpha, which can drive muscle loss. These studies have led to the identification of gut bacterial species (such as Veillonella atypica and Roseburia inulinivorans) that improve muscle endurance and strength when administered as probiotics in animal models. Several clinical trials of microbiome-focused therapies have also been conducted, with suggestion of benefits as well as potential harms. Taken together, the gut microbiome plays a key role in modulating skeletal muscle physiology, and may serve as the basis for novel therapeutics targeting muscle disease.

artigos.titulo: Evolution and impact of sarcopenia and myosteatosis in the context of liver transplantation
artigos.autores: Villeret F, Herreros V, Cayot B et al.
artigos.destaque: Sarcopenia and myosteatosis are common in cirrhotic patients listed for LT, persist after LT, and have a major and independent impact on overall mortality.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia and myosteatosis have a well-documented adverse impact on survival in liver cirrhosis patients. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and risk factors associated with muscle impairment before liver transplantation (LT), their evolution after LT, and to determine their prognostic value.

All cirrhotic patients listed for LT at our center between 2006 and 2010 were included. Sarcopenia and myosteatosis were assessed on transverse L3 CT images at LT listing and at 12 (M12), 60, 120, and 180 months after LT.

The study population consisted of 198 patients, 75.3% of whom were men, and 149 underwent LT. At LT listing, sarcopenia was diagnosed in 45.5% of patients and myosteatosis in 36.5% and 20.1% had both sarcopenia and myosteatosis. One year after LT, 56.1% of patients had persistent sarcopenia and 15.3% had de novo sarcopenia. Sarcopenia significantly improved at M12 post-LT (p=0.034). Post-LT patient survival was 89.2%, 76.3%, and 59.3% at 1, 5, and 10 years respectively. In multivariate analysis, at LT listing, MELD score ≥ 25 (HR: 2.549; p=0.001), sarcopenia (HR: 1.749; p=0.004) and myosteatosis (HR: 1.630; p=0.012) were found to be independent risk factors for overall mortality. The effects of sarcopenia and myosteatosis were additive: overall survival was significantly reduced in patients with both sarcopenia and myosteatosis compared to patients with isolated sarcopenia/myosteatosis (p=0.001).
Sarcopenia and myosteatosis are common in cirrhotic patients listed for LT, persist after LT, and have a major and independent impact on overall mortality.

artigos.titulo: Factors associated with skeletal muscle mass in patients with Behçet's disease: An exploratory study
artigos.autores: Hayashi T, Tsutsui H, Tomiyama N et al.
artigos.destaque: Low skeletal muscle mass is common in BD ambulatory outpatients and is associated with muscle-, nutrition-, and body composition-related measures. However, clear associations with disease activity and current systemic glucocorticoid use were not observed.

resumo.texto: To investigate the prevalence of low skeletal muscle mass and factors associated with skeletal muscle mass index (SMI) in Japanese outpatients with Behçet's disease (BD), while assessing sarcopenia according to the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia 2025 criteria.

This cross-sectional study included ambulatory outpatients with BD aged ≥40 years. SMI was measured using multifrequency bioelectrical impedance analysis. Sarcopenia was defined as low SMI with low handgrip strength. Clinical characteristics, physical functions, nutrition- and body composition-related measures, rectus femoris ultrasonography, and laboratory parameters were compared between the low- and normal-SMI groups. Associations with SMI were examined using age- and sex-adjusted and domain-specific multivariable linear regression models.

Among 48 patients (mean age: 65.4±11.8 years; 45.8% women), 52.1% had Low SMI, and 10.6% of 47 participants with available SMI and handgrip strength data had sarcopenia. In multivariable analyses, higher SMI remained associated with higher body mass index, greater handgrip strength, larger calf circumference, higher phase angle, and greater rectus femoris muscle thickness.

Low skeletal muscle mass is common in BD ambulatory outpatients and is associated with muscle-, nutrition-, and body composition-related measures. However, clear associations with disease activity and current systemic glucocorticoid use were not observed.

artigos.titulo: Molecular targets for the treatment of sarcopenia: a geroscience approach
artigos.autores: Picca A, Calvani R, Coelho-Júnior HJ et al.
artigos.destaque: The future of therapeutics against sarcopenia will likely depend less on identifying anabolic agents than on matching molecular targets to the dominant biological mechanisms limiting muscle function in individual patients. Biomarkers of target engagement, deep phenotyping, and mechanism-informed combination strategies integrating pharmacological, nutritional, and exercise interventions will be essential to improve patient stratification and translate molecular target modulation into meaningful functional benefit.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia is increasingly recognized as a multisystem geroscience condition. The limited efficacy of first-generation anabolic therapies has challenged the paradigm that increasing muscle mass is sufficient to restore physical performance, highlighting the need for therapeutic strategies that address the biological complexity of muscle aging.

This review examines the evolution of molecular targets for sarcopenia, from anabolic pathways to emerging geroscience-based targets. We discuss mechanistic and clinical evidence supporting these approaches, emphasizing the distinction between molecular target engagement and functional efficacy, and examine how biological context, patient stratification, and multicomponent interventions influence therapeutic outcomes. The literature was identified through a comprehensive PubMed search, with emphasis on mechanistic studies, clinical trials, and recent advances in geroscience.

The future of therapeutics against sarcopenia will likely depend less on identifying anabolic agents than on matching molecular targets to the dominant biological mechanisms limiting muscle function in individual patients. Biomarkers of target engagement, deep phenotyping, and mechanism-informed combination strategies integrating pharmacological, nutritional, and exercise interventions will be essential to improve patient stratification and translate molecular target modulation into meaningful functional benefit.

artigos.titulo: Longitudinal Taxonomic and Predicted Functional Gut Microbiome Responses to Tirzepatide and Semaglutide: An Exploratory Secondary Analysis of the OMDOT-1 Randomized Controlled Trial
artigos.autores: Morioka T, Miyaoka D, Nakatani S et al.
artigos.destaque: Tirzepatide and semaglutide were associated with partially distinct taxonomic changes, accompanied by broadly similar predicted functional patterns. These longitudinal findings complement, while remaining distinct from, Week-16 shotgun metagenomic endpoint analyses.

resumo.texto: Glucagon-like peptide-1-based therapies improve metabolic outcomes, but longitudinal gut microbiome dynamics remain poorly characterized. We compared taxonomic and predicted functional microbiome responses to tirzepatide and semaglutide in Type 2 diabetes.

This exploratory secondary analysis included 36 participants from a randomized controlled trial comparing tirzepatide, semaglutide and conventional treatment. Faecal samples were collected at five time points over 16 weeks and analyzed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Genus-level features were screened using MaAsLin2, and candidate genera were further evaluated using longitudinal mixed-effects models. Predicted microbial functions were inferred using PICRUSt2 and analyzed using MaAsLin2. Primary analyses were adjusted for baseline body mass index, with exploratory sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for changes in body weight and haemoglobin A1c.

No significant between-group differences in beta diversity were observed. Alpha diversity increased predominantly in the tirzepatide group, with a significant time-by-treatment interaction versus control. Longitudinal trajectories relative to the control group differed for several genera, including Romboutsia_B, Barnesiella and Ruminococcus_E with both treatments and Vescimonas with tirzepatide (q < 0.05). Across 2106 predicted EC features, longitudinal effects were positively correlated between tirzepatide and semaglutide (67.1% concordant direction; Pearson r = 0.450, p < 0.001). Treatment-versus-control analyses identified predicted functional changes involving energy and carbohydrate metabolism.

Tirzepatide and semaglutide were associated with partially distinct taxonomic changes, accompanied by broadly similar predicted functional patterns. These longitudinal findings complement, while remaining distinct from, Week-16 shotgun metagenomic endpoint analyses.
Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (jRCT), jRCT1051240017.

artigos.titulo: Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Hyperuricemia, Serum Uric Acid and Gout: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
artigos.autores: Lee YH, Song GG
artigos.destaque: Incretin-based therapies were associated with modest reductions in SUA and with a lower incidence of gout flares and hyperuricemia, an effect largely related to weight loss. The clinical relevance of these effects, and the mechanism of any weight-independent component, remains uncertain and warrant confirmation in dedicated trials.

resumo.texto: Hyperuricemia and gout are common but underappreciated comorbidities in Type 2 diabetes (T2D), obesity and chronic kidney disease (CKD). We aimed to quantify the pooled effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonists on serum uric acid (SUA), incident gout and hyperuricemia, and to determine whether these effects vary by drug class and are mediated by weight loss.

We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov through July 2026 for RCTs of ≥ 12 weeks' duration reporting SUA change, gout flares or hyperuricemia incidence. Random-effects meta-analysis, subgroup and sensitivity analyses and meta-regression were performed. Registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261468511).

Eighteen RCTs (77 942 participants) met inclusion criteria. Incretin-based therapy significantly reduced SUA versus control (weighted mean difference [WMD] -0.44 mg/dL, 95% CI -0.52 to -0.35), reduced incident gout flares (hazard ratio [HR] 0.62, 95% CI 0.53-0.72), and reduced hyperuricemia incidence (odds ratio [OR] 0.61, 95% CI 0.53-0.70). Dual GIP/GLP-1 RA (tirzepatide) produced greater SUA lowering than mono GLP-1 RAs (-0.62 vs. -0.35 mg/dL, p = 0.001). Body-weight loss was a significant moderator of SUA reduction (β = -0.041 mg/dL per kg, p < 0.001), explaining 84.7% of between-trial heterogeneity, with a significant weight-independent intercept (-0.19 mg/dL, p < 0.001). The SUA reduction was robust in all sensitivity analyses, including restriction to placebo-controlled trials. GRADE certainty was high for SUA and moderate for gout flares (owing to small-study effects) and hyperuricemia incidence.

Incretin-based therapies were associated with modest reductions in SUA and with a lower incidence of gout flares and hyperuricemia, an effect largely related to weight loss. The clinical relevance of these effects, and the mechanism of any weight-independent component, remains uncertain and warrant confirmation in dedicated trials.

artigos.titulo: Medicaid Coverage Withdrawal and Dispensing of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists for Obesity
artigos.autores: Nyambod FT, Msemakweli JG, Onesphore M
artigos.destaque: In this quasi-experimental study, withdrawal of Medicaid coverage was associated with the loss of most reimbursed dispensing of GLP-1 RAs for obesity within one quarter, with little replacement by other agents. Protecting enrollees already receiving these drugs, for example, by honoring existing authorizations, might limit treatment interruption, but this has not been evaluated.

resumo.texto: Five state Medicaid programs withdrew coverage of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) for obesity in late 2025 and January 2026, and others have narrowed coverage or are reconsidering it. The benefits of these drugs appear to depend on continued use, but whether withdrawal interrupts treatment for current users is unknown. This study examined changes in dispensing of obesity-indicated GLP-1 RAs after state Medicaid programs withdrew or restricted coverage.

This quasi-experimental study used quarterly Medicaid State Drug Utilization Data for 50 states and the District of Columbia from 2021 through the first quarter of 2026. Difference-in-differences and event-study models compared dispensing in states that withdrew coverage with dispensing in states that continued it, using each state's dispensing of diabetes-indicated GLP-1 RAs as a within-state comparison. The exposure was withdrawal or restriction of Medicaid coverage of GLP-1 RAs for obesity, identified from state agency documents. The main outcome was reimbursed prescriptions for obesity-indicated GLP-1 RAs per 1,000 enrollees per quarter. Estimates are reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Data were analyzed from September to October 2026.

The five withdrawing states accounted for 2,428,709 (65.2%) of 3,725,732 obesity-indicated GLP-1 RA prescriptions reimbursed by Medicaid in 2025. Compared with 12 continuing states, withdrawal was associated with an 84.7% decline in obesity-indicated dispensing (95% CI: 64.5%-93.4%; exact permutation p < 0.001), or 29.1 fewer prescriptions per 1,000 enrollees per quarter (95% CI: 14.3-43.9). No significant change was detected in diabetes-indicated dispensing (-3.2%; 95% CI: -23.4% to 22.2%), and differences between the two groups before the withdrawals were announced were small and not statistically significant. In the first quarter without coverage, obesity-indicated dispensing fell by 61% to 96% in individual withdrawing states. The four states that withdrew on January 1, 2026, reimbursed 661,353 obesity-indicated prescriptions in the preceding quarter and 134,647 in the next, a decline of 526,706 (79.6%). Dispensing of older antiobesity medications increased by at most 2.9 prescriptions per 1,000 enrollees. Narrower criteria in two states were followed by declines of 23%-37%.

In this quasi-experimental study, withdrawal of Medicaid coverage was associated with the loss of most reimbursed dispensing of GLP-1 RAs for obesity within one quarter, with little replacement by other agents. Protecting enrollees already receiving these drugs, for example, by honoring existing authorizations, might limit treatment interruption, but this has not been evaluated.

artigos.titulo: Will GLP-1-based therapies reshape the epidemiology of MASLD? An emerging public health perspective
artigos.autores: Pereira ENGDS, Rodrigues KL
artigos.destaque: We identify observations that would refute these expectations and discuss implications for prevention, healthcare systems, and the natural history of MASLD. Population benefits will depend on sustained treatment, accessibility, affordability, and equitable implementation, alongside confirmation that histological improvements translate into fewer liver-related clinical events.

resumo.texto: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the leading cause of chronic liver disease worldwide, driven by increasing obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The expanding use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) raises an epidemiological question: could therapies targeting these metabolic drivers reshape the future burden of chronic liver disease? GLP-1-based therapies reduce body weight and improve metabolic dysfunction, with potential implications for hepatic steatosis and disease progression. The phase 3 ESSENCE trial demonstrated histological benefits of semaglutide in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) with moderate-to-advanced fibrosis, supporting accelerated or conditional regulatory approvals. However, effects on liver-related clinical outcomes remain unproven. In this Perspective, we examine the evidence and translate it into an explicitly parameterized scenario using a potential impact fraction. Combining published estimates of eligibility, relative risk, treatment persistence, and effectiveness with coverage scenarios of 5%, 10%, and 20%, the model suggests relative reductions of approximately 0.3% to 1.1% in the global incidence of cirrhosis among individuals with prevalent MASLD, at equilibrium (95% uncertainty interval at 20% coverage and intermediate persistence, 0.6% to 1.6%; best-case envelope, 4.6%). These estimates represent testable hypotheses rather than established clinical effects. Effective coverage, defined as coverage multiplied by persistence, is the principal constraint. We identify observations that would refute these expectations and discuss implications for prevention, healthcare systems, and the natural history of MASLD. Population benefits will depend on sustained treatment, accessibility, affordability, and equitable implementation, alongside confirmation that histological improvements translate into fewer liver-related clinical events.

artigos.titulo: Implications of Economic Hardship for Child Well-Being in Active and Reserve Component U.S. Military Families: Applying the Family Stress Model
artigos.autores: Lucier-Greer M, Saxey MT, Hanson E et al.
artigos.destaque: Notably, parent psychological distress was more strongly associated with child mental health symptoms among active-duty than NG/R families. Findings provide further support for the utility of the family stress model in studying military families while underscoring the importance of considering contextual differences.

resumo.texto: The family stress model has guided examinations of how economic hardship is linked to child outcomes with various populations, including military families. However, many studies have relied on smaller convenience samples with insufficient variation to address unique aspects of the military community context that may moderate the associations. Military families' duty status (i.e., full-time versus part-time service) is one such consideration because it can shape access to military-provided financial supports and may have implications for relational processes that are linked to hardship. Grounded in the family stress model, this study leveraged national data from 5529 military families who participated in the U.S. Census Bureau Household Pulse Survey to assess the prevalence of economic hardship, how economic hardship was associated with economic pressure, parent psychological distress, and child mental health, and whether these patterns differed between active-duty (n = 3128) and National Guard/Reserve families (NG/R; n = 2401). On average, active-duty and NG/R respondents similarly reported few economic hardships (M = 0.74 out of 8 for both). Support for the family stress model was observed for both groups. Greater economic hardship was associated with greater economic pressure, while economic pressure was related to more parent psychological distress, and, ultimately, more child mental health symptoms. Notably, parent psychological distress was more strongly associated with child mental health symptoms among active-duty than NG/R families. Findings provide further support for the utility of the family stress model in studying military families while underscoring the importance of considering contextual differences.

artigos.titulo: Health-care burden of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in European tertiary-care outpatient clinics (CONSTANS): a prospective multicentre cohort study
artigos.autores: Ratziu V, Dufour JF, Ponnaiah M et al.
artigos.destaque: MASLD was the second most frequent single cause for outpatient visits in eight European tertiary care centers. Significant fibrosis including cirrhosis was diagnosed in 44% of patients. The cost of required additional visits and procedures was equivalent to that recommended for hepatitis C before antiviral treatment.

resumo.texto: Despite modeling-based epidemiological studies of MASLD, precise estimates of the prevalence and health-care resource utilization in outpatient clinical practice are unknown. We assessed, in a real-life setting, the prevalence of suspected/confirmed MASLD and described health-care resource utilization.

A prospective, observational study of patients attending the outpatient hepato-gastroenterology clinics of eight European tertiary care centers during three months. Follow-up data of patients with suspected/confirmed MASLD were recorded 12 months after the screening visit: final diagnosis, disease stage, diagnostic work-up and the use of health-care resources.

5240 outpatients from Germany, France, United Kingdom, Switzerland, Italy, Spain and Slovakia were screened. The main reasons for visit were: chronic viral hepatitis, 33.4% (1749/5240), miscellaneous hepatobiliary conditions including neoplasms, 32.9% (1725/5240) and known/suspected MASLD, 24.7% (1293/5240) (pooled prevalence of 26.1% (95% CI: 19.1-34.7)). 1134 suspected/confirmed MASLD patients were included, the diagnosis was confirmed in 80.2% (909/1134). Significant fibrosis was documented in 22.7% (257/1134) and cirrhosis (including burn-out MASLD) in 21.3% (241/1134). Procedures performed differed between countries, overall 66.4% (753/1134) had imaging studies, 65.3% (740/1134) non-invasive fibrosis tests, 20.4% (231/1134) liver biopsy, while referral for further cardiometabolic assessment or therapy was minimal (144/1134, 15.8%). The cost of all procedures and visits was in the range of that recommended for exploring hepatitis C before treatment, although highly variable between countries.

MASLD was the second most frequent single cause for outpatient visits in eight European tertiary care centers. Significant fibrosis including cirrhosis was diagnosed in 44% of patients. The cost of required additional visits and procedures was equivalent to that recommended for hepatitis C before antiviral treatment.
IMI2-Grant Agreement 777377-LITMUS.

artigos.titulo: Effects of melatonin and transcranial photobiomodulation on neuroinflammation-related gene expression and anxiety-like behaviors in rats under chronic restraint stress
artigos.autores: Mazaheri M, Radahmadi M, Hosseini-Nasab F et al.
artigos.destaque: Stress-induced anxiety-like behaviors were significantly reduced by MLT, with effects similar to those of the combined treatment, which outperformed tPBM alone. These findings suggest the potential of tPBM and melatonin as complementary approaches for mitigating stress-related alterations, highlighting further investigation to optimize their doses and treatment parameters.

resumo.texto: Psychological stress causes immunological and behavioral alterations that can maladaptively affect the quality of life. However, melatonin (MLT) and transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM) have promising effects on brain functions. This study investigated the effects of MLT and tPBM in rats under chronic stress by evaluating neuroinflammation-related gene expression and anxiety-like behaviors. Sixty-three male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to nine groups: Control (Co), Sham injection (Sh-I), Sham tPBM (Sh-tPBM), MLT, tPBM, Stress (St), Stress with Melatonin (St-MLT), Stress with tPBM (St-tPBM), and Stress with Melatonin and tPBM (St-MLT-tPBM). Chronic restraint stress (2 h/day for 21 days) was applied to all stressed rats. MLT (20 mg/kg; intraperitoneal) and tPBM (808 nm; delivered to the scalp surface) were administered following restraint stress. Gene expression of hippocampal neuroinflammation-associated genes (IL-17A, ICAM-1, VCAM-1, IL-1β, and Aif1) was measured by real-time PCR. Additionally, anxiety-like behaviors were evaluated by the elevated-plus maze test. Hippocampal IL-17A and ICAM-1 gene expression was higher in stressed rats than in normal subjects. However, in the St group, IL-1β expression remained unchanged, whereas Aif1 expression was decreased compared with the Co group. tPBM reversed the stress-induced upregulation of IL-17A and ICAM-1 expression, whereas MLT could not mitigate them compared with normal subjects. The combined MLT and tPBM treatment elicited gene expression changes similar to those observed with tPBM alone. Stress-induced anxiety-like behaviors were significantly reduced by MLT, with effects similar to those of the combined treatment, which outperformed tPBM alone. These findings suggest the potential of tPBM and melatonin as complementary approaches for mitigating stress-related alterations, highlighting further investigation to optimize their doses and treatment parameters.

artigos.titulo: Predictive Analytics and Workflow Automation to Reduce Administrative Burden and Clinician Burnout in United States Clinical Settings: A Systematic Review
artigos.autores: Akosah A, Hunt TJ
artigos.destaque: Workflow-integrated predictive analytics and automation interventions were associated with measurable improvements in documentation workload and selected burnout indicators in US clinical settings. However, evidence remains mixed and largely observational. Rigorous, multisite, longitudinal evaluations using standardized workload and burnout metrics are needed to determine sustainability and generalizability.

resumo.texto: Electronic health record (EHR)-related administrative burden remains a frequently cited contributor to clinician burnout in the United States. Although digital systems were implemented to improve quality, safety, and care coordination, expanded documentation requirements, inbox messaging, and regulatory reporting have increased clerical workload. Traditional interruptive clinical decision support tools may further increase cognitive demands through alert fatigue and workflow disruption. Health systems have increasingly adopted predictive analytics and workflow-integrated automation, including ambient artificial intelligence (AI) documentation, inbox prioritization, and audit log-based workflow monitoring. However, their effects on operational efficiency and clinician well-being remain uncertain. This review examined clinician-facing interventions in US clinical settings and their impact on documentation workload, operational efficiency, and burnout-related outcomes.

A systematic review guided by Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses was conducted using PubMed, CINAHL, and Embase. The search included English-language studies published between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2025, with an updated search capturing eligible early online publications through 2026. Eligible studies evaluated clinician-facing predictive analytics or workflow automation in US clinical settings and reported measurable outcomes, including documentation time, after-hours EHR use, alert burden, cognitive task load, productivity, or validated burnout measures. Findings were synthesized narratively because interventions and outcome measures varied.

Of 520 records identified, 173 unique records were screened; 24 (13.9%) underwent full-text review, and 7 of 24 (29.2%) met inclusion criteria. Ambient AI documentation platforms were associated with approximately 10%-30% reductions in documentation time, although findings on after-hours EHR activity varied. Several multisite implementations reported improvements in validated burnout measures and cognitive task load. AI-driven inbox prioritization reduced message review time, while audit log-based clinical decision support monitoring identified changes in EHR activity patterns following intervention. Evidence quality varied, and follow-up periods were generally short.

Workflow-integrated predictive analytics and automation interventions were associated with measurable improvements in documentation workload and selected burnout indicators in US clinical settings. However, evidence remains mixed and largely observational. Rigorous, multisite, longitudinal evaluations using standardized workload and burnout metrics are needed to determine sustainability and generalizability.

artigos.titulo: Mangiferin Buffers Depressive-Like Behaviors by Modulating Astrocytic DHHC2 in the Hippocampus
artigos.autores: Xia ZX, Zhao YL, Tian D et al.
artigos.destaque: Further mechanistic studies showed that MGF reverses reactive astrogliosis by regulating astrocytic DHHC2-Nrf2 signaling, including Nrf2 palmitoylation and its nuclear translocation, thereby protecting Nrf2 from Keap1-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and sustaining its transcriptional activity in reactive astrocytes. These findings demonstrate that MGF alleviates chronic stress-induced anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors by engaging the astrocytic DHHC2-Nrf2 signaling, suppressing reactive astrogliosis and reversing hippocampal synaptic and neurogenic deficits, which provides novel insights into the therapeutic potential of MGF for chronic stress-related mood disorders.

resumo.texto: Several lines of evidence indicate that mangiferin (MGF) ameliorates chronic stress-induced anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors, yet its precise role and underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that MGF effectively alleviates anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors in mice exposed to chronic stress, accompanied by reduced synaptic loss and ameliorated hippocampal neurogenesis deficits. Notably, nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) expression is preferentially altered in hippocampal astrocytes but not in neurons or microglia after chronic stress and MGF treatment, and knockdown of astrocytic Nrf2 abrogates the antidepressant effect of MGF. Further mechanistic studies showed that MGF reverses reactive astrogliosis by regulating astrocytic DHHC2-Nrf2 signaling, including Nrf2 palmitoylation and its nuclear translocation, thereby protecting Nrf2 from Keap1-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and sustaining its transcriptional activity in reactive astrocytes. These findings demonstrate that MGF alleviates chronic stress-induced anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors by engaging the astrocytic DHHC2-Nrf2 signaling, suppressing reactive astrogliosis and reversing hippocampal synaptic and neurogenic deficits, which provides novel insights into the therapeutic potential of MGF for chronic stress-related mood disorders.

artigos.titulo: Temporal and Spatial Dynamics and Mechanisms of Brain-Gut Axis Injury Induced by Confinement-Like Physical Restraint Stress in Mice
artigos.autores: Qiao Y, Cheng R, Zhang X et al.
artigos.destaque: Chronic confinement-like restraint stress induces triphasic nonlinear gut-brain axis injury rather than linear damage. PLA is a promising candidate target for mental health protection in isolated, confined, extreme environment populations and stress-related depression intervention.

resumo.texto: Long-term SIS exposure across aerospace, deep-sea, underground, and quarantine settings increases depression and gut-brain axis dysfunction risk, but long-term nonlinear injury dynamics remain poorly understood.

We analyzed GBD 2023 depression burden data in adults aged 15-49, then established a 0-35 day (d) chronic restraint stress mouse model that isolates the core physical confinement and activity-restriction component of SIS. Integrating behavior, histology, biochemistry, 16S sequencing, metabolomics, and formal nonlinear changepoint analysis, we validated picolinic acid (PLA) effects via in vivo intervention, in silico docking, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT).

Population data showed that the global depression burden during the COVID-19 period followed a rapid rise-partial recovery-persistent disability pattern, providing a temporal reference for the experimental model. In mice, confinement-like restraint stress induced triphasic nonlinear gut-brain injury with changepoints at ~7 and ~21 days: early HPA/inflammatory activation, mid-phase gut barrier disruption and anxiety-like behavior, and late hippocampal damage with despair-like behavior. Microbiota remodeling and tryptophan metabolic shift formed the core signaling cascade, with PLA identified as the key gut-brain metabolite. Exogenous PLA dose-dependently improved depressive phenotypes, repaired barriers, and suppressed HPA hyperactivity and inflammation. FMT provided suggestive evidence that gut microbiota contribute to PLA's protective effects.

Chronic confinement-like restraint stress induces triphasic nonlinear gut-brain axis injury rather than linear damage. PLA is a promising candidate target for mental health protection in isolated, confined, extreme environment populations and stress-related depression intervention.

artigos.titulo: Autistic matrescence as dynamic person-environment fit: a theoretical model of regulatory resources and support usability
artigos.autores: Steinbrück PC
artigos.destaque: Five propositions address within-person variation, sensory and communication moderation, recovery mediation, support usability, and reciprocal developmental feedback. Candidate measures are mapped onto instruments, including the Glasgow Sensory Questionnaire, state anxiety, perceived stress, the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, parenting confidence, parenting styles, and preliminary autistic-burnout measures. Generalization beyond autistic matrescence is presented as a transfer hypothesis rather than an established contribution.

resumo.texto: Matrescence is a developmental transition involving bodily, psychological, relational, and social change. Research on autistic pregnancy and early parenthood documents sensory overload, communication barriers, disrupted routines, professional scrutiny, and limited recovery alongside attachment, commitment, competence, and self-knowledge. Such divergence requires a model treating neither autism nor parenthood as sufficient explanations of psychological outcomes.

This theoretical paper reuses the 25-publication corpus of a published mapping review on autistic pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum experience, infant feeding, and early parenting. It develops a distinct theoretical synthesis by integrating that corpus with theories of stress, resource loss, functioning, and person-environment-occupation fit; it does not report a new review or formal study-quality appraisal.

The paper proposes that proximal psychological outcomes are shaped by dynamic person-environment fit among transition demands, state-dependent regulatory resources, and environmental demands and affordances. Its specific extension is the distinction between support availability and usability. Support usability is modelled as a staged conversion process through which available support must be accessed, processed, trusted, and implemented to become psychologically effective. The model specifies boundary conditions under which minority stress, trauma, psychopathology, acute clinical complications, or structural violence should be treated as primary explanations.

Five propositions address within-person variation, sensory and communication moderation, recovery mediation, support usability, and reciprocal developmental feedback. Candidate measures are mapped onto instruments, including the Glasgow Sensory Questionnaire, state anxiety, perceived stress, the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, parenting confidence, parenting styles, and preliminary autistic-burnout measures. Generalization beyond autistic matrescence is presented as a transfer hypothesis rather than an established contribution.

artigos.titulo: Burnout Among Professionals in ABA-Based Services in Brazil
artigos.autores: Sarilho C, Monteleone TV, Franklin BM et al.
artigos.destaque: These descriptive findings, which characterize the professionals surveyed rather than the Brazilian ABA workforce as a whole, point to the relevance of systemic and organizational responses to burnout in ABA services in Brazil. Improving working conditions, supervision quality, and support systems may contribute to better professional well-being and, consequently, to higher quality of care for individuals with autism.

resumo.texto: Burnout among professionals working in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA)-based services has received increasing attention internationally; however, there is limited empirical data from low- and middle-income countries. This study aimed to describe the prevalence and characteristics of burnout among ABA professionals in Brazil and to examine how burnout indicators were distributed across professional and organizational characteristics within the sample.

A cross-sectional survey was conducted with ABA professionals working in different regions of Brazil. Participants completed the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS), together with a questionnaire covering demographic, professional, and work-related variables. Burnout was analyzed descriptively, with each dimension classified into low, moderate, and high categories using established cutoff scores, and distributions were examined across professional roles, age groups, academic backgrounds, salary ranges, and caseload.

Burnout indicators were highly prevalent in this sample. High emotional exhaustion was identified in 77.4% of participants and low personal accomplishment (indicating greater burnout on that dimension) in 89.9%, whereas high depersonalization was less frequent (34.1%). Within this sample, the proportion of participants classified in the most severe category increased from behavior technicians to coordinators to supervisors across all three dimensions, and professionals managing more than 10 concurrent cases showed higher proportions of high depersonalization and low personal accomplishment. Categorical burnout distributions were similar across salary ranges.

These descriptive findings, which characterize the professionals surveyed rather than the Brazilian ABA workforce as a whole, point to the relevance of systemic and organizational responses to burnout in ABA services in Brazil. Improving working conditions, supervision quality, and support systems may contribute to better professional well-being and, consequently, to higher quality of care for individuals with autism.

artigos.titulo: High stocking density impaired growth and induced oxidative stress, lipid metabolism disorder, and ferroptosis in grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella)
artigos.autores: Zidan SRS, Yuan Y, Li W et al.
artigos.destaque: Furthermore, PUFAs overflow into acsl4 (upregulated) increased membrane lipid peroxidation, and gpx4 (downregulated) failed to reduce resulting lipid hydroperoxides, causing ferroptosis execution. In conclusion, chronic crowding stress disrupts growth, causes physiological responses, and disrupts hepatopancreas health by inducing oxidative stress, altered lipid metabolism, and induced ferroptosis in grass carp reared in RAS.

resumo.texto: Intensive aquaculture via increasing fish density became an inevitable choice to increase aquaculture output. However, crowding stress compromises growth and fish health. The present study investigated the impacts of stocking density on growth, stress responses, oxidative status, lipid metabolism, and ferroptosis in grass carp. Fish (128.02 ± 2.35 g) were reared at three densities: LSD (low stocking density, 5 kg/m3), MSD (medium stocking density, 10 kg/m3), and HSD (high stocking density, 20 kg/m3) for 65 days in the recirculating aquaculture system (RAS). The results showed that increasing fish density negatively influenced the growth performance and feed utilization. The HSD group induced a stress response by significantly increasing the serum cortisol, glucose, and cholesterol levels, as well as AST and ALT activity. Crowding stress conditions induced oxidative stress and ferroptosis, marked by depleted antioxidants including catalase (CAT), superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutathione (GSH), and total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC), decreased glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), while raising malondialdehyde (MDA) and iron content in both serum and hepatopancreas tissue (p < 0.05). Additionally, transcriptomic analysis detected that HSD treatment changed lipid metabolism and promoted ferroptosis. Interestingly, HSD treatment prompted fatty acid synthesis, causing an increase in polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) synthesis and their elongation (acaca, acsbg1, elovl2, elovl5, and elovl6 were upregulated), while it suppressed fatty acid oxidation (cpt1ab and dgat2 were downregulated), diverting PUFAs toward membrane phospholipids. Furthermore, PUFAs overflow into acsl4 (upregulated) increased membrane lipid peroxidation, and gpx4 (downregulated) failed to reduce resulting lipid hydroperoxides, causing ferroptosis execution. In conclusion, chronic crowding stress disrupts growth, causes physiological responses, and disrupts hepatopancreas health by inducing oxidative stress, altered lipid metabolism, and induced ferroptosis in grass carp reared in RAS.

artigos.titulo: Beyond adversity: Dispositional mindfulness as a potential link between positive childhood experiences and lower hair cortisol concentration in adulthood
artigos.autores: Bartolen I, Soláriková P
artigos.destaque: These findings extend existing evidence on the psychological benefits associated with PCEs by providing preliminary support for dispositional mindfulness as a potential link between PCEs and lower cumulative cortisol exposure in adulthood. Considering positive developmental experiences alongside adversity may improve understanding of individual differences in psychological functioning and long-term HPA-axis activity.

resumo.texto: Advers childhood experiences (ACEs) are associated with altered stress regulation, yet less is known about how positive childhood experiences (PCEs) contribute to adaptive physiological functioning. PCEs may represent developmental resources that promote adaptive psychological and biological functioning. This study examined whether PCEs were associated with cumulative cortisol exposure, indexed by hair cortisol concentration (HCC), through dispositional mindfulness and resilience, and whether these associations varied according to cumulative childhood adversity.

A community sample of 210 adults (M age = 28.95, SD = 10.20, range = 19-77; 74.8% female) completed an online assessment battery. A subsample of 120 participants provided hair samples for cortisol assessment. Participants completed measures of Protective and Compensatory experiences (PACE significance), ACEs, dispositional mindfulness (MAAS), resilience (RS-14), and current stress (LSC-R). Hair cortisol concentration (HCC) from 3 cm proximal segment was assessed as an indicator of cumulative hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activity.

PACE sig. showed indirect association with lower HCC through greater dispositional mindfulness, whereas resilience did not. Moderation analyses suggested that the positive PACE sig.-MAAS association was stronger at higher levels of ACE exposure. Positive and adverse childhood experiences frequently co-occurred among participants with higher cumulative adversity.

These findings extend existing evidence on the psychological benefits associated with PCEs by providing preliminary support for dispositional mindfulness as a potential link between PCEs and lower cumulative cortisol exposure in adulthood. Considering positive developmental experiences alongside adversity may improve understanding of individual differences in psychological functioning and long-term HPA-axis activity.

artigos.titulo: AI Scribe in Specialized Rehabilitation: Usability Study of Perceived Usability and Usefulness Among Physicians and Psychologists
artigos.autores: Engan HK, Landstad I, Sand K et al.
artigos.destaque: This study demonstrated broad acceptance of an AI-based ambient scribe among physicians and psychologists working in specialized rehabilitation. The AI scribe was generally perceived as valuable, easy to use, and clinically relevant. Most participants reported a reduced perceived documentation burden and improved attentiveness during consultations. These findings suggest that clinicians perceived the AI scribe as supporting more focused patient interactions. Some concerns were noted regarding completeness and occasional inaccuracies, highlighting areas for refinement. Future research should explore long-term implementation in routine rehabilitation settings and its effects on workflow, documentation quality, and patient experience.

resumo.texto: Clinical documentation in specialized, interdisciplinary rehabilitation is often time-consuming and complex and may contribute to clinician burnout and reduced time for patient interaction. AI-based scribes transcribe and summarize clinical notes and may reduce documentation burden; however, their usefulness and usability in specialized rehabilitation remain uninvestigated.

This study aimed to assess the use of an ambient AI scribe tool among physicians and psychologists in specialized rehabilitation, focusing on perceived usefulness, usability, note quality, impact on patient interaction, perceptions of time spent on documentation, and documentation-related fatigue.

Over approximately 4 weeks, physicians and psychologists at 9 specialized rehabilitation centers used an ambient AI scribe during clinical consultations. Usability and user experience were assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and a modified technology acceptance model (TAM). Participants rated an AI-generated note using a modified 8-item Physician Documentation Quality Instrument (PDQI-8) questionnaire to evaluate documentation quality. Additional questions explored perceived impact on patient interaction, documentation-related fatigue, and general attitudes toward AI technology.

Thirty-one clinicians (18 physicians and 13 psychologists) used the AI scribe over approximately one month and completed evaluation questionnaires. The mean SUS score was 78.3 (SD 10.4), with 86.7% of participants scoring above the usability threshold. Perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) were relatively high (mean PU score 5.65, SD 1.33; mean PEOU score 5.56, SD 1.17), and 87.1% expressed intention to use the AI scribe in future practice. Most participants (80.6%) agreed that using the AI scribe reduced time spent on documentation, while 66.6% reported a reduced perception of documentation-related fatigue. The quality of AI-generated notes was rated relatively high, with a mean modified PDQI-8 score of 4.3 (SD 0.3) out of 5. Comprehensibility received the highest rating (mean 4.6, SD 0.6), whereas thoroughness received the lowest rating (mean 3.9, SD 1.0) among the note quality variables. Overall, 71.0% of participants expressed some level of agreement that the AI scribe enhanced attentiveness during patient consultations, while a similar proportion (70.9%) agreed that it made active listening easier by reducing distractions associated with note-taking. A few participants reported that some notes were incomplete, lacked biopsychosocial details, and contained inaccuracies.

This study demonstrated broad acceptance of an AI-based ambient scribe among physicians and psychologists working in specialized rehabilitation. The AI scribe was generally perceived as valuable, easy to use, and clinically relevant. Most participants reported a reduced perceived documentation burden and improved attentiveness during consultations. These findings suggest that clinicians perceived the AI scribe as supporting more focused patient interactions. Some concerns were noted regarding completeness and occasional inaccuracies, highlighting areas for refinement. Future research should explore long-term implementation in routine rehabilitation settings and its effects on workflow, documentation quality, and patient experience.

artigos.titulo: Biomarkers in Patients With Acute Ischaemic Stroke Undergoing Thrombectomy Compared With Controls: A Pilot Study
artigos.autores: Vithal R, Krönlein A, El-Merhi A et al.
artigos.destaque: GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings.

resumo.texto: Detection of cerebral ischaemia is challenging in patients who are anaesthetised, sedated or have reduced levels of consciousness, as neurological examination is difficult or even impossible to assess. Furthermore, as some patients cannot be transported for radiology, for example during surgery, a reliable blood biomarker for detecting acute cerebral events would be of considerable clinical value. We aimed to compare levels of brain injury biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and total tau (tau) in patients with acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy under general anaesthesia or sedation to controls undergoing non-cerebral surgery under general anaesthesia. These biomarkers were chosen because previous studies have demonstrated their potential as blood biomarkers of acute cerebral injury and ischaemic stroke.

In this prospective, observational pilot study, conducted at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden, between 2021 and 2024, GFAP, NfL, and tau were analysed using the Simoa Neurology 4-plex assay, before thrombectomy or surgery and at 2- and 24 h thereafter.

Blood samples from 21 patients with AIS and 19 controls were analysed. GFAP concentrations in patients with AIS increased significantly from baseline to 24 h (median 301.0 → 1443.0 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and were higher than in controls at all time points (p < 0.01). In the controls there was no significant increase in GFAP from baseline to 24 h (p = 0.449). NfL and tau increased significantly in patients with AIS (p = 0.001 and 0.002) but also in the controls (p = 0.001 and 0.047).

GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings.

A biomarker of ischaemic cerebral injury could be attractive to support treatments to protect brain health during anaesthesia and surgery. In a pilot study, glial fibrillary acidic protein emerged as a potential candidate as it was increased in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy for large-vessel ischaemic stroke compared to anaesthetised patients undergoing non-cerebral surgery.
ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03919370.

artigos.titulo: Hemp bark extract attenuates scopolamine-induced cognitive dysfunction through multi-target cholinesterase, MAO-B, and antioxidant mechanisms
artigos.autores: Heo HY, Kim JK, Park S et al.
artigos.destaque: Docking, GNINA rescoring, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM-GBSA/MM-PBSA analyses further supported stable interactions of these cannabinoids with the target enzymes, particularly cannabidiolic acid with acetylcholinesterase and MAO-B. These findings suggest that HBE protects against scopolamine-induced cognitive dysfunction through coordinated cholinesterase inhibition, MAO-B modulation, and antioxidant defense, with cannabidiol, cannabidiolic acid, and cannabichromenic acid acting as key multi-target constituents.

resumo.texto: Cognitive decline associated with Alzheimer's disease is driven by several interconnected mechanisms, including impaired cholinergic signaling, MAO-B-linked oxidative stress, and reduced neuronal antioxidant capacity. In this study, ethanol extracts prepared from hemp root, stem, bark, leaf, and seed were compared to identify hemp-derived materials with multi-target neuroprotective potential. Among the tested extracts, hemp bark extract (HBE) showed the most balanced activity profile, inhibiting acetylcholinesterase, butyrylcholinesterase, and MAO-B with IC50 values of 0.56, 0.01, and 0.02 mg/mL, respectively. HBE at 0.2 μg/mL suppressed H2O2-induced intracellular reactive oxygen species formation and recovered superoxide dismutase activity in SH-SY5Y neuronal cells. In a scopolamine-induced mouse model, oral HBE administration at 100 and 200 mg/kg improved performance in the passive avoidance test and reduced escape latency in the water maze test, indicating protection against scopolamine-induced cognitive deficits. Chemical profiling by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry revealed several cannabinoids in HBE, including cannabidiol, cannabidiolic acid, and cannabichromenic acid. Enzyme assays showed that cannabichromenic acid potently inhibited acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase, with IC50 values of 1.3 and 6.6 μM, respectively, whereas cannabidiol and cannabidiolic acid were the most active MAO-B inhibitors, with IC50 values of 2.3 and 5.3 μM. Docking, GNINA rescoring, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM-GBSA/MM-PBSA analyses further supported stable interactions of these cannabinoids with the target enzymes, particularly cannabidiolic acid with acetylcholinesterase and MAO-B.
