A cross-sectional survey design was employed with 250 primary caregivers of children diagnosed with ASD. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire comprising five self-report instruments. Preliminary data screening were performed using SPSS, while the hypothesized serial mediation model was tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model demonstrated adequate reliability and validity. The structural model explained 32.4% of the variance in parental coping strategies (R2 = 0.324), 41.5% in parenting self-efficacy (R2 = 0.415), and 38.5% in child behavioral outcomes (R2 = 0.385). Parental stress was negatively associated with coping strategies (β = -0.382, p < 0.001). Social support was positively associated with both coping strategies (β = 0.427, p < 0.001) and parenting self-efficacy (β = 0.452, p < 0.001). Coping strategies (β = -0.286, p < 0.001) and parenting self-efficacy (β = -0.358, p < 0.001) were negatively associated with child behavioral outcomes. The direct path from parental stress to parenting self-efficacy was non-significant (β = -0.089, p = 0.164). Mediation analyses indicated that coping strategies significantly mediated both the stress-outcome and support-outcome relationships, whereas self-efficacy mediated only the support-outcome pathway. Serial indirect effects through coping strategies and then self-efficacy were significant for parental stress (β = 0.043, 95% CI [0.008, 0.078]) and social support (β = -0.048, 95% CI [-0.085, -0.011]). Findings highlight targeted interventions to strengthen social support, adaptive coping, and parenting self-efficacy. Coping-skills training and confidence-building may benefit children with ASD. The study supports a serial mediation framework: coping and self-efficacy are key pathways from contextual factors to child outcomes.

artigos.titulo: Effect of intranasal insulin on postoperative delirium: A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
artigos.autores: Saeed O, Nounou MV, Saeed A et al.
artigos.destaque: Intranasal insulin probably reduces POD in adult surgical patients. The dose-response findings suggest that 30 IU may provide the greatest benefit, with no apparent additional reduction at higher doses. Larger multicentre trials are needed to confirm the optimal regimen and comprehensively evaluate safety.

resumo.texto: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common neurological complication associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Intranasal insulin may improve cognitive function, but its effectiveness and optimal dose for preventing POD remain uncertain. We evaluated the effect of intranasal insulin on POD and explored its dose-response relationship.

PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through November 2025. Randomised controlled trials comparing intranasal insulin with placebo in adult surgical patients were included. Random-effect pairwise and one-stage dose-response meta-analyses were performed. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation framework.

Eight randomised controlled trials involving 892 patients were included (502 receiving intranasal insulin and 390 receiving placebo). Intranasal insulin probably reduces POD (moderate-certainty evidence) compared with placebo (risk ratio, 0.39; 95% confidence interval, 0.29-0.51). Subgroup analyses found no significant differences according to surgery type or anaesthetic technique. A dose-response analysis demonstrated a nonlinear association, with a rapid reduction in POD risk at lower doses and the greatest modelled benefit at 30 IU (risk ratio, 0.39; 95% confidence interval, 0.29-0.53). The dose-response curve plateaued above 30 IU, with no additional reduction in POD risk at higher doses. Seven trials had a low risk of bias, while one raised some concerns because of bias in measurement of the outcome.

Intranasal insulin probably reduces POD in adult surgical patients. The dose-response findings suggest that 30 IU may provide the greatest benefit, with no apparent additional reduction at higher doses. Larger multicentre trials are needed to confirm the optimal regimen and comprehensively evaluate safety.

artigos.titulo: Mindfulness-Based Intervention Improves Cognitive Function in Patients With Schizophrenia in Remitted: A Randomized Controlled Trial
artigos.autores: Lyu P, Yuan X, Zhang Y et al.
artigos.destaque: MBI significantly improved the primary outcome of mindfulness (FFMQ) and showed promising exploratory improvements in processing speed (P300 latency) and sustained attention (CPT-IP). FER change may represent a potential indirect pathway associated with change in SQLS. These findings support MBI as a promising cognitive rehabilitation intervention.

resumo.texto: Patients with schizophrenia exhibit deficits in facial emotion recognition (FER), attention, P300, and quality of life (QoL), which severely hinder functional recovery. This study aims to explore the effects of mindfulness-based intervention (MBI) on these outcomes and the potential mediating mechanisms.

In this 8-week randomized, single-blind, controlled study, a total of 70 remitted patients with schizophrenia were randomly assigned to the MBI group or the control group. The Five-Factor Mindfulness Scale (FFMQ), FER, P300 indices, Continuous Performance Test-Identical Pairs (CPT-IP), and Schizophrenia Quality of Life Scale (SQLS) were measured at baseline and week 8 to assess mindfulness levels, cognitive function, neurophysiological parameters, and QoL. Linear mixed models evaluated intervention effects. Mediation analyses used pre-post change scores with bootstrap resampling.

For the primary outcome, MBI significantly improved FFMQ (β = 16.750, 95% CI [7.769, 25.731], p < 0.001). For the exploratory outcomes, significant improvements were observed for P300 latency (β = -63.602, 95% CI [-88.651, -38.554], p < 0.001) and CPT-IP (β = 8.219, 95% CI [4.004, 12.433], p < 0.001). FER and P300 amplitude showed nominal improvements only, and SQLS showed a non-significant trend. A significant indirect effect through FER change was observed for change in SQLS (indirect effect = -6.343, 95% CI [-11.467, -2.288]), but CPT-IP change did not mediate P300 amplitude improvement.

MBI significantly improved the primary outcome of mindfulness (FFMQ) and showed promising exploratory improvements in processing speed (P300 latency) and sustained attention (CPT-IP). FER change may represent a potential indirect pathway associated with change in SQLS. These findings support MBI as a promising cognitive rehabilitation intervention.
https://www.chictr.org.cn, identifier ChiCTR 2500106735, registered on: 29/07/2025.

artigos.titulo: Neural substrates related to memory consolidation of learning multiple motor sequences during wakeful rest
artigos.autores: Yoon S, Caraballo A, Kim S
artigos.destaque: In contrast, neural activity patterns in the right hippocampus, right putamen, and sensorimotor regions during interleaved rest showed greater similarity to post-learning rest patterns than pre-learning rest patterns. These findings suggest that under highly interfering, multi-sequence learning conditions, the consolidation of motor memories may not be related to a specific sequence but may instead reflect a generalized or abstract representation of sequences, potentially to stabilize and minimize interference among newly acquired skills.

resumo.texto: Motor learning has long been considered independent of the hippocampus, but recent evidence suggests that the hippocampus contributes to motor memory consolidation during wakeful rest. However, whether hippocampal reactivation supports consolidation during interleaved rest remains unclear. We investigated the fMRI evidence of motor memory consolidation of learning multiple motor sequences during wakeful rest. We found that while sensorimotor regions exhibited sequence-specific activity patterns during practice, these were not reliably discriminable in the sensorimotor regions and hippocampus during interleaved rest. In contrast, neural activity patterns in the right hippocampus, right putamen, and sensorimotor regions during interleaved rest showed greater similarity to post-learning rest patterns than pre-learning rest patterns. These findings suggest that under highly interfering, multi-sequence learning conditions, the consolidation of motor memories may not be related to a specific sequence but may instead reflect a generalized or abstract representation of sequences, potentially to stabilize and minimize interference among newly acquired skills.

artigos.titulo: Sequential Sampling from Memory Underlies Perceptual Decisions Unyoked from Actions
artigos.autores: Sharma P, Shadlen MN, Shushruth S
artigos.destaque: Our results reveal a strategic feature of working memory of retaining information based on its future utility. This observation opens new avenues for investigating how memory and decision-making interact.

resumo.texto: Perceptual decision-making refers to the class of decisions in which sensory evidence is used to categorize percepts and guide actions. Conventionally, categorical decisions are thought to precede motor actions. However, recent studies in nonhuman primates challenge this assumption-when perceptual decisions were uncoupled from the actions they bear upon, animals postponed the decisions until relevant response options were revealed. To determine whether this postponement stems from cognitive limitations unique to nonhuman primates, we conducted a similar experiment with human participants. Naive participants viewed a random dot motion (RDM) stimulus that was difficult to categorize. After a delay period following the RDM, two choice targets were presented and participants decided which target lay closer to the perceived motion direction. Decision accuracy varied across participants, reflecting individual differences in ability to integrate motion evidence. Notably, participants with higher decision accuracy showed prolonged deliberation after choice-target presentation. Furthermore, the time they took to report their decisions depended on the strength of the motion evidence. This pattern of accuracy and decision reporting time could be accounted for by a bounded diffusion model in which participants sequentially sample stored sensory information from memory during the target selection phase. When the RDM was challenging to categorize, the subsequent appearance of the targets provided a framework to interrogate stored evidence and render a decision. Our results reveal a strategic feature of working memory of retaining information based on its future utility. This observation opens new avenues for investigating how memory and decision-making interact.

artigos.titulo: An anti-aging drug may help protect the brain before Alzheimer's symptoms begin
artigos.destaque: A surprising new study suggests that an anti-aging drug could help protect people genetically predisposed to Alzheimer's disease. Researchers found that just four weeks of low-dose rapamycin improved brain blood flow in healthy middle-aged adults carrying the high-risk APOE4 gene variant, with women showing the strongest benefits. Because declining blood flow can occur years before Alzheimer's symptoms appear, the discovery raises hopes for preventing or delaying the disease before memory loss begins.

artigos.titulo: Scientists discover mysterious “lonely” brain waves linked to memory loss
artigos.destaque: Scientists have uncovered a surprising link between Alzheimer’s-related protein buildup, disrupted brain waves during deep sleep, and fading memory. The findings suggest that hidden changes in how the brain processes memories overnight may contribute to age-related memory loss long before Alzheimer’s symptoms appear.

artigos.titulo: Does obesity pharmacotherapy change eating behaviour in humans? Evaluation of the literature using learnings from bariatric surgery
artigos.autores: McKee CE, Price RK, Miras AD
artigos.destaque: Whether the effects of pharmacotherapy and surgery engage in the same biological processes and whether their effects follow a similar time course remains an unresolved question. We consider the implications of this framework for nutrition and dietetic practice.

resumo.texto: Obesity is characterised by the dysregulation of the neurobiological systems governing hunger, satiety and food reward. Dysfunction in signalling across the gut-brain axis impairs both homeostatic and hedonic control of eating, ultimately resulting in excessive energy intake. The weight loss achieved through pharmacological and surgical interventions is not primarily the result of cognitive behavioural restraint; it instead reflects the direct biological modification of the neuroendocrine circuits involved in regulation of eating behaviour. This review applies a conceptual framework structured around two axes; homeostatic versus hedonic eating and the appetitive versus consummatory phases of feeding to interpret how these interventions change eating behaviour. Bariatric surgery has a substantially more mature evidence base. The Roux-en-Y gastric bypass in particular, produces sustained modification in consummatory homeostatic behaviour - with earlier satiation and meal termination, in conjunction with short-term changes in food preferences. Evidence for GLP-1 receptor agonists and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists demonstrates a parallel profile of reduced hunger, increased satiety, attenuated food-cue reactivity and subduing of the hedonic drive. Whether the effects of pharmacotherapy and surgery engage in the same biological processes and whether their effects follow a similar time course remains an unresolved question. We consider the implications of this framework for nutrition and dietetic practice.

artigos.titulo: Food marketing in South Africa by influencers on social media
artigos.autores: Deyce LA, Frank T, Khan AS et al.
artigos.destaque: The study proposes that mandatory government-led regulations on the marketing of unhealthy products to children should be implemented, such as prohibiting posts featuring unhealthy products in child-directed content and mandatory disclosure of marketing if the influencer is getting paid for posting unhealthy products. These regulations should include social media and cover children up to the age of 18 years old.

resumo.texto: Childhood obesity has been linked to social media marketing of unhealthy foods and beverages. Apart from targeted marketing practices on social media, food and beverage companies also make use of social media influencers to market their products, blurring the lines between organic content and marketing content. This study aimed to investigate the types of commercial food and beverage products found in posts by influencers on YouTube and TikTok, as well as the marketing techniques used to promote these products.

Cross-sectional analysis. Public posts by nineteen influencers were downloaded and analysed for branded products. Nutritional information for these products was collected and analysed using the proposed South African nutrient profiling model.
Public profiles of nineteen influencers on YouTube and TikTok.

This study found that 52 % of posts contained branded food and beverages, 80 % of posts that contained marketing also contained at least one unhealthy product that would carry a warning label for being high in either sugar, saturated fat, Na or non-sugar sweeteners. Of the marketed posts, only 8 % were labelled as containing marketing. The most used marketing techniques were references to children, such as cartoons.

The study proposes that mandatory government-led regulations on the marketing of unhealthy products to children should be implemented, such as prohibiting posts featuring unhealthy products in child-directed content and mandatory disclosure of marketing if the influencer is getting paid for posting unhealthy products. These regulations should include social media and cover children up to the age of 18 years old.

artigos.titulo: Stakeholder perception on the implementation and effectiveness of front-of-pack labelling on processed foods and beverages: a qualitative study in Peru
artigos.autores: Proaño GV, Meza-Hernández M, Yabiku-Soto K et al.
artigos.destaque: Perceptions among stakeholders centred on prioritising future FOPL evaluation and education and on ensuring adequate resources are allocated to ensure that FOPL is properly implemented within supportive environments.

resumo.texto: In response to rising obesity rates in Peru, front-of-pack labelling (FOPL) for processed foods and beverages was implemented in 2019 as part of Law No. 30 021, with the final phase implemented in 2021, to promote healthier consumer choices. However, policy evaluations investigating implementation and effectiveness are limited. Thus, this study aimed to determine stakeholders' perceptions of the implementation of the FOPL final phase in Peru.
Using the reach, effectiveness, adoption, implementation and maintenance (RE-AIM) framework, semi-structured interviews with stakeholders were conducted and analysed using thematic analysis.
Hybrid in-person and virtual interviews took place between February and March 2025.
Stakeholders from government, civil society, academia and industry were eligible to participate if involved in FOPL implementation or evaluation in Peru.

A total of twenty stakeholder interviews were conducted, and four themes were developed. Firstly, stakeholders reported that FOPL reach remained constrained by certain products and locations despite the national law. Secondly, while comprehensive impact evaluations should be prioritised, a lack of complete implementation of Law No. 30021 can impact FOPL effectiveness. Stakeholders emphasised that poor acceptance and unsupportive environments can impede effective FOPL implementation (e.g. industry/political resistance, inadequate FOPL monitoring, poor consumer knowledge and healthier alternatives). Finally, healthier environments to support effective obesity prevention were emphasised, with additional FOPL education, research, and regulation updates necessary to support sustainability.

Perceptions among stakeholders centred on prioritising future FOPL evaluation and education and on ensuring adequate resources are allocated to ensure that FOPL is properly implemented within supportive environments.

artigos.titulo: From compartments to dynamic physiology: toward actionable body composition
artigos.autores: Friedl KE, Potter AW, Miles-Chan JL et al.
artigos.destaque: Future body composition assessment practices must include demonstrated added value over previous methods, and the greatest advances will come from technologies that bring physiologically meaningful assessment to large populations. The success of future technologies should be judged less by how precisely they estimate tissue compartments than by how effectively they improve physiological understanding, prediction, and decision-making.

resumo.texto: The 12th International Symposium on In Vivo Body Composition Studies (ISBCR 2025) highlighted a fundamental transition from estimating static tissue compartments to dynamic physiological phenotyping, actionable interpretation, and demonstrable value for clinical decision-making, health prediction, and human performance assessment. This represents an evolution in technological capability and conceptual framing, as an extension of the Functional Body Composition concept. Classical multicompartment models and established methods such as dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, isotope dilution, bioimpedance, computed tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging remain foundational; however, emerging approaches increasingly integrate advanced imaging, artificial intelligence, bioimpedance spectroscopy, stable isotope methods, wearable sensing, and multidimensional phenotyping. Several themes were prominent at ISBCR 2025, including expansion of imaging beyond traditional DXA paradigms, increasing emphasis on muscle quality and fluid compartments, greater attention to visceral and ectopic adipose tissue, clinical applications in oncology and critical illness, the evaluation of obesity pharmacotherapy, the importance of generalizability to individuals across sex and ethnicity, and data governance. This perspective proposes a framework for future research in which body composition measurements become integral components of predictive models of health, performance, and physiological resilience. Future body composition assessment practices must include demonstrated added value over previous methods, and the greatest advances will come from technologies that bring physiologically meaningful assessment to large populations. The success of future technologies should be judged less by how precisely they estimate tissue compartments than by how effectively they improve physiological understanding, prediction, and decision-making.

artigos.titulo: Polyphenol supplementation and skeletal muscle health in older adults: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials
artigos.autores: Diaz-Vallejo JA, Gonzalez-Correa CH, Padilla CJ
artigos.destaque: Polyphenol supplementation shows biologically plausible but currently inconsistent effects on skeletal muscle outcomes in older adults; the evidence base remains too small, heterogeneous, and methodologically limited to support therapeutic recommendations. Larger, standardized randomized trials in populations with confirmed sarcopenia, incorporating direct neuromuscular assessment, are required before clinical translation.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia is a progressive age-related skeletal muscle disorder characterized by the decline of muscle mass and function, driven by mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and chronic low-grade inflammation. Polyphenols have been proposed as candidate modulators of these pathways on mechanistic and preclinical grounds, but whether this plausibility translates into measurable structural and functional benefit in clinical trials remains unresolved. A systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and the Cochrane Handbook (PROSPERO CRD420251183284) was conducted. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials evaluating polyphenol supplementation in adults aged ≥ 55 years for outcomes related to skeletal muscle mass, strength, or physical function. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and because a formal meta-analysis was not feasible given the small number of trials and substantial clinical heterogeneity, effect estimates and measures of uncertainty were tabulated alongside a structured direction-of-effect synthesis, following recommended practice for reviews that cannot pool data quantitatively. Six randomized controlled trials were identified; five had reported outcome data and were included in the synthesis, while a sixth remains an ongoing registered protocol with no results yet available and is reported separately. Interventions included quercetin, epicatechin-rich extracts, tea catechins, cocoa flavonoids, and marine-derived polyphenols, with durations ranging from 4 to 24 weeks among completed trials. Muscle strength improved significantly on between-group comparison in two of five completed trials; effects on muscle mass were inconsistent, with one trial showing a significant group-by-time interaction under a combined polyphenol, amino-acid, and exercise intervention, another showing an attenuated loss without a significant between-group difference, and others showing null or less clearly attributable effects; functional and balance outcomes improved in two of three trials that assessed them. Polyphenol supplementation shows biologically plausible but currently inconsistent effects on skeletal muscle outcomes in older adults; the evidence base remains too small, heterogeneous, and methodologically limited to support therapeutic recommendations. Larger, standardized randomized trials in populations with confirmed sarcopenia, incorporating direct neuromuscular assessment, are required before clinical translation.

artigos.titulo: Muscle atrophy and functional impairments in patients admitted to the high care unit: a single-center observational study in Japan
artigos.autores: Nakaguchi A, Kawamura A, Shino A et al.
artigos.destaque: Muscle atrophy in HCU patients was associated with illness severity, whereas ADL decline occurred irrespective of muscle atrophy.

resumo.texto: Muscle atrophy and functional decline are well recognized in critically ill patients in the intensive care unit. However, little is known about these changes in elderly patients admitted to high care units (HCUs), who are generally less severely ill.

We conducted a prospective observational study in an HCU. Muscle mass was assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis, and physical function was evaluated using the modified Barthel Index at baseline, 1 week, and 2 weeks after admission. Changes were analyzed using a mixed-effects model for repeated measures. Subgroup analyses were performed according to illness severity based on the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score.

Fifty and thirty-five patients were included in the 1- and 2-week analyses, respectively. The mean age was 81±8 years, and 27 patients (49%) were male. The median SOFA score was 2 (interquartile range, 1-4). The skeletal muscle index changed by -2.9% (95% CI, -7.3% to 1.4%) at 1 week and by -4.3% (95% CI, -9.3% to 0.6%) at 2 weeks (P=0.18). In contrast, the modified Barthel Index declined by -28.3% (95% CI, -38.9% to -17.7%) at 1 week and by -34.0% (95% CI, -46.0% to -22.0%) at 2 weeks (P<0.01). In subgroup analysis, significant muscle atrophy was observed only in patients with SOFA score ≥4 (P=0.04). Activities of daily living (ADL) declined regardless of muscle atrophy or illness severity.
Muscle atrophy in HCU patients was associated with illness severity, whereas ADL decline occurred irrespective of muscle atrophy.

artigos.titulo: Association of CT-Based Sarcopenia, Clinical Frailty, and Nutritional Status With Mortality After Aortic Valve Replacement for Severe Aortic Stenosis
artigos.autores: Park JH, Zhang HS, Lee S et al.
artigos.destaque: Among patients with severe AS undergoing AVR, higher CFS scores and CT-based sarcopenia were independently associated with survival after adjustment for the STS score. The prognostic association of the CONUT score differed according to sarcopenia status. These findings support the incorporation of functional and structural vulnerabilities into risk assessment for patients undergoing AVR for AS; however, the role of nutritional status requires further investigation.

resumo.texto: This study investigated the association between multiple frailty-related markers-Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score, and computed tomography (CT)-based sarcopenia-and overall survival after aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS), with particular emphasis on the first year after AVR.

A total of 407 patients with severe AS who underwent surgical or transcatheter AVR at a tertiary center between November 2020 and December 2022 were retrospectively included. Three frailty-related markers were analyzed: CFS score for functional frailty, CONUT score for nutritional status, and CT-defined sarcopenia for structural muscle depletion. The CONUT score was calculated using serum markers, and sarcopenia was defined according to cohort-specific tertiles of the paravertebral muscle index quantified at the 12th thoracic vertebra (T12) vertebral level using CT. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed to assess the prognostic associations of the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score and the three frailty-related markers with all-cause mortality after AVR.

Within 1 year after AVR, 32 patients (7.9%) died. In the overall multivariable analysis, higher CFS scores and CT-defined sarcopenia were independently associated with mortality, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.82 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.40-2.38; P < 0.001) and 2.63 (95% CI, 1.22-5.67; P = 0.014), respectively. The STS score and CONUT scores were not associated with survival, with HRs of 1.00 (95% CI, 0.95-1.06; P = 0.883) and 1.05 (95% CI, 0.90-1.22; P = 0.563), respectively. A significant interaction was observed between the CONUT score and sarcopenia.

Among patients with severe AS undergoing AVR, higher CFS scores and CT-based sarcopenia were independently associated with survival after adjustment for the STS score. The prognostic association of the CONUT score differed according to sarcopenia status. These findings support the incorporation of functional and structural vulnerabilities into risk assessment for patients undergoing AVR for AS; however, the role of nutritional status requires further investigation.

artigos.titulo: Association between serum cotinine and muscle mass: The mediating role of systemic inflammation in NHANES 2013-2018
artigos.autores: Zheng Q, Chen J, Zheng H et al.
artigos.destaque: Elevated cotinine levels are significantly associated with decreased muscle mass, and this association is partially mediated by systemic inflammation.

resumo.texto: Smoking is a modifiable risk factor for muscle loss, but the underlying mechanisms are not fully understood. This study investigated the association between serum cotinine and appendicular skeletal muscle mass index (ASMI) and the mediating role of the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI).

Data from NHANES 2013-2018 were used for secondary analysis. A total of 4174 adults with complete records of cotinine and data for calculating ASMI and SIRI were included. Weighted multiple linear regression assessed associations of cotinine with ASMI and SIRI, and univariate analysis was performed to screen relevant variables. Mediation analysis with SIRI as the mediator subsequently quantified the indirect effect. All analyses were performed after adjustment for potential confounders.

In females, ASMI was significantly lower in the high‑cotinine group than in the low‑cotinine group; no significant difference was observed between the two groups in males. Univariate analysis demonstrated significant negative correlations of cotinine and SIRI with ASMI. Across all weighted regression models, cotinine was negatively associated with ASMI (fully adjusted, β= ‑0.000; 95% CI: ‑0.000 - ‑0.000) and positively associated with SIRI (fully adjusted, β=0.001; 95% CI: 0.001-0.001). In the fully adjusted model, SIRI was negatively associated with ASMI (β= ‑0.003; 95% CI: ‑0.005 - ‑0.001). Mediation analysis showed that SIRI partially mediated the cotinine‑ASMI relationship, with a proportion mediated of 14.170%.
Elevated cotinine levels are significantly associated with decreased muscle mass, and this association is partially mediated by systemic inflammation.

artigos.titulo: Late Gastric Remnant Necrosis Associated with Paraesophageal Hernia After Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass
artigos.autores: Flores Huidobro Martinez A, Connors K, Weltz A et al.
artigos.destaque: Recent tirzepatide use may have contributed to impaired remnant emptying and progressive distention, although causality cannot be established. This case highlights the importance of considering remnant pathology in postbypass patients with acute abdominal pain and demonstrates the utility of minimally invasive exploration with fluorescence-guided perfusion assessment.

resumo.texto: Gastric remnant ischemia is a rare but life-threatening complication after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. We report a 65-year-old man who presented nearly 20 years after bypass with acute left upper quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated marked distention of the excluded gastric remnant with pneumatosis, without evidence of small bowel obstruction, biliopancreatic limb obstruction, or mesenteric vascular occlusion. Diagnostic laparoscopy revealed a severely distended and ischemic gastric remnant, and indocyanine green angiography confirmed absent perfusion. The patient underwent laparoscopic resection of the ischemic remnant and repair of an associated paraesophageal hernia containing the gastric pouch. He recovered without complications. Recent tirzepatide use may have contributed to impaired remnant emptying and progressive distention, although causality cannot be established. This case highlights the importance of considering remnant pathology in postbypass patients with acute abdominal pain and demonstrates the utility of minimally invasive exploration with fluorescence-guided perfusion assessment.

artigos.titulo: Antidiabetic Therapy and Atrial Fibrillation: Pathophysiological Links, Therapeutic Implications, and Evidence-Based Outcomes
artigos.autores: Zisis M, Cheiletzaris T, Pieper OF et al.
artigos.destaque: Incorporating atrial fibrillation risk into the individualization of antidiabetic therapy is a promising and clinically relevant strategy. However, establishing any specific agent as a preferred option for AF management remains premature in the absence of dedicated trials with primary AF endpoints.

resumo.texto: Diabetes Mellitus (DM) is strongly associated with an increased risk, severity, and recurrence of Atrial Fibrillation (AF). This narrative review aims to synthesize the mechanistic links between DM and AF and evaluate the impact of major antidiabetic drug categories on AF incidence, burden, and post-ablation outcomes.
A focused narrative review of the literature was conducted using predefined eligibility criteria for study selection and specific keywords to search major scientific databases and grey literature.

Hyperglycemia, oxidative stress, epicardial adipose tissue expansion, autonomic imbalance, and atrial remodeling represent core pathophysiological mechanisms connecting DM and AF. Among antidiabetic pharmacotherapies, the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist semaglutide displays a potential to reduce AF incidence. Sodium-glucose transporter 2 inhibitors have similarly been shown to lower the incidence of AF in most of the available evidence, while offering an emerging, preliminary benefit for post-ablation success. Metformin also demonstrates a positive impact across both primary and secondary AF prevention, albeit with less robust evidence. Other incretin therapies, including tirzepatide, exhibit neutral effects, while thiazolidinediones and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors yield conflicting results. Data from insulin and sulfonylureas suggest an unfavorable risk profile, though potentially confounded by indication.

Antidiabetic therapy selection may have clinically meaningful implications for AF risk modification and rhythm-control outcomes. Weight-centric and cardio-protective strategies, particularly SGLT2 inhibitors and semaglutide, alongside the traditional option of metformin, show promising signals. Nevertheless, available data derive largely from unadjudicated adverseevent reporting and observational cohorts, currently precluding definitive class-wide or agentspecific recommendations.

Incorporating atrial fibrillation risk into the individualization of antidiabetic therapy is a promising and clinically relevant strategy. However, establishing any specific agent as a preferred option for AF management remains premature in the absence of dedicated trials with primary AF endpoints.

artigos.titulo: The effect of a seven-week online mindfulness intervention on the relationship between menstrual symptoms and mental health - A non-randomized controlled trial
artigos.autores: Kullik L, Birnkraut T, Kellmann M et al.
artigos.destaque: The results indicate that menstrual symptom frequency is associated with mental health outcomes in physically active students. Participation in the MBI was associated with changes in anxiety over time. However, the non-significant three-way interaction provided no conclusive evidence of moderation. These preliminary findings suggest potential benefits of MBI for anxiety in menstrual health context. Future studies should investigate programs that explicitly address menstrual-related aspects.

resumo.texto: Menstrual symptoms are common among physically active women and may affect their well-being and performance. Moreover, symptom frequency has been associated with mental health in previous studies. Although mindfulness-based interventions (MBI) have shown beneficial effects on psychological and physiological health outcomes, their potential role in the relationship between menstrual and mental health remains unclear. Therefore, this study examined whether participation in an MBI was associated with changes in this relationship.

39 physically active students were split into an experimental group (EG; n = 14; 22.68 ± 2.23 years) and a control group (CG; n = 25; 22.76 ± 4.88 years), which conducted a baseline and post-intervention measurement, including a psychometric screening. The CG received no intervention during the study and was offered access to the intervention materials afterwards. Assessed constructs included the 21-item version of the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale and the Menstrual Symptom index (MSi). The MBI was developed based on mindfulness-based stress reduction, incorporating the dimensions of acting with awareness, non-judgmental acceptance, and present-moment attention.

At baseline in the control group, MSi scores were positively associated with anxiety (B = 0.16; p = .004) and depression (B = 0.14; p = .012). No significant group × time interactions were observed for depression or stress. For anxiety, the group × time interaction was significant at the grand-mean MSi score (B = - 3.30; 95% CI [- 6.50, - 0.11]; p = .043), whereas the three-way interaction was not significant (p = .054).

The results indicate that menstrual symptom frequency is associated with mental health outcomes in physically active students. Participation in the MBI was associated with changes in anxiety over time. However, the non-significant three-way interaction provided no conclusive evidence of moderation. These preliminary findings suggest potential benefits of MBI for anxiety in menstrual health context. Future studies should investigate programs that explicitly address menstrual-related aspects.

This study was registered as 'Impact of an online mindfulness intervention on sleep quality in physically active students' in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS) under the identifier DRKS00038462 on 13 November 2025. Retrospectively registered.

artigos.titulo: Working memory gating across sensory modalities reveals modality-specific maintenance mechanisms
artigos.autores: Limburg R, Beste C, Prochnow A
artigos.destaque: However, the functional localization and relative magnitude of these oscillatory modulations varied between tasks. Together, our findings suggest that working memory gating is not amodal, but that maintenance processes in particular are shaped by the sensory context.

resumo.texto: The flexible resolution of the conflict between updating and maintenance demands in working memory is thought to rely on a selective gating mechanism. While gating of visual information has been extensively studied, gating of multisensory information remains poorly understood. We addressed this gap by contrasting task performance and accompanying neuro-oscillatory modulations across a purely visual and two audiovisual variants of a working memory gating task. Task-dependent performance differences emerged specifically for gate closing. Across tasks, gate closing was consistently associated with alpha band activity modulations supporting the integration of task-relevant information and beta band activity modulations controlling the reconfiguration of the gate state, while theta band activity modulations were overall negligible. However, the functional localization and relative magnitude of these oscillatory modulations varied between tasks. Together, our findings suggest that working memory gating is not amodal, but that maintenance processes in particular are shaped by the sensory context.

artigos.titulo: Rethinking endpoints for anti-obesity pharmacotherapy in patients with HR+ early breast cancer receiving endocrine therapy: from body weight and BMI to body composition
artigos.autores: Lampropoulou DI, Dedes V, Pliakou E et al.
artigos.destaque: Body composition should be considered as a complementary endpoint, alongside metabolic, functional and oncologic outcomes. Future studies should also assess endocrine therapy adherence and persistence to better characterize the benefits and risks of anti-obesity pharmacotherapy in patients with HR+ eBC.

resumo.texto: Body weight (BW) and body mass index (BMI) are commonly used to assess obesity and response to weight-management interventions in patients with hormone receptor-positive (HR+) early breast cancer (eBC) receiving endocrine therapy. However, these measures do not adequately reflect changes in fat mass, visceral adiposity, lean mass and sarcopenia-related phenotypes.

This focused narrative review examines whether BW and BMI are sufficient endpoints for evaluating obesity management and anti-obesity pharmacotherapy in patients with HR+ eBC receiving endocrine therapy. PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for relevant evidence until 23 June 2026, including BC-specific studies of obesity pharmacotherapy and registered interventional trials. Studies have reported increases in total and visceral fat mass after adjuvant BC treatment, while changes in lean mass have been less consistent. The identified BC-specific studies remain mainly retrospective and weight-centric, with none assessing body composition as a key outcome.

BW and BMI may be useful entry and monitoring variables, but insufficient as stand-alone endpoints. Body composition should be considered as a complementary endpoint, alongside metabolic, functional and oncologic outcomes. Future studies should also assess endocrine therapy adherence and persistence to better characterize the benefits and risks of anti-obesity pharmacotherapy in patients with HR+ eBC.

artigos.titulo: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
artigos.autores: Börchers S, Mazzini G, Zetterberg H et al.
artigos.destaque: This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer's disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

resumo.texto: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer's disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

artigos.titulo: Obesity management medications: The way forward
artigos.autores: Blüher M
artigos.destaque: Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

resumo.texto: Obesity is now widely recognized as a chronic progressive condition. The altered biological mechanisms that cause obesity frequently require long-term treatment, including pharmacotherapies or bariatric surgery. In recent decades, the pathophysiology of obesity has been understood to an extent that obesity management medication (OMM) discovery could be rationally pursued. Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

artigos.titulo: Plant-Forward Dietary Patterns and Cardiometabolic Risk Among US Adults: Findings From the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 2009-2023
artigos.autores: Lov D
artigos.destaque: Greater adherence to plant-forward dietary patterns was associated with lower BMI and reduced odds of obesity and diabetes among US adults.

resumo.texto: The objective of this study was to describe the relationship between plant-forward dietary patterns and metabolic profiles.

A repeated cross-sectional analysis of adults aged 18 years or older was conducted using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), 2009-2023. Plant-forward dietary adherence was estimated from the mean of two 24-hour dietary recalls and categorized into tertiles. Survey-weighted multivariable regression examined associations with body mass index (BMI), obesity, prediabetes, and diabetes, adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, dietary, and behavioral factors.

Among 33,532 NHANES participants, greater plant-forward dietary adherence was associated with lower BMI (β = -1.45; 95% CI, -1.82 to -1.09), lower odds of obesity (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.62-0.79) and diabetes (AOR = 0.72; 95% CI, 0.62-0.84) but not prediabetes (AOR = 0.92; 95% CI, 0.82-1.04).
Greater adherence to plant-forward dietary patterns was associated with lower BMI and reduced odds of obesity and diabetes among US adults.

artigos.titulo: Completeness of care provision and inequalities in care for people with hypertension, diabetes, and obesity: an analysis of the Brazilian National Basic Health Units Census
artigos.autores: Facchini LA, Tomasi E, Thumé E et al.
artigos.destaque: After adjusting for contextual and BHU characteristics, the family health was associated with 70% higher completeness of care provision. Although access to consultations is well established, weaknesses persist in comprehensiveness and care coordination for chronic diseases, highlighting the need for structural policies that strengthen the capacity of PHC to effectively address health needs.

resumo.texto: This study aimed to identify patterns and inequalities in the completeness of care provision for people with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and obesity in Brazilian primary health care (PHC), drawing on the 2024 Brazilian National Basic Health Units Census (BHU Census). This was a cross-sectional online survey covering 44,938 BHUs registered in the Brazilian National Registry of Health Establishments and validated by municipal health managers. Variables related to geographic region, municipal characteristics, and health service characteristics were analyzed. Care provision was considered complete when the response was positive for all 14 actions related to hypertension, 15 for diabetes, and 10 for obesity. A low proportion of BHUs demonstrated complete provision of care for people with hypertension (15.3%), diabetes (15.6%), and obesity (13.4%), across all regions and municipality profiles. Completeness was higher in the Southeast and Northeast and lower in the South. Large municipalities, municipalities with high or very high social vulnerability, and municipalities with 100% family health coverage also showed higher completeness levels. After adjusting for contextual and BHU characteristics, the family health was associated with 70% higher completeness of care provision. Although access to consultations is well established, weaknesses persist in comprehensiveness and care coordination for chronic diseases, highlighting the need for structural policies that strengthen the capacity of PHC to effectively address health needs.

artigos.titulo: NUTRITIONAL OUTCOMES AFTER ONE ANASTOMOSIS GASTRIC BYPASS VERSUS ROUX-EN-Y GASTRIC BYPASS: A ONE-YEAR COMPARATIVE STUDY
artigos.autores: Sampaio P, Pajecki D, Santo Filho MA et al.
artigos.destaque: Under structured multidisciplinary follow-up, OAGB and RYGB demonstrated comparable nutritional outcomes. OAGB appears to be a nutritionally safe alternative at one year of follow-up, with the need for ongoing monitoring of iron and vitamin D status.

resumo.texto: Metabolic and bariatric surgery is an effective obesity treatment. One anastomosis gastric bypass (OAGB) has emerged as an alternative to Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB); however, evidence regarding its postoperative nutritional outcomes remains limited. Objective: To compare food tolerance, gastrointestinal symptoms, and nutritional status between OAGB and RYGB one year after surgery.

This retrospective, observational, comparative study included 46 patients (16 OAGB and 30 RYGB). Weight loss, laboratory parameters, dietary intake, food tolerance, and gastrointestinal symptoms were evaluated one year postoperatively. Linear regression models were adjusted for relevant confounding variables, including age, sex, and baseline values when appropriate.

The percentage of total weight loss (29.55% vs 26.32%) and excess weight loss (63.36% vs 58.29%) were similar between RYGB and OAGB groups (P>0.05). A high prevalence of vitamin D deficiency was observed in both groups (RYGB: 82% vs. OAGB: 92%). Elevated parathyroid hormone levels were more frequent in the OAGB group (75% vs 50%), although the difference was not statistically significant. OAGB patients showed numerically lower serum iron and reduced transferrin saturation; however, none of the patients developed anemia. Mean protein intake met the recommended levels in both groups, whereas fiber intake was below the minimum recommended level. OAGB patients presented significantly lower gastrointestinal symptom scores for diarrhea, indigestion, and total score (P<0.05). Food tolerance was satisfactory and similar between groups.

Under structured multidisciplinary follow-up, OAGB and RYGB demonstrated comparable nutritional outcomes. OAGB appears to be a nutritionally safe alternative at one year of follow-up, with the need for ongoing monitoring of iron and vitamin D status.

artigos.titulo: Cutoff values of muscle-specific strength using arm circumference: Results from NHANES 2011-2014
artigos.autores: Costa-Pereira JP, Prado CM, Bennet JP et al.
artigos.destaque: Our study provides practical, sex-specific reference cutoff values for MUAC-based muscle-specific strength (HGS/MUAC) derived from a population-based sample. This accessible anthropometric metric showed strong correlations with DXA-based muscle-specific strength and small average standardized differences, supporting its potential as a pragmatic surrogate when regional body composition assessment is unavailable. Further validation is needed before its clinical or diagnostic application.

resumo.texto: Muscle-specific strength, the ratio of muscle strength to muscle mass, reflects functional capacity and has been incorporated into contemporary conceptual definitions of sarcopenia, although its operational diagnostic role remains undefined. Ideally, muscle-specific strength relates muscle strength to the mass of the muscles that generate it; however, such measures are rarely available in clinical practice. Mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) may serve as a practical regional surrogate for muscle mass.

To examine the relationship between conventional muscle-specific strength from dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and a MUAC-based muscle-specific strength, and to propose sex-specific cutoff values for the latter.

This cross-sectional study used NHANES 2011-2014 data from adults aged 20-59 years with MUAC, right-hand HGS, and right-arm DXA measurements. Adults aged 20-39 years with normal-range body mass index (BMI, 18.5-24.9 kg/m2) served as the reference subsample. Survey-weighted Pearson correlations and linear regression models were used to examine relationships between MUAC- and DXA-based muscle-specific strength. Cutoff values were derived at 1 and 2 standard deviations (SD) below the survey-weighted sex-specific reference mean. Bland-Altman analyses assessed agreement between the two metrics after transformation to sex-specific standardized scores.

A total of 4,518 participants were included (survey-weighted proportion: 52.7% males). MUAC was strongly correlated with DXA-derived arm lean soft tissue in males (r = 0.80) and females (r = 0.74). MUAC-based muscle-specific strength was also strongly correlated with DXA-based muscle-specific strength in males (r = 0.79) and females (r = 0.72). Associations between the two metrics remained significant after adjustment for age, race and ethnicity, and BMI. Rounded cutoff values for MUAC-based muscle-specific strength were <1.3 kg/cm for low and <1.0 kg/cm for very low values in males. In females, the corresponding cutoff values were <0.9 kg/cm for low and <0.8 kg/cm for very low muscle-specific strength. Exploratory Bland-Altman analyses showed small mean differences between the standardized metrics (0.14 SD in males and -0.02 SD in females), although the 95% limits of agreement indicated individual variability (-1.12 to 1.40 SD in males and -1.79 to 1.74 SD in females).

Our study provides practical, sex-specific reference cutoff values for MUAC-based muscle-specific strength (HGS/MUAC) derived from a population-based sample. This accessible anthropometric metric showed strong correlations with DXA-based muscle-specific strength and small average standardized differences, supporting its potential as a pragmatic surrogate when regional body composition assessment is unavailable. Further validation is needed before its clinical or diagnostic application.

artigos.titulo: Dietary 1,5-anhydro-D-fructose attenuates sarcopenia-related phenotypes: Insights from C. elegans and aged mouse models
artigos.autores: Komiya Y, Sakashita R, Sugiyama M et al.
artigos.destaque: Collectively, these findings demonstrate associations between dietary 1,5-AF supplementation and selected age-related functional and tissue phenotypes in C. elegans and mice. These results highlight the potential of 1,5-AF as a dietary component to support muscle health and promoting healthy aging.

resumo.texto: Sarcopenia, the age-related loss of skeletal muscle mass and function, represents a major health challenge. Although 1,5-anhydro-D-fructose (1,5-AF) has been investigated in relation to gut microbiota, oxidative stress, and metabolic disorders, its impact on aging remains unclear. Here, we evaluated the potential of 1,5-AF as a nutrition-based intervention using cross-species aging models. In Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans), 1,5-AF enhanced late-life locomotor activity and upregulated transcripts encoding myofibrillar proteins. In aged mice, 1,5-AF administration improved forelimb grip strength, reduced rimmed vacuole-containing muscle fibers. In addition, 1,5-AF promoted a shift toward a more oxidative muscle fiber phenotype and increased expression of mitochondrial-related proteins. Beyond skeletal muscle, 1,5-AF attenuated hepatic lipid accumulation and fibrosis, while showing a trend toward reduced macrophage accumulation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate associations between dietary 1,5-AF supplementation and selected age-related functional and tissue phenotypes in C. elegans and mice. These results highlight the potential of 1,5-AF as a dietary component to support muscle health and promoting healthy aging.

artigos.titulo: Incretin-Based Therapies and Pulmonary Fibrosis: Preclinical Evidence, Body Composition, and Translational Perspectives: A Narrative Review
artigos.autores: Pianigiani T, Postiferi S, Simoncini F et al.
artigos.destaque: This narrative review integrates current preclinical evidence on the potential antifibrotic effects of incretin-related pathways with clinical evidence on body weight, adiposity, and skeletal muscle in pulmonary fibrosis. Future clinical and translational studies are required to determine whether the potential pulmonary and metabolic effects of incretin-based therapies translate into meaningful clinical benefits in fibrotic interstitial lung disease.

resumo.texto: Pulmonary fibrosis comprises a heterogeneous group of interstitial lung diseases characterized by progressive extracellular matrix deposition and structural remodeling. Although currently available antifibrotic therapies can slow disease progression, additional biological pathways remain under investigation. Incretin-based therapies, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors, have attracted increasing interest because their biological effects extend beyond glucose regulation and may involve pathways relevant to pulmonary fibrogenesis. Preclinical studies suggest that incretin-related pathways may modulate transforming growth factor-β signaling, fibroblast activation, extracellular matrix deposition, mesenchymal transition, inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic mechanisms involved in fibrosis. However, these findings remain predominantly experimental, and evidence of antifibrotic efficacy in patients with fibrotic interstitial lung disease is currently lacking. A complementary aspect is represented by the profound effects of incretin-based therapies on body weight and composition. This is particularly relevant in pulmonary fibrosis, where excess adiposity may contribute to metabolic and functional burden, whereas low body mass index, unintentional weight loss, and skeletal muscle depletion are associated with adverse outcomes. Incretin-induced weight loss predominantly reflects reduction in adipose tissue, but is accompanied by variable reductions in lean or fat-free mass, whose implications for skeletal muscle and functional reserve remain incompletely defined. This narrative review integrates current preclinical evidence on the potential antifibrotic effects of incretin-related pathways with clinical evidence on body weight, adiposity, and skeletal muscle in pulmonary fibrosis. Future clinical and translational studies are required to determine whether the potential pulmonary and metabolic effects of incretin-based therapies translate into meaningful clinical benefits in fibrotic interstitial lung disease.

artigos.titulo: Experiences of compassion fatigue among health and social care practitioners supporting children and young people who self-harm
artigos.revista: Int J Qual Stud Health Well-being
artigos.autores: Fox C, Lee L
artigos.destaque: Clinical implications include the need for health and social care organisations to prioritise targeted workforce wellbeing interventions to better support practitioners and improve care for CYP who self-harm.

resumo.texto: Health and social care (HSC) practitioners are at an increased risk of developing compassion fatigue, particularly when working with vulnerable children and young people (CYP) who self-harm. This can negatively impact both practitioner wellbeing and the quality of patient care. Despite this, no research has explored experiences of compassion fatigue among HSC practitioners supporting CYP who self-harm. This study aimed to explore HSC practitioners' experiences of compassion fatigue when working with this population.
Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 12 HSC practitioners supporting CYP who self-harm who identified as having experienced compassion fatigue.

Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis (RTA) and three key themes were generated: 'compassion fatigue as an emotional balancing act', 'compassion fatigue as a mismatch between responsibility and influence', and 'professional evolution through compassion fatigue'. The findings highlight the complex interplay of relational, emotional and systemic factors influencing HSC practitioners' experiences of compassion fatigue when supporting CYP who self-harm.

Clinical implications include the need for health and social care organisations to prioritise targeted workforce wellbeing interventions to better support practitioners and improve care for CYP who self-harm.

artigos.titulo: Sleep disturbance and enhanced aggression after chronic mild stress in mice: Association with hypothalamic nerve growth factor
artigos.autores: Chikahisa S, Shiuchi T, Chiba S et al.
artigos.destaque: Intracerebroventricular administration of NGF promoted sleep in control and CMS mice (n = 6-7 per group), but aggressive behaviour was suppressed only in CMS mice (n = 8 per group). These findings suggest that hypothalamic NGF may contribute to mechanisms that link chronic stress-related sleep disturbances with aggressive behaviour, although the precise downstream mechanisms are not known.

resumo.texto: Chronic stress disrupts sleep and induces behavioural abnormalities. However, the mechanisms linking stress-related sleep disturbances to abnormal social behaviour are unclear. In this study, a predictable chronic mild stress (CMS) paradigm was used, in which male mice were housed on a wire mesh for 3 weeks. CMS mice (n = 7 per group) had reduced non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep and NREM slow-wave activity, and they had enhanced aggressive behaviour, whereas anxiety- and depression-related behavioural measures were not markedly altered. At the molecular level, CMS was associated with lower hypothalamic Ngf mRNA levels, and hypothalamic NGF protein levels were related to aggressive behaviour. Intracerebroventricular administration of NGF promoted sleep in control and CMS mice (n = 6-7 per group), but aggressive behaviour was suppressed only in CMS mice (n = 8 per group). These findings suggest that hypothalamic NGF may contribute to mechanisms that link chronic stress-related sleep disturbances with aggressive behaviour, although the precise downstream mechanisms are not known.

artigos.titulo: Association of LATE-NC With Neuropathologic Lesions and Cognitive Abilities: A Population-Based Autopsy Study
artigos.autores: Matos Silva C, Justo AFO, Ribeiro Paes V et al.
artigos.destaque: LATE-NC was prevalent and associated with cognitive impairment in this ethnoracially and socioeconomically diverse sample. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and some estimates had wide confidence intervals due to the small number of advanced-stage cases.

resumo.texto: Limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy neuropathologic change (LATE-NC) is a common finding in aging brains. However, most previous studies were limited to ethnoracially homogeneous cohorts from high-income countries. The objective of this study was to investigate the associations between LATE-NC, cognitive performance, and coexisting neuropathologic lesions in a large, ethnoracially and socioeconomically diverse sample from Brazil.

This cross-sectional study analyzed data from the Biobank for Aging Studies, a Brazilian population-based autopsy study based at the University of São Paulo. The study included a consecutive series of autopsies performed between 2004 and 2024. Inclusion criteria required participants to be at least 18 years old with a knowledgeable informant. LATE-NC, Alzheimer disease neuropathologic change (ADNC), Lewy body pathology (LBP), lacunar infarcts, small vessel disease, cerebral amyloid angiopathy, and hippocampal sclerosis were assessed following international criteria. Cognitive abilities were evaluated with the Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes (CDR-SOB). Logistic and linear regression models were applied to examine associations of LATE-NC with comorbid neuropathologies and cognitive outcomes, with adjustments for sociodemographic, clinical, and neuropathologic covariates.

The sample comprised 1,860 participants (mean age = 72.6 ± 14.2 years; 49.1% female; 62.2% White; 35.4% Black). LATE-NC was present in 7.4% of participants (stage 1: 3.0%; stage 2: 4.0%; stage 3: 0.4%). After adjustment for sociodemographic, clinical, and other neuropathologic covariates, LATE-NC (stages 2-3) was associated with hippocampal sclerosis (OR = 14.95; 95% CI 7.42-30.27; p < 0.001), advanced Braak NFT stages (OR = 2.23; 95% CI 1.32-3.83; p = 0.003), and LBP (OR = 1.89; 95% CI 1.02-3.37; p = 0.036). Factoring in other pathologies, LATE-NC was associated with the CDR-SOB score (β = 4.06; 95% CI 2.95-5.18; p < 0.001), demonstrating a consistent association with cognition, similar to the one observed for moderate/severe ADNC (β = 3.78; 95% CI 3.14-4.42; p < 0.001) in the same sample.

LATE-NC was prevalent and associated with cognitive impairment in this ethnoracially and socioeconomically diverse sample. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and some estimates had wide confidence intervals due to the small number of advanced-stage cases.

artigos.titulo: Reinterpreting homographs in context
artigos.autores: Woerle TA, Dixon P
artigos.destaque: These ratings were compared to ratings obtained when an unambiguous synonym was substituted for the homograph. The results suggest that in many cases, readers can identify both possible interpretations of the homograph, even after an intervening sentence. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

resumo.texto: When readers encounter an ambiguous homograph, they are typically able to immediately select an appropriate meaning based on the preceding context. However, in cases where there is not enough context to select the correct meaning, it is unclear how readers process the ambiguous word. In the present study, we investigated how readers select meanings of homographs when the disambiguating information is delayed. Participants read two or three sentence passages in which a homograph appeared in the first sentence and the disambiguating information was in the last. After each passage, participants rated how much sense the passage made. These ratings were compared to ratings obtained when an unambiguous synonym was substituted for the homograph. The results suggest that in many cases, readers can identify both possible interpretations of the homograph, even after an intervening sentence. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

artigos.titulo: Mechanistic understanding of the role of the lung-brain axis in the pathogenesis of PM2.5-induced Alzheimer's disease
artigos.autores: Defrancesco AD, Wang B, Yi C et al.
artigos.destaque: We also discuss important modifiers of susceptibility and heterogeneity in reported associations, including pollutant composition, co-exposure to other air pollutants, sex, APOE genotype, and epigenetic reprogramming. Overall, the present review proposes an integrated multi-organ model of PM2.5 neurotoxicity that aligns environmental exposure with key mechanisms of AD pathogenesis and highlights priorities for strengthening causal inference and future translational research.

resumo.texto: Air pollution, particularly fine particulate matter (PM2.5), has emerged as an important yet under-recognised environmental contributor to cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease (AD) across the life course. Although epidemiological studies consistently associate long-term PM2.5 exposure with impaired cognition, from reduced neurodevelopmental performance in children to accelerated neurodegeneration in older adults, the biological mechanisms linking inhaled particles to AD-related brain pathology remain incompletely defined. In the present review, we synthesise current epidemiological and experimental evidence to position the lung-brain axis as a central mechanistic framework through which PM2.5 may influence brain aging and AD pathogenesis. Rather than acting solely through direct particle entry into the brain, PM2.5-induced pulmonary injury initiates systemic signalling cascades, including inflammatory mediators, oxidative stress, blood-brain barrier disruption, and extracellular vesicle-mediated intercellular communication, which together propagate disease signals from the lung to the brain. We further examine how these pathways intersect with core AD-related processes, including amyloid-β accumulation, tau pathology, impaired protein clearance, maladaptive microglial responses, and autophagy-lysosomal dysfunction. We also discuss important modifiers of susceptibility and heterogeneity in reported associations, including pollutant composition, co-exposure to other air pollutants, sex, APOE genotype, and epigenetic reprogramming. Overall, the present review proposes an integrated multi-organ model of PM2.5 neurotoxicity that aligns environmental exposure with key mechanisms of AD pathogenesis and highlights priorities for strengthening causal inference and future translational research.

artigos.titulo: An international women in radiology retreat: Design, impact, and a framework for leadership, community, and well-being
artigos.autores: Reichman M, Dodelzon K, Averill S et al.
artigos.destaque: An intentionally designed, community-centered retreat may provide a reproducible framework for fostering leadership, professional fulfillment, and physician well-being among women radiologists. Incorporating principles of connection, mentorship, reflection, and belonging into retreats may represent an important strategy for addressing burnout, strengthening retention, and supporting a more sustainable radiology workforce.

resumo.texto: Burnout among radiologists remains a global challenge and disproportionately affects women because of persistent inequities in leadership opportunities, mentorship, work-life integration, and professional advancement. While wellness initiatives have expanded, few interventions foster enduring professional relationships and community for women radiologists. This study describes the design and evaluation of an international retreat developed to promote leadership, collaboration, and physician well-being among women in radiology.

The American Association of Women in Radiology (AAWR) International Women in Radiology Retreat was designed to address challenges specific to women in radiology through a small-group, immersive experience emphasizing mentorship, reflective discussion, leadership development, and authentic connection rather than traditional didactic programming. Twenty-six women radiologists representing multiple countries and career stages participated. A post-retreat anonymous survey assessed participant experience through quantitative questions and qualitative free-text responses, analyzed using inductive thematic analysis.

Eighteen participants completed the survey (69% response rate). All respondents expressed interest in participating in future retreats. Qualitative analysis identified seven domains of impact: connection and community, shared experiences across cultures, professional growth, personal renewal, inspiration, networking and collaboration, and commitment to action. Participants also reported sustained engagement following the retreat through mentorship, communication, collaborative scholarship, and networking, suggesting benefits extending beyond the retreat.

An intentionally designed, community-centered retreat may provide a reproducible framework for fostering leadership, professional fulfillment, and physician well-being among women radiologists. Incorporating principles of connection, mentorship, reflection, and belonging into retreats may represent an important strategy for addressing burnout, strengthening retention, and supporting a more sustainable radiology workforce.

artigos.titulo: A surprising discovery could help aging muscles repair themselves
artigos.destaque: Scientists have discovered a compound that transforms a natural muscle-repair protein into a more powerful version dubbed "Super HGF," more than doubling its ability to bind to a key receptor while protecting it from age-related chemical damage. The breakthrough, supported by early mouse experiments, could eventually help combat muscle loss and preserve strength as people age.

artigos.titulo: Scientists may have finally explained why our brains and bodies are cross-wired
artigos.destaque: Scientists propose that the brain’s mysterious cross-wiring, which connects each hemisphere to the opposite side of the body, may have originated more than 500 million years ago in the visual systems of ancient fish. Rather than evolving for a specific advantage, this unusual arrangement may simply be a legacy of evolution building new brain circuits on an ancient foundation.

artigos.titulo: AI helps Stanford scientists discover a “natural Ozempic” with a surprising advantage
artigos.destaque: Stanford researchers have discovered an AI-identified natural molecule that dramatically suppresses appetite and promotes fat loss in animals, potentially offering an Ozempic-like weight-loss treatment without common digestive side effects or significant muscle loss. Called BRP, the molecule reduced food intake by up to 50% and targets a different brain pathway, raising hopes for a more precise obesity treatment if future human trials prove successful.

artigos.titulo: A randomized comparison of comprehensive weight loss intervention vs. usual care on recurrences of atrial fibrillation in obese patients after catheter ablation: HOBIT-AF trial
artigos.autores: Koščálová K, Novodvorský P, Jakubíková I et al.
artigos.destaque: HOBIT-AF trial showed that despite the beneficial effect of body weight reduction on metabolic profile of obese patients with predominantly paroxysmal AF after CA, no reduction in AF/AT recurrence was observed in comparison with control patients. This may be likely due to low AF burden after previous CA, limiting further improvement.

resumo.texto: Obesity is one of the strongest risk factors for the development of atrial fibrillation (AF), and its reduction is associated with the alleviation of AF burden. The HOBIT-AF study aimed to evaluate the impact of complex weight loss interventions on AF recurrence rate in obese individuals after catheter ablation (CA).

The HOBIT-AF was a randomized controlled trial with a 15-month treatment period (3-18 months post CA) involving complex weight-reducing interventions in the active arm. The primary outcome was the change in AF/atrial tachycardia (AT) burden assessed from baseline and the final 14-day Holter monitoring. A total of 167 individuals (aged 59 years, body mass index of 35.6 kg/m2) were randomized into the active (n = 85) and control group (n = 82). At the end of the treatment period, a mean reduction of 6.8 ± 7.0% of the initial body weight accompanied by improvement of metabolic parameters was achieved in the active group. The AF/AT burden change was 0.6 ± 2.5% (95% CI: -4.2-5.5%) in the active group and -0.9 ± 1.8% (95% CI: -4.5-3.0%) in the control group. The AF/AT recurrence-free survival during the 3-18-month follow-up period was comparable between groups (70.4% vs. 69.6%).

HOBIT-AF trial showed that despite the beneficial effect of body weight reduction on metabolic profile of obese patients with predominantly paroxysmal AF after CA, no reduction in AF/AT recurrence was observed in comparison with control patients. This may be likely due to low AF burden after previous CA, limiting further improvement.

artigos.titulo: Functional and body composition outcomes of pharmacological interventions for sarcopenia in older adults: A systematic review and pairwise meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
artigos.autores: Tsutsumi T, Hieda S, Gnanavelou M et al.
artigos.destaque: Functional and body-composition estimates varied across therapeutic Groups and Classes. The observed functional differences were small relative to commonly cited benchmarks, and Class-level evidence was sparse. Future trials should prioritize durable mobility, independence, and safety outcomes.

resumo.texto: Pharmacological trials in sarcopenia have reported changes in muscle mass or selected functional measures, but the consistency and clinical importance of these effects remain uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and pairwise meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in adults aged ≥65 years.
The original review search used MEDLINE and Embase from inception to 9 February 2026.

gov was checked immediately after completion of the systematic review. Interventions were analyzed within four broad therapeutic Groups and complementary pharmacological Classes. Random-effects pairwise meta-analyses used mean differences (MDs) for functional outcomes and Hedges' g standardized mean differences (SMDs) for body-composition outcomes.

Twenty-six RCTs including 3237 participants were included. At the Group level, Hormonal and anabolic therapies showed small pooled differences in grip strength (MD 1.003 kg, 95% CI 0.007 to 2.000) and 6-minute walk distance (MD 12.335 m, 95% CI 5.043 to 19.627). Myostatin inhibitors showed a gait-speed difference of 0.0300 m/s (95% CI 0.0295 to 0.0305) and a single-study estimate for appendicular lean body mass (SMD 0.573, 95% CI 0.291 to 0.855). The functional differences were below commonly cited meaningful-change benchmarks. Class-level evidence was sparse, with several Classes represented by one trial. Functional estimates for RAAS-based and Metabolic therapies were based on few trials and varied across outcomes.

Functional and body-composition estimates varied across therapeutic Groups and Classes. The observed functional differences were small relative to commonly cited benchmarks, and Class-level evidence was sparse. Future trials should prioritize durable mobility, independence, and safety outcomes.

artigos.titulo: Muscle ultrasound for nutrition assessment: Practical clinical protocols
artigos.autores: Bode A, Russell L, Hawes C et al.
artigos.destaque: Limited standardization of acquisition protocols and insufficient access to structured, hands-on operator training continue to hinder reproducibility across clinical settings. Further implementation studies are needed to ensure high-quality measurements are conducted and incorporated into nutritional assessment.

resumo.texto: Muscle ultrasound (mUS) is an emerging and increasingly utilized tool for assessing body composition. Bedside mUS can provide reliable measurements of skeletal muscle and adipose tissue that can strengthen nutrition assessment. As current malnutrition diagnostic frameworks emphasize the evaluation of lean body mass, mUS offers a practical, radiation-free, serial, and accessible method for quantifying muscle status in real time.
